CDA and D66 are willing to take a look at it.

lead: The cabinet plans to refrain from the planned cuts to social security. In doing so it is reaching out to left-wing parties. On the box 3 file, however, the cabinet wants to move to the 'right', sources confirm to NU.nl after reporting by De Telegraaf .

lead: A 38-year-old Dutchman has been sentenced by the German court to a prison sentence of two years and nine months, after he was caught with about 3 kilos of drugs in his car. The man stated that he was on his way to a wedding in the Austrian capital Vienna.

lead: A painting by Claude Monet raised 43 million euros at an auction on Thursday. This makes it the most expensive painting ever sold at auction in France.

title: Do we still have anything to say against the impending mass unemployment?
Five questions about box 3: how could it become such a problem and what is the solution now?
lead: The new coalition plan for the tax on wealth (box 3) will be the main topic during the General Financial Review, which takes place over the next two days. The question is whether this headache of a file, which has occupied politics for years, will finally come to an end. What is box 3 and how did it become such a problem? The most important questions at a glance. Box 3: what does it cover again? If you have little savings, no investments and no second home, you probably have nothing to do with box 3. In that case, like most Dutch people, you only pay tax in box 1 on your wages or benefits. This box brings the treasury by far the most: around 90 percent of all income tax. Box 2 is intended for people with a business, such as a private limited company. An estimated 500,000 people fall into this category. Box 3 contains around 2.5 million people. In it you pay tax on the return on savings, shares, cryptocurrencies and also a second home. Why does box 3 have to be overhauled? Politics had no choice after a ruling by the <entity id="org:hoge-raad">Hoge Raad</entity> in 2021. It judged that the estimated return used by the <entity id="org:belastingdienst">Belastingdienst</entity> was not fair. Savers in particular bore the brunt: they often paid more tax than they received in interest from the bank. To comply with the court ruling, <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>-Rutte III quickly introduced a temporary method of calculating tax, which still applies today. But this system also has a major drawback: people with high returns now pay relatively little tax. As a result, the treasury receives 3 billion euros less each year than before. Every year that no new plan comes, those billions 'leak' away. For this reason, political parties feel time pressure to come up with an alternative quickly. Work on this was done under the Rutte IV, Schoof and Jetten cabinets. Debate on Box 3 The <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">Tweede Kamer</entity> is debating today with <entity id="person:eelco-heinen">minister Heinen</entity> (<entity id="org:ministerie-van-financien">Financiën</entity>) about the budget and Box 3. The debate can be followed live via a livestream on NOS.nl and in the NOS app from 10.30 a.m. Which plan was being worked on? The difference between accrual tax on assets and tax on capital gains is important here: - With an accrual tax on assets, you must pay every year on the profit you make, even if that profit is still 'locked up' in, for example, shares. So if you have no savings, you may have to sell (part of) your shares or crypto to pay your tax. - With a tax on capital gains, you pay tax on the shares or cryptocurrencies you have sold. The disadvantage of this method is that owners can postpone sales to avoid tax. The coalition parties D66, VVD and CDA agree that a capital gains tax should be introduced in the long term. But there is a technical problem: according to the Ministry of Finance, this is only possible from 2030 or even 2032, because the Belastingdienst and banks must adjust their systems for it. Over the past years, politics has debated what should happen in the meantime. The Tweede Kamer (including D66, VVD and CDA) voted at the beginning of this year for a new, temporary solution to introduce an accrual tax on assets on shares and cryptocurrencies from 2028 and a capital gains tax on real estate. After that, work would be done towards a full capital gains tax. This interim solution caused so much unrest among businesses and investors that minister Heinen (Finance, VVD) said two weeks later that the law had to go back to the drawing board. A major difference of opinion then arose between coalition parties about what should be done instead. What were they disagreeing about? The VVD wants to move to a full capital gains tax as soon as possible, even though the Belastingdienst will then temporarily be less able to check tax returns because the systems have not yet been adjusted. The biggest problem is that the treasury would then receive an estimated 15 billion euros less in the coming years. This is because people only start paying tax when they sell their shares. The parties disagreed mainly about who should pay for this. D66 and CDA did not want lower incomes to contribute to this. What is the solution now? The cabinet now wants to switch to a capital gains tax for shares, bonds and second homes from 2028, with the rest following in 2030. The funding is being sought in box 2 and box 3. Of these, the proposal regarding the tax-free income in box 3 is the most politically sensitive. In the new box 3 there will be no more tax-free assets (which now amount to 59,357 euros for one person), but a tax-free income. The idea is that people with high returns also pay more tax. In the original plan, you pay tax on an annual return above 1,800 euros. In the new plan, this has been lowered to 1,000 euros. As a result, hundreds of thousands of small investors would also have to start paying tax on their profits from shares. JA21 and SGP have already said that this part of the funding is "unacceptable". They say the cabinet promised them it would come up with a different solution. This part of the plan may therefore be struck out again. The situation surrounding box 3 is now quite chaotic. Because the Tweede Kamer has already approved the accrual tax in the box 3 law, it now lies with <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Eerste Kamer</entity>. If the cabinet has a majority for the new plan, it must go back to the Tweede Kamer through an amendment (novelle). Only after that can the Eerste Kamer vote on it.

title: New Public Prosecution Service guideline: higher sentence demands for violence against care and emergency workers
lead: The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> must from now on always bring cases about violence against people with a public function before the court. In addition, prosecutors must also always demand a sentence twice as heavy, with a prison sentence as the starting point. That is set out in a new guideline from the College van procureurs-generaal, the national leadership of the Openbaar Ministerie, which takes effect tomorrow. Minister of Justice Van Weel writes to <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> that besides police officers and care workers, the guideline will also apply to, for example, teachers who face violence. The minister gives as an example an attempted serious assault on a care worker, where the perpetrator does not use a weapon, has not previously gone wrong, and the care worker was not injured. The sentence demand would then in principle be three months in prison, instead of 80 hours of community service if the victim was not a care worker. Heavier sentencing is already possible. The new guideline is a concession to the Tweede Kamer. Earlier this year, shortly before <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>-Jetten took office, it argued for heavier sentences to be demanded for violence against care workers. The House expressed its abhorrence of the increasing violence against police officers and care workers after it had again completely got out of hand during the New Year's celebrations a few weeks earlier. Since 2006, people who are aggressive and violent towards people with a public duty can already be punished 200 percent more severely than other perpetrators of violence. But according to the House, the OM does too little with this, so that perpetrators can still get away with a community service order or a fine. Right-wing parties in particular in the Tweede Kamer have asked in motions for heavier sentences for violence against care workers. 'I fully endorse that line', the minister of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-justitie-en-veiligheid">Justitie en Veiligheid</entity> writes today in his letter. Banning community service orders: Van Weel finds it 'unacceptable' that prosecutors would not follow earlier norms on heavier sentences, because 'violence and aggression against people with a public task is intolerable'. 'Society cannot do without the police officer, the care worker, the teacher and all other people with a public task', he states. 'They keep our society running and must be able to do their work safely and unhindered.' The Tweede Kamer also has a proposal to ban community service orders for violence against care workers altogether. Last year, the <entity id="org:raad-van-state">Raad van State</entity> and judges criticised this, wanting to keep the room to judge independently and to weigh specific circumstances.

title: House of Representatives wants to scrap tax for small investors and savers
lead: In the House of Representatives there is little enthusiasm for the plan to tax hundreds of thousands of small investors and savers. JA21, ChristenUnie and SGP are against it, and Pro is also opposed on principle. That seems to put a majority in the House for the plan out of sight. "It is a penalty on thrift or successful entrepreneurship," says SGP MP Flach during the General Financial Deliberations. "Disastrous for the ambition to get more Dutch people to invest their savings," thinks JA21 MP Hoogeveen. After a barrage of questions to coalition parties D66, VVD and CDA, they said they were willing to look at other solutions. "We too think this is an unfortunate point," said CDA MP Van Dijk. What exactly is in box 1, 2 and 3, and what is the solution now proposed for box 3? You can read that in this article: Many parties are nevertheless positive that the coalition wants to introduce a capital gains tax on shares, bonds and second homes from 2028, and on cryptocurrencies from 2030. This would finally offer a solution to the political problem surrounding box 3 after years of discussion. '200 euros taken, 100 euros given back' The opposition was more critical of the billions that <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> wants to bring in next year by raising income tax. Although the cabinet says that work should pay, the opposite is happening, the <entity id="org:raad-van-state">Raad van State</entity> noted earlier. Still, VVD MP Van Eijk does not intend to scrap this plan. She points out that many people's purchasing power is still going up. Opposition parties reacted critically. "That's first 200 euros taken, 100 euros given back, and then you're supposed to be happy," said, for example, BBB <entity id="person:hendrik-vermeer">Kamerlid Vermeer</entity>. How the coalition wants to get a majority for the Tax Plan therefore remains unclear. JA21 and Pro also only want to support the cabinet if the increased income tax is scaled back. Calming concerns: For left-wing parties the morning started festively: they congratulated each other that the cuts to social security are off the table after strikes. Because Pro wants to support the budget of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-sociale-zaken-en-werkgelegenheid">Sociale Zaken en Werkgelegenheid</entity> as a result, there now seems to be a majority for this budget. Still, there were many questions about the table that <entity id="person:eelco-heinen">minister Heinen</entity> (<entity id="org:ministerie-van-financien">Financiën</entity>) circulated, after it leaked via the NOS yesterday. It shows that a large part of the amount no longer being cut from social security now temporarily sits in the education budget. D66, which presents itself as an education party, tried to allay the concerns of the left-wing parties. MP Oosterhuis (D66) spoke of a table written by an "overeager civil servant" that was "not so relevant" and "without political value". But a different tone could be heard from Van Eijk (VVD). She confirms that it is "the technical elaboration" of the agreement within the coalition that if the cut to social security does not succeed, cuts will be made in education. Asked whether that is a sensible choice, she answers that more money "has not necessarily led to better quality education". The coalition said yesterday it expects the reforms of social security to still lead to savings. If any amount remains, the parties want to sit down next year to see where that money should come from. Starting shot for further negotiations: Tomorrow is the second day of the General Financial Deliberations. Then minister Heinen (Financiën) and <entity id="person:eelco-eerenberg">staatssecretaris Eerenberg</entity> (Fiscaliteit) will respond to the questions from the House of Representatives. It will be the starting shot for further negotiations. The uncertainty about the cabinet's financial plans will therefore linger for a while. This may change ahead of the treatment of the Tax Plan, which the House of Representatives will discuss from mid-October. It sets out how the government will collect taxes in the coming years.

title: Government takes over oversight of estate agents from estate agents themselves
lead: Housing minister Boekholt-O'Sullivan (D66) reluctantly is going to get involved in the estate agency sector. She is going to introduce an estate agents' register and a complaints desk for dissatisfied buyers and sellers. "A great many people feel that buying or selling a house is not a fair process." The minister had research carried out. Nearly a third of respondents had at least one negative experience with an estate agent, in many cases a selling agent. Nearly ninety percent of the complaints concerned an estate agent affiliated with a trade association. Only two percent of those people filed an official report. The minister would have preferred that the sector itself reach agreements on quality and fairness. The professional organisations together represent a large part of the market and should normally have a lot of influence on implementing improvements, the minister thought. But in talks with the various estate agent organisations, they told her that despite codes of conduct and improvement plans they had not succeeded. They do not feel strong enough compared with rogue estate agents. So the government has to step in. "That is a big step and I would rather not have done it", says Boekholt. At the government's estate agents' register, all estate agents will have to register in order to be allowed to practise their profession. "By doing so you commit yourself to certain rules. You work transparently, you are honest and you show the bid book." A bid log is a record of all bids that have been made on a home. "Sometimes people get advice from their estate agent to bid ten thousand euros more", says Boekholt. "But they have no idea whether there is a bid from other people below that." Some estate agents thus drive up the price. Or they favour certain clients. Or they harm their client by passing on confidential information. Boekholt stresses that most estate agents work normally and support their clients well. It concerns a small number who misbehave. For clients who run into that, a disputes committee will be set up. Depending on the seriousness of the complaints or the number of complaints, in the most extreme case it can strike an estate agent off and remove them from the register. That agent can then no longer practise their profession in the Netherlands. Estate agent is a free profession. Since 2001 anyone who wants to can call themselves an estate agent. No legally required diploma is needed. You can join a trade association, but you do not have to. There are currently two trade associations: NVM and Vastgoed Nederland. They have drawn up rules, but these are not strictly enforced. The trade associations say that estate agents would then cancel their membership. Complaints about estate agents are not a new phenomenon and there are many of them. Vereniging Eigen Huis (VEH) reported in August that since February more than 900 complaints about estate agents had come in to the complaints point. The PVV in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> is responding to the ongoing complaints with a bill for the estate agency sector. Member of parliament Mooiman proposes codes of conduct, a national professional register, external oversight and fines for violations. The trade organisations reacted positively to this. <entity id="person:elanor-boekholt-osullivan">Minister Boekholt</entity> sees Mooiman's bill as help on the way to effective and workable legislation. "That is why I am happy to team up with the submitter." Concrete proposals will be on the table by early 2027, the minister promises.

title: Self-employed act must give zzp'ers and clients clarity
lead: After years of discussion about sham self-employment, a new act must put an end to the debate about when someone is a zzp'er and when not. "This must provide clarity for entrepreneurs and clients", says <entity id="person:thierry-aartsen">minister Aartsen</entity> of Work and Participation. Clients who work with sham self-employed people risk back-tax assessments from the <entity id="org:belastingdienst">Belastingdienst</entity> for tax and social premiums. Because of the unclear rules, some clients stopped hiring zzp'ers. The new act contains criteria that zzp'ers and clients can hold on to, says Aartsen. If you work independently of others, bear entrepreneurial risks and have the freedom to organise your work yourself, then you are an entrepreneur. Three clients In concrete terms, this means you must have a registration with the <entity id="org:zbo-kamer-van-koophandel">Kamer van Koophandel</entity>, a VAT number, a business bank account, and issue invoices and make business payments. Over a period of two years you must have at least three different clients or customers and be actively recruiting new clients. "These are not unreasonable criteria we set", says Aartsen. "If you meet them, you can be sure you do not need to fear back-tax assessments." The work itself must also meet criteria. As an entrepreneur you must in principle be free to decide where, when and how you carry out the assignment. Unless the work can really only be carried out in a certain place, such as a construction site, or at a certain time, such as repair work outside office hours or opening hours. Pensions and insurance Furthermore, the zzp'er must make arrangements that an employee does not need. Insurance against illness and incapacity for work, pension, insurance for damage caused by the work, and other entrepreneurial risks. A minimum amount for this will be included in the act; you do not have to have all of these arrangements. "We want to talk with entrepreneurs about the amount a zzp'er must at least spend on these arrangements", says Aartsen. "It must not be too much, but it must not be a token amount either." For most entrepreneurs these are all matters of course. With this act they are legally recognised as self-employed entrepreneurs. But precisely for the group where it is unclear, the act must help them still meet the criteria. Until 29 October, stakeholders can respond to the draft act texts via Internetconsultatie.nl. Afterwards there will be further debates with the Tweede Kamer and the <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">Eerste Kamer</entity>. The act will not take effect before 1 January 2028.

title: Bolle Jos now also on the agenda in Europe: payments to Sierra Leone stopped
lead: The European Commission has immediately stopped payments to Sierra Leone because the country is not cooperating in the extradition of drug criminal Bolle Jos. This is confirmed by <entity id="person:david-van-weel">minister Van Weel</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-justitie-en-veiligheid">Justitie en Veiligheid</entity> after a report in De Telegraaf. Sierra Leone was due to receive 18 million euros in budget support from Brussels this year. That money is intended for, for example, food programmes, education and infrastructure in the very poor country. The Netherlands hopes that a further payment of 22.5 million can be stopped next year. This is still being negotiated among the EU member states. Turning off the money tap has long been a wish of the Netherlands, because the fugitive Jos L., alias Bolle Jos, has found refuge in the African country. He is said to have close ties there with people in high positions, including the president. Hundred years' imprisonment: L. is called the most wanted criminal in the Low Countries. In the Netherlands he has been sentenced to 24 years in prison for cocaine trafficking and an attempted murder, and in Belgium he has received more than a hundred years of imprisonment in various cases combined. "With this step I am very pleased", says Van Weel in the Telegraaf. "It is bitter that EU money is going to a country that does not want to cooperate in the extradition of someone like Bolle Jos." The Dutch minister hopes this will be seen as a firm statement, that not only the Netherlands but the entire European Union disapproves of Sierra Leone's unwillingness. Tightening sanctions The EU is looking at ways to further tighten its sanctions policy for criminals who stay outside Europe, for example by imposing an entry ban or freezing financial assets. Van Weel is now in Luxembourg for a meeting of European justice ministers, where this will also be discussed. The European Parliament recently adopted a resolution stating that "persons convicted of serious drug trafficking offences must not escape prosecution." The Dutch drug baron Jos L. is named in it.

title: Cabinet willing to spare smaller savers and investors after all
lead: The minority cabinet is willing to change the wealth tax plans so that smaller savers and investors are spared. That is what <entity id="person:eelco-heinen">minister Heinen</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-financien">Financiën</entity> said on the second day of the General Financial Debate. He did warn that it is "enormously complicated" to find an alternative that yields the same amount. To free up money for introducing a profit tax on investments in box 3, the cabinet proposed that small investors and savers pay tax earlier and more from 2028. The exemption would be lowered, so that people would already be taxed if they earn more than a thousand euros a year in returns on their savings or investments. That plan was very poorly received by both the left and right opposition, as became clear yesterday. The cabinet could therefore not count on a majority for the budget. The factions of the coalition parties also indicated they were not happy about it either. Not many levers. Minister Heinen said today that he chose that threshold because a couple with savings of up to about 100,000 euros would then be excluded. But he also acknowledged today that the lower limit may not have been chosen so well after all. Many people who now still pay no tax on their savings will suddenly have to start paying. He underestimated that. "We are willing to accept a different threshold", he said. It does mean that money has to be found elsewhere in the tax area, and according to Heinen that is difficult. "We do not have very many levers to pull. And every choice you make is enormously complicated. It takes a lot of calculation." Temporary tax increase: In <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> there is also much concern about a temporary tax increase on wealth for next year. The exemption would then be lowered from just under 60,000 euros to about 31,000 euros. The percentage of tax people pay would also go up. The minister is also looking into that and wants to consult with the House of Representatives about a different lower limit from 2028. In two weeks, when the Tax Plan is discussed in the House, there must be clarity. 'The polder must deliver' In the debate there was also discussion about scrapping the cuts to social security. Heinen said he expects that if a social agreement is reached between employers and trade unions, it will yield more money than the cabinet had originally booked for the cut. According to him, the social partners have said they can deliver on that promise. A consequence of a social agreement should be that less money is spent on benefits such as the WW and WIA. But if an agreement in the 'polder' does not come about, or the reforms yield too little, the money must be found by cutting spending of the ministries. On Tuesday it turned out that in that case the Ministry of Education would be hit hardest: in the worst case 1.2 billion euros would have to be saved there. Education minister Letschert said yesterday there is no coalition agreement to cut education. Heinen stated today in the debate that the saving is "technically booked", but that it will never take place if the social partners keep their promise. "Then it is a non-discussion", said Heinen.

title: Minister Van Weel: Sierra Leone can resolve Bolle Jos conflict within 24 hours
lead: Sierra Leone can immediately resolve its problem with the European Commission by extraditing drug criminal Bolle Jos to the Netherlands. That is what minister Van Weel of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-justitie-en-veiligheid">Justitie en Veiligheid</entity> says from Luxembourg. This morning it became known that the European Commission has halted budget support to <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity> of the African country. The country would still receive 18 million this year for, for example, food programmes, education and infrastructure. Van Weel is in Luxembourg for a meeting of European justice ministers. They will discuss, among other things, tightening sanctions against fugitive criminals who stay outside Europe. The Dutch minister is pleased that the money tap to Sierra Leone has now been shut off. "It is a very clear signal from the European Commission that Sierra Leone must stop giving shelter to this criminal." 'Building pressure' Asked whether the measure is not too harsh, he points to the government of the poor country. That government is protecting a criminal "who is destroying an enormous amount, also for the population of Sierra Leone", he says. "They can resolve this within 24 hours by arresting this man and extraditing him." If this penalty measure does not help, "we will continue building pressure through other means", says Van Weel. "We are very keen to get this criminal to the Netherlands." Bolle Jos L. is called the most wanted criminal in the Low Countries. In the Netherlands he was sentenced to 24 years in prison for cocaine trafficking and an attempted liquidation, in Belgium he has received more than a hundred years of imprisonment in various cases combined.

title: Cabinet sits down with unions and employers on Wednesday after months of delay
lead: On Wednesday, the unions and employers will sit down with the cabinet for the first time in months to talk about the future of social security. The cabinet has invited six organisations, VNO-NCW, MKB NL, LTO, FNV, CNV and VCP, to come to the Catshuis on Wednesday. On behalf of the cabinet, <entity id="person:rob-jetten">premier Jetten</entity> and the three ministers most involved, Vijlbrief (Social Affairs), Aartsen (Work and Participation) and Herbert (<entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-ez">Economische Zaken</entity>), will attend. The unions FNV and CNV are coming to The Hague, the organisations said. That makes it likely that the other organisations will also accept the invitation. Since the end of May, the unions have not been talking with the cabinet about scaling back social security, the arrangements that exist to help Dutch people who cannot work or are retired. In May there was a Catshuis meeting on this, but the views diverged so much that it remained a single conversation. Talks would only resume, the unions made clear again and again, if the Jetten cabinet scrapped the planned cuts. The unions also announced actions. Scaling back The Jetten cabinet initially wanted to save around 6 billion euros by speeding up the increase in the AOW age and by scaling back the WW and WIA (incapacity for work) arrangements. The cabinet withdrew the AOW plan earlier, but the unions, supported by the largest opposition party PRO, kept insisting that all cuts to social security be withdrawn. The cabinet has now done so, at the beginning of this week, and talks with the 'polder' are being restarted. Long-term The unions, like the employers and the cabinet, recognise that the problems must be solved, especially with the WIA, the Work, Income and Labour Capacity Act. Around 60,000 people flow into the WIA each year, often young people and women with psychological problems. There is a major shortage of occupational physicians and the waiting lists are long. "We must not wait until people fall out of work for a long time, but prevent that," the unions FNV, CNV and VCP wrote earlier this week in a joint press release.

title: Van Weel stands by it: halting aid to Sierra Leone linked to Bolle Jos
lead: <entity id="person:david-van-weel">Minister Van Weel</entity> says there is no tension between him and the European Commission over halting aid to Sierra Leone. He maintains that it is a means of pressure, meant to lead to the extradition of drug criminal Jos L. Yesterday Van Weel announced that European aid had been ended because Sierra Leone was unwilling to extradite L. Those statements caused irritation behind the scenes at the European Commission. Halting the payments would be a purely technical matter and not a sanction to bring <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity> of Sierra Leone to its knees. But Van Weel sticks to his story. "I am glad that the European Commission has found a legal way to do this, and I think it helps build pressure on Sierra Leone," he said this morning ahead of <entity id="org:ministerraad">de ministerraad</entity>. The minister repeated that he is "on a mission" to get Jos L., alias Bolle Jos, extradited. He says he shuns no means and "also wants to confront Sierra Leone, if I think it is in the interest of this case". Diplomacy He is not aware that there is irritation about this within the European Commission. "I do not know the sources behind the scenes." He has only spoken with Eurocommissioner Brunner, who is responsible for the approach to organised crime. And "there was really no tension between us, we have a good relationship." According to Van Weel, Brunner did yesterday at a press conference make a connection to Bolle Jos, though in a less explicit way. In a subordinate clause the Eurocommissioner said: "We need the cooperation of Sierra Leone. That is what it is about." That the European Commission cites a technical reason externally for pausing development aid has to do, among other things, with diplomacy, he thinks. But Van Weel himself chooses "direct confrontation" with the country that is harbouring the fugitive criminal. "I chose this because I see that alongside diplomacy we need to build pressure in a different way." Sierra Leone was to receive 18 million euros in budget support from Brussels this year. That was suspended with immediate effect yesterday. As far as the Netherlands is concerned, the payment of 22.5 million for next year will also not go ahead, if Bolle Jos has still not been extradited by then.

title: Excise duty on vapes in just over two years
lead: Vapes (e-cigarettes) and refills will become euros more expensive from 1 January 2029 because the government is going to levy more tax on these products. Users already pay 21 percent VAT now. Excise duty will be added on top of that in just over two years. "It is shocking how many young people are now hooked on vapes," says <entity id="person:eelco-eerenberg">staatssecretaris Eerenberg</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-financien">Financiën</entity>. "When consumers see that it becomes much more expensive, they will think twice before spending their money on unhealthy junk." Flavour ban The rules for vapes are now almost the same as for regular cigarettes and tobacco products. Since 1 January 2024 there has been an official ban on flavoured vapes. The tobacco flavour is still allowed. Where smoking bans apply, those also apply to vapes. Points of sale for e-cigarettes must register just like tobacco shops. The expectation is that from 1 July 2027 or 1 January 2028, vapes may only be sold in specialist shops. Eerenberg: "It cannot be explained why only regular cigarettes are taxed extra to make sure people do not smoke. It should make no difference whether you do one or the other." The vape excise duties still have to be calculated, but they will be comparable to those on tobacco products. Harmful Vapes are, like tobacco products, harmful to health. In a vape, liquid with or without nicotine is heated so that vapour is produced. No tobacco is burned, so no tar or carbon monoxide is released. Users do, however, take in chemical substances. If excise duties on vapes come into effect in Europe earlier than 1 January 2029, then <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> will withdraw this proposal.

title: Podcast De Dag: David van Weel's hunt for Bolle Jos
lead: Sierra Leone will receive millions less from Europe this year. Justice Minister Van Weel said yesterday that this was decided because the country does not want to extradite Bolle Jos to the Netherlands. A different reason, technical in nature, then came from Brussels. This morning Van Weel says both are correct and that Europe is behind him in his hunt for Bolle Jos. Listen here: You can listen to this episode of De Dag via <entity id="org:zbo-nederlandse-publieke-omroep">NPO</entity> Luister and all other podcast apps. Do you like it? Then be sure to subscribe. What is Minister Van Weel doing to catch the drug criminal? Political reporter Jorn Jonker sees a determined minister who, despite personal consequences, is trying everything in his hunt for Bolle Jos. But do all these steps make sense? Sierra Leone expert at the Clingendael Institute Kars de Bruijne sees cracks forming in the drug criminal's empire. But extradition is anything but closer after all these steps. Questions or comments? Email dedag@nos.nl Presentation & editing: Marco Geijtenbeek Editorial: Marco Geijtenbeek & Max Smedes

title: Podcast De Stemming: Hyperfocus, financial charlatans and the Tweelco's
lead: <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Premier Jetten</entity> en <entity id="person:eelco-heinen">minister Heinen</entity> spoke last weekend and on Monday with various opposition parties about support for the budget. And that suddenly produced a breakthrough after <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> had scrapped the cuts to social security. But where you remove one cut from one budget, another usually gets added to someone else's. And that in turn led to confusion and unrest in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>. Podcast De Stemming This episode of De Stemming by Vullings and De Rooy can be listened to at <entity id="org:zbo-nederlandse-publieke-omroep">NPO</entity> Luister. You can also find all previous episodes there. Just like all other well-known podcast channels. About this podcast Political journalists Joost Vullings (EenVandaag, AVROTROS) and Marleen de Rooy (NOS) go through the Hague week every Friday, with sharp analyses, rumours and predictions. Want to respond? Email destemming@nos.nl.

title: Jetten on box 3 uncertainty: 'Understandable if people can no longer keep up'
lead: "I can imagine people can no longer keep up", <entity id="person:rob-jetten">premier Jetten</entity> admits about the uncertainty that arose around box 3. For a moment, hundreds of thousands of smaller investors and savers thought they would also have to pay tax on their assets. But after a day and a half, that plan is off the table again. The coalition had spent days trying to agree internally on a new plan for box 3. It was ready at the last minute, on the evening before the General Financial Considerations. The next day, not only the opposition was critical, but it also became clear that coalition parties had little appetite for taxing smaller savers and investors. And so <entity id="person:eelco-heinen">minister Heinen</entity> (<entity id="org:ministerie-van-financien">Financiën</entity>) could do nothing but admit, a day and a half later, that he had not thought the funding through properly. "A minority cabinet is tough", sighed the VVD minister as he arrived for <entity id="org:ministerraad">de ministerraad</entity>. 'Fear of a left-wing agenda' Also VVD deputy prime minister Yesilgöz said it had been "not a nice week", because of the "noise, commotion and image-making" around the Tax Plan. According to her, it has caused "fear of a left-wing agenda" among the VVD's base. As far as she is concerned, the emphasis should mainly be on what the right did manage to secure, such as the lower excise duty on petrol, the lower tax in box 2 and the lower flight tax. That there is now any majority at all for an accelerated capital gains tax in box 3 is also seen by the VVD as a major victory. "If you explain it factually, people understand very well what we are doing. The mega-problem around box 3 is now being solved in 2028", Yesilgöz said at the Council of Ministers. "Until two months ago, nobody thought that was possible." Still, there are some hurdles to clear. Introducing the accelerated wealth tax is estimated to cost 15 billion euros. <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> must now come up with a new funding plan within a few weeks, to still meet introduction in 2028. One of the options mentioned is to abolish a construction around inheritance tax, the gift on paper. That option is also sensitive for the VVD and other parties on the right. What is the solution now proposed for box 3? You can read that in this article: The coalition still hopes to find "broad support" for the Tax Plan, which sets out how the government collects tax in the coming years. It is still unclear how. Both Pro and JA21, parties needed for a majority, only want to support it if income tax goes down. The negotiations are made extra complicated because some parties only want to agree to the Tax Plan if the cabinet meets other conditions. For example, BBB wants the nitrogen plans to be amended and SGP wants abortions to be curtailed. Fits and starts The cabinet now has a few weeks to find a majority, because on 12 November <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> will vote on the Tax Plan. Meanwhile, the amendment for box 3 must also pass through the Eerste and Tweede Kamer, with fits and starts. "If the discussion is mainly about the funding of the proposal, that can always be resolved", Jetten remains optimistic. A bright spot for the cabinet is at least that the trade unions will sit back down at the table next Wednesday. Then the talks will begin on reforms to the WW and WIA, which according to the cabinet are ultimately also expected to yield savings.

title: VVD leader Yesilgöz very rosy about mood within party: yet members are cancelling
lead: VVD leader Yesilgöz has presented the reaction of her grassroots to the revised cabinet plans in a very rosy light. She said that new VVD members had joined, but that is not the whole story, as becomes clear when asking about the number of VVD members cancelling their membership this week. At the start of <entity id="org:ministerraad">de ministerraad</entity>, journalists asked Yesilgöz this morning whether it had been a tough week for her party. The VVD leader began listing the many things going well for her grassroots as well. For example, many people are happy that a solution has been found for box 3, the wealth tax, said Yesilgöz. And, she added: "We have also gained dozens of new members". The VVD party office has kept track of what has happened to membership numbers since Tuesday evening, when the revised cabinet plans were presented. From that moment through Thursday, the party says there were 78 cancellations. In those few days, 21 new sign-ups also came in. A spokesperson for the party office says that what Yesilgöz stated is therefore not incorrect. 'Exploding' There is discontent within the VVD about the cabinet plans revised this week. Members who spoke to the NOS talk about chat groups that seem to be "exploding". Mainly because <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> had initially wanted savers and investors to pay more tax in box 3. It also does not sit well that, for example, landlords and people with a second home must pay more. There are also groups of members who think the cuts to social security have been dropped too easily. They believe that reform is still needed on that issue. Some also feel that a knee-jerk move towards opposition party Pro has been made, while the campaign promised that the VVD would not go in that direction. Fred Teeven, a former state secretary for the party, said this week on Nieuws van de Dag: "I see many people leaving the VVD. If they want to keep any representation in the Provincial Councils, they had better watch out". Nuancing According to a spokesperson for Yesilgöz, the party leader is not at all dodging the fact that there are also people cancelling. The politician only wanted to nuance the picture being painted these days, namely that the whole world is negative about the VVD, by saying that new members have also joined. VVD-<entity id="person:vincent-karremans">minister Karremans</entity> of Infrastructure said this morning that it was a "turbulent week" for his party. He stressed that much unrest among his grassroots fades once it is explained what the VVD has secured in the revised cabinet plans. According to Karremans, the VVD suffers from the image that the party is so positive about scrapping the cuts to social security. Right-wing people then think the package will turn out badly for them if Pro is so positive, reasons the VVD member. Meanwhile, according to him, a great deal has indeed been agreed for the VVD grassroots, such as a swift shift to a capital gains tax. "That is being buried a bit, under Jesse Klaver's smile. But if you look under the bonnet, there is, I think, a solid package."

title: State secretary in favour of ban on slaughter without stunning: 'Taboo gone'
lead: <entity id="person:silvio-erkens">Staatssecretaris Erkens</entity> of Agriculture believes that, just as in Belgium, there should be a ban on slaughtering animals without stunning. He is using World Animal Day to make clear that slaughter without stunning, for animal welfare reasons, "does not belong in the Netherlands", he said this morning on the television programme WNL op Zondag . In an interview with RTL Nieuws that came out this morning, Erkens had already said that he "personally" believes that ritual slaughter without stunning hardly fits within cabinet policy to improve animal welfare in the Netherlands. The debate about slaughter without stunning has been going on for almost fifteen years and has become topical again because the Party for the Animals is submitting a bill again this month to ensure that animals are no longer slaughtered before they have been stunned. Razor sharp According to certain Islamic and Jewish religious rules, animals must be slaughtered without stunning. In the Netherlands this now happens under all kinds of rules to limit animal suffering. In a slaughterhouse an animal receives a cut in the neck with a razor-sharp knife from a certified so-called 'pre-cutter'. If the animal has not died within forty seconds, it must still be stunned. State Secretary Erkens considers that a long period for an animal. "That is forty seconds of animal suffering," he said on WNL op Zondag . He believes the taboo on the subject must be lifted. Complex He is not, incidentally, going to make a law himself to end slaughter without stunning in the Netherlands and mainly makes clear that <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> is positive about the Party for the Animals' bill. "It is a complex subject that touches on freedom of religion." He stresses that a law must come that is legally tenable. The Party for the Animals already put forward a bill in 2011 for a ban on ritual slaughter. In <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Eerste Kamer</entity> the bill was defeated; a majority of senators found that it conflicted with freedom of religion. The Party for the Animals then went on drafting an adjusted bill, which was also received positively by the <entity id="org:raad-van-state">Raad van State</entity>. Impact MP Ouwehand, who drafted this bill, stresses that not only religious slaughter was examined but also regular slaughter. "It is important to conduct the debate carefully, because this has an impact on the Jewish and Islamic faith communities." She is glad that State Secretary Erkens now clearly acknowledges that animal welfare is important in Dutch society. On WNL op Zondag Erkens stressed that there does not need to be an end to ritual slaughter, as long as the animal is stunned. He says that half of ritual slaughter in the Netherlands already happens this way. The animal is then temporarily stunned. That is acceptable to some religious groups, because the animal is then not dead.

title: Cabinet tightens screen use advice, phones in lockers for the entire school day
lead: The cabinet wants primary and secondary schools to ban the use of mobile phones throughout the entire school from 1 January 2027. Pupils may then no longer use their phones during break, in the assembly hall or on the schoolyard. Currently, at many schools, pupils are only not allowed to bring their phones into the classroom. This is one of the proposals from the so-called 'Strategy letter on online children's rights', in which, under the leadership of <entity id="person:willemijn-aerdts">staatssecretaris Aerdts</entity> (Digital Economy), various ministries have set out new and existing rules to better protect children online. The cabinet is not responsible for the phone use of pupils at Dutch schools, but can give an urgent recommendation. That also happened in 2024, when the Ministry of Education made national agreements with primary schools on limiting phones during lessons. The cabinet wants the tightened advice to take effect from 1 January 2027 at secondary schools and in primary education. Scrolling The cabinet, like many parents and other institutions, is concerned about the increasing online use of Dutch children and young people. At school, children are distracted and can concentrate less well. At home, parents find it difficult, for example, to curb their children's hours of scrolling. Because of addictive algorithms and automatically playing videos, it proves very hard to put the phone away, and daily screen times of around 5 to 6 hours are not unusual. Experts have long warned about the negative consequences of excessive screen use, such as sleep problems, short-sightedness and depression. Furthermore, it is unclear exactly what young people watch, and there is little insight into cyberbullying or other unpleasant matters. Unwanted contact Several ministries have for some time been working on various plans to offer young people sufficient protection against everything that can be viewed online. Today, State Secretary Aerdts presents a strategy for a "safe and healthy online world for children", with around forty arrangements, of which, according to her, fifteen are new. "Online, on social media or in video games, children quickly lose sight and run unacceptable risks", said the State Secretary. "Think of addictive algorithms, harmful images and unwanted contact." Work has been underway for some time on a number of measures from the Strategy letter, because they require a long-term effort. The European Commission has recently made a proposal for an age limit on social media. The European Commission considers 13 years, the Dutch cabinet 15 years. Other proposals include, for example, banning addictive techniques such as algorithms in the design of digital services at European level. A reliable age verification system must also be developed, in which the privacy of young people is well protected. Child labour The cabinet is also working on stricter rules for buy now, pay later services, such as the deferred payment service Klarna. The cabinet is also continuing to develop tightened rules for vlog families and kidfluencers. Online content of children under 15 will be seen as child labour and can be fined as such. The cabinet is also commissioning research into Netflix, YouTube, Roblox, Fortnite, ChatGPT, Instagram, Snapchat and TikTok to "gain better insight into how digital services affect the experience, development and choices of children who use digital services". The most concrete measure, banning phones in and around schools, must, according to the cabinet, therefore take effect in three months. <entity id="person:judith-tielen">Staatssecretaris Tielen</entity> of Education is now going to make agreements on this with the education sector.

title: Introducing a capital gains tax in 2028 becomes a race against the clock
lead: <entity id="person:eelco-heinen">Minister Heinen</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-financien">Financiën</entity> promised <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> last week that he would do everything possible to introduce the new capital gains tax as early as 2028. It will be a race against the clock, and those involved are wondering whether it will all work out. On Friday <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> sent the bill needed to make the new system possible to the <entity id="org:raad-van-state">Raad van State</entity> for advice. Many MPs asked whether that advice would arrive in time for the next parliamentary debate on the subject, on 12 October. Heinen was optimistic on Thursday: "We are asking everyone for a maximum stretch, but then 2028 is achievable." He did acknowledge the risk that it will become 2029. A swift introduction of the new wealth tax is politically important to Heinen. It was an important commitment to right-wing opposition parties such as JA21 and the SGP. On request, the Raad van State says it will certainly not meet the deadline of 12 October. "We have only seven days left, impossible," a spokesperson states. The advice will arrive at the earliest on 19 October, and possibly not until the 26th. That makes it even tighter for the House to handle the law in time. Fraud lurking The banks say on request that they have too little time to adapt their IT systems. As a result, it will not be possible to have their customers' data pre-filled when those customers file their tax returns in 2028. The banks had already warned about this, but <entity id="person:eelco-eerenberg">staatssecretaris Eerenberg</entity> of Financiën suggested last week that there would be a solution. According to him, many banks have recently spoken out in favour of the new capital gains tax. "So I think we may also ask: now you must also help your clients make that possible." The Nederlandse Vereniging van Banken does not recognise that. "We have never expressed a preference for taxation of capital gains or capital accrual." A meeting with the <entity id="org:belastingdienst">Belastingdienst</entity> will soon take place to see what is possible as long as the pre-filled returns are not available, a spokesperson says. If banks and asset managers cannot supply the data, the Belastingdienst cannot check whether citizens have filled in their returns correctly. And then fraud lurks. For people who fill in their returns in good faith, it is questionable whether they can find the information themselves. Not all banks can supply the data directly to their customers. In any case, it makes filling in the return more complicated. Officials at Financiën already warned about this in an advice: "This places an additional burden on the 'doing capacity' of citizens." Even if the above problems are solved, it will be a real challenge for the Belastingdienst to carry out the system change by 2028. The service is also busy with adjustments to its computer systems, because a mandatory disability insurance for self-employed people arrives in 2030. If both adjustments have to be carried out at the same time, the introduction of that insurance will probably be delayed by a year, officials warned. Last week the cabinet made a new proposal for an accelerated transition to a capital gains tax, as a replacement for the current capital accrual tax. The VVD came under great pressure from its base, because investors object to paying tax on 'paper profit', that is, tax on shares that have not yet been sold and have only become more valuable on paper. Paying on sale But if citizens only start paying once the shares are sold, billions of euros in tax revenue will temporarily come in less. The cabinet wanted to fill that gap by also making smaller savers and investors pay capital gains tax, but there was no majority for that in the House of Representatives. Remarkably, the proposal sent to the Raad van State still contains that funding, which the House rejected. Meanwhile the cabinet is looking for alternatives, in consultation with opposition parties. That means further adjustments to box 3 are coming, also for next year. If the legislation does not get through the House of Representatives and the <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">Eerste Kamer</entity> this year, the current system will remain in force for at least another year. Each year of delay costs the treasury 3.5 billion euros in lost revenue. Eerste Kamer This evening Heinen and Eerenberg will provide text and explanation in the Eerste Kamer. The senators have repeatedly postponed votes on the box 3 plans at the request of the cabinet. And now there is urgency. Senator Crone of Pro is indignant about this course of events: "This is a major system change. We must handle it carefully, including by hearing experts." His colleague Griffioen of government party D66 urges the cabinet to make good use of the short time left: "The cabinet is responsible for getting this right, so do not dawdle and come up with good proposals."

title: Cabinet wants to link public transport and other transport in the region
lead: The cabinet wants to counter the erosion of public transport in the region by linking public transport and other types of transport, such as pupil transport, with each other. Trials with self-driving buses must also come. <entity id="person:annet-bertram">Staatssecretaris Bertram</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-infrastructuur-en-waterstaat">Infrastructuur en Waterstaat</entity> writes in two letters to <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> that she is very concerned about accessibility in the region. She wants to look at whether, "with the available resources", hospitals and cultural institutions, for example, can also become more accessible. She points out that besides regular public transport there are already all kinds of alternatives, such as regional taxis, on-demand buses, neighbourhood buses and shared cars. However, these still largely operate alongside each other. For example, you see buses driving one after another to the same place, one time for pupil transport and another time for WMO transport for people who cannot travel independently by public transport. As far as she is concerned, much more efficient cooperation is possible. 'Fine-meshed network' Bertram envisions a "fine-meshed network of public transport", in which an important role is reserved for a mobility centre where all requests come in and "characteristics of all travellers" are known, so that "the available vehicles" can be deployed optimally. The state secretary also wants to conduct three trials with self-driving buses. Since last year one such bus already runs in Rotterdam, carrying people from a metro station to the airport. The state secretary fears a downward spiral when it comes to accessibility outside cities. Fewer older people can reach a hospital within three quarters of an hour, she notes. The ANP reported this week that 1100 bus stops have disappeared in the past six years, mainly in Drenthe and Groningen. Stalling "The current system is starting to stall", Bertram concludes. Transport operators are struggling with driver shortages, while buses outside peak hours often run empty. On Prinsjesdag the cabinet announced that it will set aside 300 million euros annually to improve regional accessibility. Later this month the minister will announce how she plans to spend this money.

title: Former head of German intelligence arrested for espionage
lead: The former head of the German intelligence service BND, August Hanning, has been arrested. According to German media, Hanning is suspected of espionage, high treason and disclosing state secrets, among other things. The German public prosecution service has confirmed his arrest. Hanning headed the Bundesnachrichtendienst (BND) from 1998 to 2005. He is alleged to have purchased, among other things, secret information from a BND employee up until 2022. He is said to have used this information to draw up a security analysis for a foreign intelligence service. It is not known which country, but according to German media it would not be Russia. He is also said to have shared internal information with a foreign agent. House search The 80-year-old Hanning was arrested at his home this morning. The former employee, who held a senior position at the service, has also been arrested. The man was previously an important right-hand man of Hanning and worked for the BND until spring. The authorities came onto the case after they conducted a house search at Hanning's home in September last year in connection with a kidnapping case. In the investigation into that case, a tip came in that information may have been leaked from the BND. Hanning may also have been involved in the kidnapping itself, although he has always denied this. During the house search, agents found highly sensitive information originating from the BND. The secret documents dated from the recent past, so Hanning should never have possessed them. According to sources, Hanning is said to have received around 2,000 documents, which reportedly included reports on Iran's nuclear programme and the Russian army. Key positions Throughout his career, Hanning held key positions in German security services for many years. After his period at the BND, he was responsible for security as state secretary at <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity>, after which he went into the business sector. In recent years Hanning has worked as a consultant in the security and business world, among other things. He did so in places all over the world. German media report that he has good connections with Russia and China and their government authorities.

title: Measles outbreak in New York and Pennsylvania largest since the 1990s
lead: Measles is spreading rapidly in the American states of New York and Pennsylvania. New York has even declared a state of emergency, after more than a hundred people have already been infected this week. Because of the state of emergency, care workers can intervene faster and may, for example, test and distribute vaccines more quickly. In Pennsylvania, the number of registered measles cases this year has passed the thousand mark. This makes it one of the largest outbreaks since the early 1990s. Nearly two hundred patients have been admitted to hospital and five people have died. Health experts link such outbreaks to the falling vaccination rate in the US. Large outbreaks have also been reported since the beginning of last year in other states, such as Texas, Utah and South Carolina. What is measles? Measles is a highly contagious infectious disease caused by a virus. A measles infection usually runs a mild course, but serious complications can occur and the patient can die from it. According to WHO figures, around 95,000 people worldwide died of measles in 2024, mainly children under the age of 5. Measles can be recognised by a sudden high fever, red eyes, coughing, a cold and red spots on the skin that often feel rough. In the Netherlands, more than five hundred people got measles last year, mainly children at primary schools where few pupils were vaccinated. In the Netherlands there is a shot against measles, the MMR vaccine. Along with Pennsylvania and New York, Ohio is also dealing with a serious measles outbreak: more than 200 infections have already been confirmed there this year. As in Pennsylvania, some of the hardest-hit areas in Ohio are home to strictly Christian Amish communities, where the vaccination rate is generally lower. According to the American health agency CDC, the US is experiencing its worst measles outbreak nationwide since 1991, with nearly 4,000 cases in total so far. About twenty percent of these are children under the age of five. In the past two years, eight people have died of complications related to measles. That is more deaths than in the thirty years before that combined. Deaths In February 2025, Robert F. Kennedy Jr. was appointed Minister of Health in the Trump <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity> administration. For years he was one of the loudest vaccine critics in the US. For example, shortly after taking office he dismissed all the experts on the vaccine advisory committee and partly replaced them with vaccine sceptics. After several deaths from measles, he somewhat softened his positions on the disease. For instance, he stated that the MMR vaccine is the most effective way to prevent the spread of the disease. But the consequences of his criticism are already becoming visible. The vaccination rate is now already below the 95 percent needed to contain the spread of measles. As a result, infection figures are rising rapidly in several states. In November, international health officials will meet to determine whether the US and Mexico have lost their status as measles-free countries. A country must go twelve months without cases of the disease to be declared measles-free. Disinformation about vaccines and problems with access to healthcare also cause some parents not to have themselves or their children vaccinated. Salmonella Alongside measles outbreaks, the US is also struggling with a number of foodborne diseases. For example, this year nearly 13,000 Americans developed diarrhoea and other stomach and abdominal complaints from eating lettuce contaminated with the intestinal parasite. The American Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has since traced the contamination to a Mexican farm. American media report that food products in the US are increasingly being recalled due to contamination by bacteria, viruses or parasites. This concerns eggs, chicken or meat, among other things. According to various media, this development is caused by budget cuts and staff leaving the FDA and the US Department of Agriculture, which puts food inspections under pressure. The American health service CDC is currently investigating 33 outbreaks of food-related diseases, including salmonella, E. coli and listeria.

title: Drone attack on ships off Bulgarian coast, prime minister holds emergency meeting
lead: A ship has sunk off the coast of Bulgaria in the Black Sea after a drone attack. A fire broke out on another ship, Bulgarian President Iotova confirms in a statement. According to Prime Minister Radev, the crew of the sunken ship is missing. It is not clear how many people are involved. A search operation has been launched for them. Eighteen crew members have been rescued from the burning ship. Some have been taken to hospital in Varna, on Bulgaria's east coast. Local media report that one of them has serious burns, and another is reportedly injured in the head. Several others have minor injuries. Cargo ships. According to media sources, these are cargo ships. The sunken ship, named Alfa Watan, sailed under the flag of Togo. It is not known what cargo the ship was carrying. The ship where the fire broke out, named Able, sailed under the flag of Palau. That ship is known to have been carrying grain. The attack took place at around 03.00 local time, about 112 kilometres from the coast, still within Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone. That country is a member of NATO. After the incident, both ships sent out distress signals. Bulgarian Prime Minister Radev held an emergency meeting with the relevant ministries and security services. It is not yet clear whether this was an attack with drones in the air, sea drones, or both. Reference to war between Russia and Ukraine. It is not yet clear who is behind the drone attack. However, in a televised statement, the Bulgarian prime minister referred to the Russian war in Ukraine. Reuters news agency, citing a source in maritime security, writes that initial analyses of the attack point to it likely being a Russian attack. "If this war does not end in time, the risk of a global conflict grows," said Prime Minister Radev. "We see that the war is escalating: all rules of international law are being violated and civilian ships are being attacked at sea. This is completely unacceptable." Russia has not yet responded to the incident. Fire on Turkish ship. The attack follows shortly after a fire on a ship in the Black Sea yesterday, outside the territorial waters of Romania. Two people died in that incident, and eleven crew members could be rescued. The Romanian Ministry of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> says it is not yet known what caused that fire. Ukrainian President Zelensky accuses Russia of a drone attack on a Turkish ship carrying maize. Since the start of the war between Ukraine and Russia four years ago, several European countries have had to deal with Russian drones violating their airspace, as well as with mines in the Black Sea on important trade and energy routes.

title: 'Swimming lessons for children with disabilities need to be more accessible'
lead: For children with a disability, swimming lessons are not always a given, especially when their parents have money worries. Municipal income support for these parents falls short, says the Mulier Institute, which carried out research on the subject. Swimming lessons for children with a disability are often more expensive than regular swimming lessons. The research shows that children benefit from smaller groups of four or two pupils and sometimes even one-on-one lessons. "That is so they have fewer distractions from other children and get more attention from their teacher," explains researcher Mirjam Stuij of the Mulier Institute. A swimming instructor also needs to know how to handle a child with a disability. These two factors make adapted swimming lessons more expensive. "That is difficult for parents, but also for swimming instructors." Existing schemes fall short Municipalities already offer schemes and allowances, but these are sometimes unclear and differ from municipality to municipality. Parents run into several issues when applying, Stuij explains. "For example, the allowance they receive does not cover the cost of the swimming lessons." There are also parents who formally have too high an income, but who, because of high care costs or other high costs due to the child's disability, still have money worries. They therefore do not qualify. Thirdly, the institute sees that applying for schemes can demand a lot from parents. This is because information from the municipality is unclear or because parents do not know where to turn. Fewer or no certificates Stuij stresses that parents consider a swimming certificate of great importance. "If my child falls into a ditch, I want them to be able to save themselves. I think we can all picture that very well in the Netherlands." Figures from the <entity id="org:zbo-centraal-bureau-voor-de-statistiek">CBS</entity> show that 14 percent of children living in poverty have a disability, compared with 8 percent of children not living in poverty. Figures from Mulier also show that children with a disability obtain a swimming certificate at a later age, fewer certificates, or no swimming certificate at all. Clarity and flexibility The institute advises municipalities to map out how things are arranged for them, what the municipality reimburses and for whom. "Because we know that varies enormously," says Stuij. The research leads to a number of recommendations for local governments. For example, good information provision for parents should be established and the application process should be made as clear as possible. The institute calls for more flexibility in income support. For example, a standard allowance that can be increased if the costs for a child are higher, Stuij explains. The institute also advises appointing a fixed point of contact for parents. "Someone who can help them with the application and, for example, with finding suitable swimming lessons."

title: Event organisers in Breda send urgent letter about higher permit costs
lead: Eighteen event organisations in Breda, such as Breda Jazz, Ploegendienst and carnival activities, have together sent an urgent letter to the city council. They demand more transparency about the announced price increases for event permits, writes Omroep Brabant . From 2027 the municipality will increase the costs of an event permit. For example, the cost of a permit for large events, such as the big carnival parade, will rise from 17.000 euro to nearly 37.000 euro. For smaller events, the rate will double from 4900 to just over 10.000 euro. 'It is not going to work' The organisations fear that the higher costs will be the downfall of some events. Stichting Kielegat, a volunteer organisation for carnival activities in the city, says it cannot afford the price increase. "I see no possibility of raising that amount extra within a year. It is simply not going to work", said chairman Rutger Westenburg after the announcement. The Breda Jazz Festival attracts around 250.000 visitors each year. Even so, the price increase also shocked chairwoman Hanneke Griffioen. "It is a substantial amount, so you blink and then think: am I reading this correctly?" She therefore wants to sit down with the municipality. "Because this is not a normal price increase." The municipality says the higher costs are necessary because for many years Breda has only passed on around twenty percent of the costs related to permit applications. "We have tried to keep the increase limited, but unfortunately... Everything is getting more expensive", said the responsible alderman Arjen van Drunen. According to Van Drunen, even after the increase the full costs are still not covered. Transparency Among the signatories of the letter are volunteer organisations, but also commercial organisers. Koninklijke Horeca Nederland Breda and organised hospitality entrepreneurs have also joined. "We above all want transparency with all these organisations about how these permit fees have been built up", says Johan de Vos of Koninklijke Horeca Nederland Breda. "We want to see what the justification is. That this is a broadly supported demand is clear from all the organisations that have backed this letter." The organisers demand access to the full calculation behind the new rates. They want to know how many official hours are charged, which hourly rates are passed on, and whether costs for enforcement, public order and traffic measures have been included in the rates. Afterwards they want to discuss with the municipality which part of the costs organisers should pay. According to them, it should be clear which costs really belong to the permit and which belong to the municipality's normal tasks. "The mere fact that certain work takes place around events does not automatically mean that these costs can be recovered from the individual organiser through event fees", they write. The event organisations also want to examine whether the permit process can be made cheaper.

title: Heavy art book with work by Dalí stolen from French museum
lead: One of the most expensive and heaviest books in the world has been stolen from a museum in France. The cover of the artwork Apocalypse, made by Salvador Dalí alone, weighs 150 kilos. It is a mystery how the thieves got the extremely heavy book out of the building. The public prosecutor has started an investigation into the theft in the municipality of Issoire, about a hundred kilometres west of Lyon. The police have not released details about the art theft in the night from Sunday to Monday. It is unclear whether there are suspects. 'Murder of heritage' The owner of the artwork calls the theft an attack on the French cultural sector. "France has been murdered last night. French heritage has been murdered", Christian Karoutzos said yesterday evening to French media. The Apocalypse was made between 1958 and 1961 and weighs about 210 kilos in total. Fourteen of the most renowned artists of that time contributed to the project. The famous Spanish painter Dalí made the bronze cover. Dalí was one of the best-known artists of the last century. He painted surrealist works and was an eccentric person. He wore a distinctive thin moustache, with the tips curled upwards. The moustache is "the most serious part of my personality", Dalí once said jokingly in an interview.

title: Cat-theft ring in Vietnam busted: 'Thousands of animals stolen'
lead: The Vietnamese <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> has dismantled a network responsible for the theft of thousands of cats in Ho Chi Minh City. Twelve men are suspected of stealing and reselling the animals, presumably for consumption, state media report. The main suspect is 39-year-old Luu Thanh Binh, who is the suspected gang leader. According to the police investigation, Binh bought live cats and stored them at a location in the city before reselling them. Several people worked under him, who in turn recruited others to steal cats in different parts of the city. The network consisted of small groups, each with its own area. At night, the groups went through residential neighbourhoods on motorbikes in search of cats. They made their own cat traps. According to the suspects, each group stole four to ten cats per night. 50 cats rescued In July, the police raided the Dong Thanh district. 50 cats were rescued during the raid. Dozens of cat traps, scales, mobile phones, motorbikes, clippers and cash were also seized. Of the 50 rescued cats, thirteen have since been reunited with their owners, while the search for the other owners continues. During questioning, the suspects reportedly admitted to having stolen a total of 2,700 cats. It is not known exactly how long the gang was active. During an earlier raid in June, 400 cats were rescued. The animals were locked up in 45 cages. During that raid, more than 80 dead cats were also found, which were being kept cold with ice. Nine people were arrested. Eating cats and dogs Eating cats and dogs is not illegal in Vietnam, provided sellers hold the proper licences. The police emphasise that knowingly buying illegal meat is punishable, as is trading in stolen animals. There are no official figures on the local consumption of dogs and cats, but resistance to it has been growing in Vietnam in recent years. Particularly among young people and pet owners, writes animal welfare organisation Humane World for Animals. They point to the cruelty and animal abuse involved in the illegal catching, trade, storage and transport of the animals. But there is also increasing opposition because cats and dogs are increasingly seen as companion animals and not as food.

title: Online trade in 'blackmail packages' of women, Belgium and Netherlands investigate
lead: <entity id="person:david-van-weel">Minister Van Weel</entity> (VVD) of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-justitie-en-veiligheid">Justitie en Veiligheid</entity> will ask the Dutch <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> to offer help to the Belgian police, who are investigating the trade in nude photos of women on the so-called darkweb. He said this in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>, where he was asked questions about the case, which RTL reported. Nude photos and private data of hundreds of Belgian and Dutch women are being traded on the hidden part of the internet, RTL reported. Ready-made packages with intimate photos, social media profiles and contact details are offered on a site that has been active since 2023. Women can be harassed and blackmailed with them. For one euro per victim, access to private data and photos is provided. The 'packages' are sold to several people at once. The website offers, for a payment of 250 euros, to remove the data from the platform, but it is unclear whether this actually happens. 'Perverse practices' There is great revulsion across the House. Minister Van Weel spoke of appalling practices of a "perversity you do not often see". He also expressed his sympathy with the victims. One of the victims is a 31-year-old woman from Limburg who told her story to RTL. She had panic attacks when she heard she was on the site. Fifteen years later her photos still keep appearing. Van Weel called her story shocking and believes she is doing fantastic work, including by removing the shame felt by victims. MPs want justice to act firmly, if necessary at European level. "This concerns organised sexual violence", says VVD MP Becker. "These are not incidents, but a business model", says Pro MP Mutluer. The House wants the site to go offline as soon as possible. Parties also want the Dutch <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> to be involved in the case quickly. 'Investigation difficult' What is happening here is punishable, but investigating it will not be easy, says Van Weel. "It is technically not simple to find out who is behind it on the darkweb, where the server is, how a site can go offline". Van Weel says he "cannot take the darkweb offline with a bill tomorrow". According to him there are ways to take sites offline, but "first very specific technical investigations are needed, and we will certainly commit to those". The Belgian police have announced an investigation and Van Weel will ask the Dutch police to "consult the Antwerp police and see how we can help". The Dutch Openbaar Ministerie is not yet conducting an investigation into the case, a spokesperson told the NOS, but the OM does not rule out joining a later international joint investigation. "Given the facts and the number of potential Dutch victims, it would make sense if a request for help comes from Belgium; then we are also willing to help." Can you check whether your data has been leaked? For anyone worried after this news about whether her data or photos can be found on the darkweb, there is unfortunately no satisfactory answer: there is currently no simple way to search for that, says a spokesperson for the knowledge centre Offlimits to the NOS.
