ING has not wanted clients linked to Russia, such as Gazprom, since the Russian invasion of Ukraine. After the invasion, countless Russian companies were placed on the European sanctions list. Although Gazprom is not on it, the company does pose a risk to ING, the bank says. There would be sanctions and money laundering risks, and the bank also fears reputational damage. For that reason ING terminated the business relationship at the end of 2023. Gazprom did not accept this because it has no other European bank account. Without such an account, Gazprom cannot, for example, pay taxes or pay wages to European employees. Russian banking activities The bank wanted to accommodate the energy company by postponing the termination, so that it could open a bank account elsewhere. But on 1 October this year ING's patience ran out and it wanted to move to terminating the contract. The Russian company went to court to have the termination prohibited. According to its own account, Gazprom is simply not managing to find an alternative. The court agrees. Moreover, there is no concrete evidence of money laundering risks, the court says. Conversely, ING is not managing to get rid of its Russian banking activities. Last year the company found a buyer for ING Russia, but the Russian buyer has not been able to obtain approval from the local authorities for the deal.

title: Poland as Europe's growth champion: why the takeover of neighbourhood supermarket Zabka says a lot
lead: You can't miss them in Poland, because they are everywhere: Zabka stores. Sometimes opposite each other, or in the same building. These characteristic neighbourhood supermarkets with green facades and logo sell everything: from simple groceries to drinks and a hot dog. The popularity of Zabka is telling on several levels of the blossoming Polish economy. It shows that consumers in Poland have more and more money and that the country is becoming increasingly attractive to foreign investors. For example, the Canadian Alimentation Couche-Tard wants to take over the store chain for about 7.5 billion euros. The takeover is expected to be completed in December. Yes, a Zabka store is more expensive than a regular supermarket. "But you save time with it", says Rafal. He is a stylist, on his way to work, and has just got coffee at a neighbourhood supermarket in the centre of Warsaw. "I have one in my apartment building too, I do my shopping there every day." Europe's growth champion In the Netherlands we may know comparable shops, such as Hema or Albert Heijn to Go. But Zabka appears about ten times as often in proportion. According to the company, half of the 37 million Poles now live within 500 metres of a Zabka. Poland is the 'growth champion of Europe', concludes economist Marcin Piatkowski. He is affiliated with the Kozminski University in Warsaw. "Poland has changed dramatically from a poorly performing, bankrupt communist economy, where no sausage could be found in the shops, to a country where investing in consumer goods is the right choice", he tells the NOS. The Polish economy was already growing strongly, but after joining the EU in 2004 it went even faster. The European market offered many opportunities for a country with high production capacity. EU subsidies also contributed to economic development, including the financing of the construction of motorways. The transformation of Poland can be seen and felt everywhere. In Warsaw one skyscraper after another is being built. Since 2022 the Polish capital has even housed the tallest building in the European Union: the Varso Tower, which is 310 metres high including its spire. Economic growth Poland's economic growth has been above the European average for years. This year the economy is expected to grow by 3.4 percent, considerably faster than the Netherlands (1.5 percent) and the EU average of 1.4 percent. Poles are relatively well educated and willing to work long hours, but labour in many sectors is still half as expensive as in the Netherlands, Piatkowski points out. "But they do want to become just as rich as the Dutch." Moreover, the Polish economy is highly diversified and therefore not dependent on a single sector. That makes the country less vulnerable to problems in individual industries, such as the car industry, which is currently having a difficult time. Zabka is certainly not the only Polish company attracting foreign interest. InPost, which grew big with parcel lockers, has been taken over by a large consortium in which the American parcel delivery company Fedex plays a major role. According to economist Piatkowski, this shows that Poland has won a firm place on the world economic map. "People realise that Poland is a reliable and safe place to invest." Still, Poland also faces major economic challenges. A towering budget deficit that <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity> is failing to bring under control is one of them. In addition, Poland is also experiencing a shortage on the labour market. Rising wages are also gradually making it harder for Poland to compete. But for now, the expectation is that growth will continue. Poland's international standing is also growing. In December the country has been invited as a guest to the G20 summit in Miami, where the leaders of the world's largest economies gather. Piotr (40) comes out of Zabka with a cap on. He has just bought a phone card and a bar that was on offer. Yes, that budget deficit is indeed a worrying matter. But otherwise Piotr is positive about the future of his country. In his view, Warsaw is unrecognisable compared with the nineties. "If someone had left back then and came back now, he would be pleasantly surprised", he concludes. "Because the progress is clearly visible."

title: Renewed unrest in Amsterdam's Floradorp: stones and glass thrown at police
lead: In the Floradorp neighbourhood in <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">Amsterdam</entity>-Noord there was again unrest yesterday evening. Police detained two people. At the end of the afternoon a group of residents gathered around Sneeuwbalstraat. Fireworks were set off and small fires were started on the road and in underground waste containers. Later in the evening the mood turned and became more menacing. Stones and glass bottles were thrown at police. The ME was called in to restore order. A 39-year-old man has been arrested on suspicion of throwing fireworks at police officers. A 14-year-old boy has been picked up for public violence. Bonfire The cause of the unrest is a letter from mayor <entity id="person:femke-halsema">Femke Halsema</entity>. In it, a smaller-scale alternative to the annual bonfire on New Year's Eve was rejected, AT5 writes. Residents had come up with an alternative to their traditional bonfire, which was banned last year because of safety risks. The neighbourhood proposed lighting a smaller fire in an open container, but according to the fire brigade an open fire in a residential area is still too dangerous. Halsema has adopted the fire brigade's advice. Since this decision there has been unrest in the neighbourhood several times. Last week there were disturbances and the ME had to be deployed several times. According to Het Parool, a death in the neighbourhood also plays a role in the unrest. Youth workers There have already been several arrests, including of minors. Last Saturday a 22-year-old Amsterdammer was sentenced to 40 hours of community service. The man was arrested that Wednesday evening after, among other things, throwing a garden table belonging to a neighbourhood resident into a fire. Two minors were referred to Halt. Police say that residents are worried about the unrest and that "a great deal has been invested in the neighbourhood to make contact". For example, police are present with (neighbourhood) officers and youth workers. Police advise residents to contact the neighbourhood officers or the non-emergency police number. Tensions around the annual bonfire have been present in the neighbourhood for longer. At the end of 2025 there was also unrest in Floradorp after the annual bonfire was officially banned. Then too, fires were set repeatedly and the ME had to intervene.

title: At least 14 dead in landslide at illegal gold mine in Colombia
lead: At least fourteen people have died in a landslide at an illegal gold mine in a remote area of Colombia, local authorities report. Seven people were injured. Rescue services are still searching for missing people trapped under the rubble. The accident happened yesterday morning at around 08.00 local time in the department of Nariño, in the southwest of Colombia. At that time, thirty people were working in the gold mine, a Colombian media outlet writes. How do landslides occur? Landslides like this one are often caused by heavy rainfall. Because of the rain, the ground becomes heavier and less stable. The construction of (illegal) gold mines can worsen the consequences. When mines are built, a lot of deep digging is done. As a result, the soil becomes even more vulnerable to landslides. Illegal mines are not regulated, and no precautions are taken to prevent collapse. In bad weather the miners are then especially vulnerable. Rescue workers have difficulty reaching the site. Santa Bárbara de Iscuandé is surrounded by rainforest and can only be reached by boat or small plane. "At this moment our priority is to save lives, to support the families and to ensure an adequate response to this painful tragedy," writes Luis Alfonso Escobar, governor of Nariño. 'Protecting lives' Mining accidents occur more often in Colombia, especially in illegal mines. In the department of Nariño, on the border with Ecuador, a lot of illegal mining takes place and various armed groups are active, including dissidents of the former guerrilla movement FARC. They profit from that mining, among other things. In a statement, the Colombian ombudsman called on armed groups in the area to allow humanitarian aid passage to the affected area. "All of our efforts must be aimed at protecting lives and addressing this emergency." In August, thirteen miners died in a similar mining accident in Policarpa, also in Nariño.

title: Apu character returns to The Simpsons with Indian-American voice actor
lead: After eight years of silence, Apu is speaking again in the popular American animated series The Simpsons . The beloved Indian supermarket manager had no lines for years after strong criticism arose about the stereotypical way the character was portrayed. His voice is now provided by Indian-American voice actor Sunil Malhotra, and no longer by a white actor. The cartoon character Apu Nahasapeemapetilon works in The Simpsons , a series that is now almost forty years old, as manager of the Kwik-E-Mart supermarket in the fictional town of Springfield. There he regularly dealt with the antics of regular customer Homer Simpson, and they had numerous adventures together, including a trip to the Himalayas. Pop culture There had long been discussion about Apu. The character had a thick, exaggerated Indian accent and was voiced by white American actor and comedian Hank Azaria. Critics felt he was portrayed as too stereotypical and discriminatory. That criticism gained wide attention through The Problem with Apu from 2017, a documentary that criticises the way South Asian people are depicted in pop culture. After the death of George Floyd in 2020, attention to representation and diversity in Hollywood increased further. The makers of The Simpsons also came under pressure as a result. Azaria, who plays several characters in The Simpsons, then decided to stop as the voice of Apu. The last time Apu spoke was in an episode in October 2017. With Malhotra's arrival, the character now gets a voice again. This should contribute to a more representative image of the Indian character. This is how the new Apu sounds: Apu's wife Manjula has also received a new voice actress. She will now be voiced by Indian-American actress Janina Gavankar. Malhotra and Gavankar said on Instagram they were delighted with the news. "The return of Apu feels like a reclaiming. It really feels like his homecoming." The discussion around the stereotypical character of Apu was not a standalone matter. In 2020 the producers of The Simpsons announced that white actors would no longer voice non-white characters. Other characters then also got a new voice actor who better fits the character's background.

title: Australian hairdresser intervenes after attack on MP, prime minister calls him a hero
lead: A hairdresser in Australia is being praised for his quick response after a member of parliament was run down outside her office. Ricky Jefferies, owner of hair salon Ricky Chops, overpowered the driver who is suspected of deliberately driving into her. Jefferies had just finished cutting the hair of a young family when he heard a loud bang outside. When he looked outside, he saw that the driver of a Toyota LandCruiser had hit MP Helen Haines. She was seriously injured. "It was bizarre. I ran outside immediately to see what was going on", he told reporters. Ricky Chops is next to Haines's party office, in the city of Wangaratta in the state of Victoria, about three hours' drive northeast of Melbourne. Boot Jefferies took a knife from the suspect's pocket and pulled the suspect out of the car. He then restrained the man until police arrived. Australian Prime Minister Albanese has praised Jefferies' quick action and calls him a hero. The collision took place yesterday. The 65-year-old parliamentarian Haines was hit at her office. She was standing at the boot of her car when a driver drove into her. She reportedly became trapped between two cars. A 43-year-old man was arrested shortly afterwards. According to The Guardian Australia, he is an environmental activist who for years campaigned against logging in the northeast of the state of Victoria. Nothing is yet known about a motive. The suspect's father and stepmother have issued a statement saying they have been friends with the victim for more than twenty years. The statement does not say to what extent the suspect knew her as well. They call the incident "devastating and incomprehensible". Because anti-terror authorities are also involved in the case, there is fear that it is political violence. Such incidents are rare in Australia. Amputated Haines was taken to a hospital in Melbourne by trauma helicopter after the collision, where she was operated on last night. Her condition remains critical. According to the Australian broadcaster ABC, one of her legs had to be amputated. According to Prime Minister Albanese, preliminary investigation indicates that the driver made a U-turn before driving into Haines. Albanese speaks of an attack on the parliamentarian. Flowers have been laid at the spot where Haines was hit. Silver lining "In this dark and difficult time, it is a silver lining that a bystander rushed to help Helen in Wangaratta. In doing so, he possibly also put himself in danger. That person is a hero today", said Albanese on the programme Today of television channel Nine. In response, Jefferies says he does not see himself as a hero. "I was simply someone who had the chance to intervene in a way that was reasonably safe."

title: Wake-up call 20/10: Negotiations on Israel and Hezbollah • PSV plays FC Porto in CL
lead: Good morning! In Florida, Lebanon, Israel and the US are meeting to negotiate peace between Israel and Hezbollah, and PSV plays FC Porto in the Champions League. First the weather: today the day starts sunny everywhere. Later this afternoon clouds will increase in the south with a chance of rain. With a moderate to fairly strong south-easterly wind it will be 11 to 13 degrees. Are you going out today? Here you can find an overview of traffic jams and roadworks, and here everything about the situation on the rail network. What can you expect today? What did you miss? The night in France has, as far as is known, passed quietly. In several French cities a curfew was imposed after massive rioting and looting at the weekend. The measure applied to parts of the capital Paris, to the southern cities of Lyon and Nice, and to Lille in the north of France. In Paris the curfew applied between 23.00 and 06.00 in the centre, to the Place de la République and the streets around Les Halles, reports the French broadcaster BFMTV. The curfew there was in force for everyone; in other places young people specifically were not allowed on the street. Other news from the night: And then this too: Turnastar Sanne Wevers, 35, announced yesterday that she is putting an end to her career after missing out on a place in the final of the World Gymnastics Championships in Rotterdam. Wevers had previously indicated that this World Championship would probably be her last tournament. She wanted to close her career in her home country. Have a great day!

title: Presenter Christiane Amanpour leaves CNN after 43 years
lead: CNN presenter Christiane Amanpour is leaving the broadcaster after 43 years. In a farewell message she says she will stop with her programme Amanpour next May; from the beginning of next year the daily broadcasts will already be scaled back to once a week. Amanpour (68) started in 1983 as an assistant at the news channel, which had been founded three years earlier. Although her boss initially told her that she was not cut out to become a correspondent, she grew into one of the best-known faces of CNN. She rose from reporter to international correspondent. Over the years she was sent to various international conflicts, such as the civil war in Bosnia, the genocide in Rwanda and the conflicts in Afghanistan and Ukraine. She herself said that her mixed British-Iranian background gave her the unique opportunity to explain diverse perspectives well. Without giving a reason Amanpour remains silent about why she is now taking a step back. "After many months of thinking and many sleepless nights, I have decided to say goodbye to CNN, my partner in 43 fantastic years," she writes in a farewell message. "I will always keep rooting for CNN and its independent journalism. Remember: always the truth, never neutral." The departure comes at a time when CNN is getting a new owner, the media conglomerate Skydance. Its subsidiary Paramount recently received permission to take over Warner Bros. This brings the broadcaster CBS under the same umbrella.

title: Left-wing coalition on the way in Berlin, Merz wants to derail coalition talks
lead: Berlin is all but certain to get a very left-wing government. Election winner Die Linke reached a preliminary agreement this weekend with the Greens and the SPD. The leaders of those parties gave the green light last night to the plans, which include expropriating large property companies. This clears the way for Elif Eralp to become mayor of Berlin, as the first woman with a migrant background and indeed the first Linke politician to hold that office. Resistance to a left-wing city government is strong. Among others, Chancellor Merz wants to prevent a left-wing government in Berlin. Antisemitism Die Linke are under heavy fire over accusations of antisemitism. This mainly concerns criticism of Israel, which many German parties equate with hatred of Jews. "Jews are no longer safe in Berlin if Eralp becomes mayor," says the CDU Minister of Education, Karin Prien, who is Jewish and grew up in the Netherlands. Eralp knows how harmful even the suspicion of antisemitism is. She therefore repeatedly says that she will protect the lives of Jewish Berliners. Radical members, such as Hannah Bruns, who refuses to condemn Hamas's attacks of 7 October 2023 and denies Israel's right to exist, are being expelled from the party. The parties forming a government in Berlin have signed a statement recognising Israel's right to exist. This has caused division within Die Linke. "States have no right to exist, people do," said parliamentarian Vanessa Emde. The party leadership decides today whether she will be expelled from the party. In addition, Die Linke are under attack over alleged contacts with organised crime in Berlin. Members of the notorious Remmo clan were at the Linke election party in the Neukölln district but were sent away during the evening. A Bundestag member from that district sent friendly chats to a Remmo member. This politician has also been sidelined. "Nie wieder ist jetzt" It is a balancing act for Eralp, because Die Linke won the election partly thanks to their pro-Palestinian stance. The socialist party is, however, willing to compromise on this point in order to secure the most important dossier: a radical turnaround in housing policy. That seems to be succeeding. The three parties have agreed to expropriate the five largest property companies. With a loan of up to 16 billion euros, 160,000 homes must be brought into state hands to stop rent increases. Smaller landlords also face stricter rules. The CDU/CSU, supported by right-wing media such as Bild and Welt, is doing everything it can to prevent a left-wing government. CSU leader Söder speaks of a return of communism and, like other state premiers, wants to stop funding Berlin. The CDU youth are campaigning with 'Nie wieder ist jetzt', a slogan usually used against the AfD. The parties are mainly putting pressure on the SPD and the Greens not to cooperate with Die Linke. Chancellor Merz called on the SPD last week to come to their senses immediately. "Stop this," he repeated this weekend. Such interference by the chancellor in a local coalition is considered a no-go, as is putting one's own coalition partner under such pressure. Criticism within the national SPD is also growing. At least twenty Bundestag members have declared in a statement that they oppose the Berlin coalition. Parliamentary group leader Miersch says he has "considerable doubts" about Die Linke. Among the Greens too, some prominent figures are turning against cooperation with the Berlin Linke. Others criticise precisely the fact that the CDU is so categorical about this, while it increasingly works with the far-right AfD at local level. For example, in Heidenau the CDU and AfD recently voted for a ban on Stolpersteine, memorial stones for the Holocaust. Several CDU members also most likely voted for an AfD member as parliamentary chair in Saxony-Anhalt. Blueprint More is at stake for the CDU/CSU. A successful coalition of Linke, Greens and SPD could serve as a blueprint for a future national <entity id="org:regering">regering</entity>. As the CDU/CSU declines in the polls, such a left-wing option is increasingly in view. In Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, the popular SPD politician Manuela Schwesig is already forming a similar left-wing coalition. She is regarded as the future SPD leader and chancellor candidate. The Berlin coalition thus puts extra pressure on the national coalition, which is already struggling with internal tensions and mistrust. At the same time, there is no stable alternative in Berlin. A coalition of CDU, Greens and SPD does have a narrow majority, but left-wing Green politicians rule this option out. If the federal government fails to prevent a left-wing government in the capital, it can actively obstruct the state government. Federal legislation could, for example, ban the expropriation plan, as well as the planned more generous asylum legislation. A long conflict between the capital and the federal government is looming.

title: Curfew in French cities: empty streets, but lots of police on the move
lead: In France, it remained quiet last night, French media report. In several cities a curfew was in force after riots broke out at the weekend during protests against government policy and rising costs of living. In Paris, Lille, Lyon, Nice and Bordeaux, among others, minors were not allowed on the street in certain areas last evening and overnight. Prime Minister Lecornu says on X that the measure contributed to keeping the peace last night. The curfew is therefore also in force again tonight in places where the local authorities deem it necessary. He also expressed his thanks to the police and local authorities for their efforts. Police present in large numbers on the street In Paris, the measure in the centre applied to the Place de la République and the streets around Les Halles, not only to young people but to everyone. Footage shows that the police were present in large numbers on the street and that the order was well observed. In Lyon it was briefly restless last evening when, before the curfew took effect, a gathering was held of people wanting to show their solidarity with the shop owners and riot police affected by rioting youths. A far-right group joined that gathering and then marched through the city centre until they encountered the riot police and dispersed. In Bordeaux the curfew applies until 26 October in neighbourhoods that were hard hit by the looting of 17 October. In Lille the curfew remains in force tonight as well. The ban on going out also applies in surrounding municipalities such as Douai, Wattignies and Denain.

title: Former police Porsche of collector from Borne auctioned for over 200,000 euros
lead: A car collector from Borne sold his <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>-Porsche at an auction yesterday. The 1979 Porsche 911 from the former Rijkspolitie went to a new owner for over 200,000 euros. "A nice result, and the new owner will soon have a very special car," the seller tells RTV Oost anonymously. The Dutch Rijkspolitie used various Porsche models as patrol cars from 1962 to 1996. The 911 Targa was not only fast and conspicuous on Dutch motorways, but thanks to its open roof officers could stand up in the car to warn other road users with hand signals. Stripped Although the police had hundreds of Porsches in use over the years, few remained in original condition. Most were stripped and then resold as 'ordinary' cars. One original example went to a collector from Borne. Due to his health he could no longer make much use of it, so he wanted to make someone else happy with it, he says. According to the regional broadcaster there was a lot of interest, and bids kept coming in until a second before closing. The winner of the auction paid 202,000 euros for the car. Auction costs of 6,000 euros come on top of that. The seller is satisfied with the result. "The previous police Porsche to be auctioned brought in 250,000 US dollars. At the time that was a record for the American market. As far as I have been able to establish, this is a record for the European market." No minimum bid The seller took a gamble by not setting a minimum bid, so there was no lower limit. This is a popular tactic for auction houses, but a risk for the seller. It paid off for the collector. "The difficult thing with cars like this is that they never come up for sale. Because you have no frame of reference, you have no idea what to expect. But in the end it has been a nice result." Who the new owner is has not been disclosed. "I'll only hear that later. The protocol is that the money must be credited within a week. After that the transfer takes place. And then I hope to also hear who the new owner is." The anonymous collector looks back on fond memories with the car: "I did a lot of nice things with it. Drove rallies, but also took rides with police officers who were retiring and had once driven it themselves. Those were sometimes very emotional outings."

title: Probe Idefix on its way to collect 10 grams of material from Martian moon
lead: A Japanese space mission has successfully started its journey to Mars's moon Phobos. The aim is to bring back about 10 grams of material from that moon to Earth. More than 500 million euros has been set aside for the international mission, named MMX (Martian Moons eXploration). On board the rocket are the exploration rover Idefix and a lander that is due to scoop up some soil in a few years. The mission is expected to reach Mars next summer. The rocket was launched in Japan: the Franco-German Idefix, a 25-kilogram rover the size of a microwave, named after Asterix's dog, will first land on the surface of Phobos. It will find a good spot where the mothership can eventually touch down for a few hours to drill and collect samples. That will only happen in 2028 or 2029. The return trip to Earth is due to be completed in 2031. Mars has two moons: the larger Phobos and the smaller Deimos. Apart from our own Moon, they are the only moons of the inner planets of our solar system. The moons are considerably smaller than ours: Phobos is only 20 kilometers across, Deimos about half that. Because of their small size they also have less gravity, so landing on the surface is no easy task. The aim of the mission is to find out how Mars's moons formed. Are they the result of an ancient collision with the planet that flung debris into space? Or are they asteroids that were pulled in by the planet's gravity? The characteristics of the material that is brought back should be able to answer that question. It would be the first time that material from (near) Mars has been returned to Earth. Earlier, the Apollo astronauts already collected rocks and dust from our own Moon, and NASA used a probe to collect a handful of dust from asteroid Bennu. Whether this will really be the first for this mission is still uncertain: China plans to launch a round trip to Mars in 2028, which would return in the same year as this mission. NASA has also collected Martian samples with the Perseverance rover, but there are no concrete plans yet to retrieve them.

title: Residents of Alberta vote against separation from Canada
lead: Residents of the Canadian province of Alberta have voted in a referendum against independence. Not all votes have been counted yet, but according to the Canadian broadcaster CBC it is already clear that more than three quarters of voters have chosen to stay in Canada. The outcome is a boost for Canadian prime minister Carney. During the campaign he called for national unity and pointed in particular to the dangers emanating from the United States. Canada needs stability because of the trade war and President Trump's wish to annex the country, Carney said. He has therefore responded with pleasure to the outcome of the referendum. "The people of Alberta have made a clear choice," he writes in a statement. "Canada is much greater than the sum of its parts." The premier of the province, Danielle Smith, is also against separation. She nevertheless called the referendum under pressure from separatist party colleagues. Oil-rich Alberta is by far the richest province of Canada. Traditionally, residents are critical of the national government in Ottawa, partly because they feel they pay relatively high taxes. Non-binding The referendum was not binding. Residents of Alberta were asked whether they want to stay with Canada or start a "process towards independence", in the form of a later referendum that would be binding. No more than 23 percent appears to have voted for the latter, CBC reports. It is not yet known what the turnout was.

title: PostNL asks again for extra money for mail delivery
lead: PostNL wants an extra allowance of 80 million euros for next year. The postal company says costs keep rising because fewer and fewer people and businesses send letters by post, but PostNL is legally obliged to deliver the post. "The costs arising from a legal obligation cannot be placed on the company. This uncertainty puts unacceptable pressure on the postal company and our employees. Moreover, it undermines the competitiveness and investment capacity of PostNL as a whole", says Maurice Unck, director of post at PostNL. The postal company also calls on <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> to introduce the new Postwet quickly. This law has been with <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> since 2020. At the moment PostNL must comply with rules from 2009. The postal market has changed enormously since then. According to PostNL, for example, the volume of post has fallen by 70 percent over the past 20 years. Earlier requests have been rejected. This is not the first time PostNL has asked the cabinet for money. It also submitted subsidy requests for this year and last year. The previous cabinet has always rejected this request, and a legal procedure is currently ongoing for these requests. PostNL states that in 2025, 2026 and 2027 it will lose 148 million in total because the company still has to comply with the outdated rules. Last July PostNL already adjusted the delivery time for post. Since then, letter mail has been delivered within two days instead of within one day. If the new Postwet is introduced, the postal company may take at most three days to deliver letters and cards. PostNL wants to scale back further and in future also stop delivering post on Saturdays.

title: Formula 1 and darts can definitively move from Viaplay to Videoland
lead: Videoland may take over all sports licences and subscribers of Viaplay Nederland. The regulator Autoriteit Consument & Markt (<entity id="org:zbo-autoriteit-consument-en-markt">ACM</entity>) approved the takeover this morning. This means sports such as Formula 1, English football, darts and hockey will soon be broadcast on Videoland. Approval from the ACM was needed for the takeover, because it had to be investigated whether Videoland would not become too large. That is not the case, the ACM ruled. For viewers and advertisers there would be no disadvantages, mainly because Videoland currently mainly broadcasts films, series and programmes. The sports rights being transferred are also temporary in nature, the ACM states. Viaplay Nederland was allowed to broadcast Formula 1 in the Netherlands until and including 2029. If this contract expires, other broadcasters may try to take over the licence. Not too large Scandinavian Viaplay has been in serious financial trouble for years. For that reason it is withdrawing from many countries. Videoland was always part of RTL Nederland. A little over a year ago, publisher DPG received permission from the ACM to take over RTL. The Belgian-origin DPG publishes newspapers in the Netherlands such as the AD, de Volkskrant, Trouw, Het Parool and various regional newspapers. The ACM does not expect that DPG will become too large in the advertising market with the sports rights and subscribers of Viaplay now. The number of viewers and advertisers at Viaplay was, according to the ACM, not large enough.

title: Zelensky speaks with Rubio about delay in Patriot deliveries, talks in Oslo
lead: Ukrainian president Zelensky has spoken with US Secretary of State Rubio about the delivery of crucial air defence missiles and the situation surrounding Starlink. Zelensky writes this on X. The conversation follows reports by the Kyiv Independent and the Washington Post, which write that US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth has not yet approved the delivery of Patriot interceptor missiles to Ukraine. "All of this points to a political decision having been made to slow down support for us," Zelensky responded. "We want to understand what is going on, why this is happening and where all this is leading." The delay in the crucial missiles comes amid increasing American pressure on Kyiv to make concessions to end the war. President Trump said yesterday at a press conference that "Russia, frankly, has positioned itself very well with regard to Ukraine" and that it "may be better for someone else to negotiate on behalf of Ukraine". Shortage of Patriots Since the summer, Ukraine has been struggling with a shortage of the important Patriot missiles. That makes the population vulnerable to ballistic missile attacks, powerful, fast missiles that are hard to defend against without the Patriots. Meanwhile Russia is stepping up attacks on Ukraine: the country wants to bring Ukraine to its knees this winter with attacks on the energy infrastructure. Ukraine fears that the US is withholding weapons to put pressure on the country. There were also reports last week that the Ukrainian army suddenly no longer received intelligence from the US and no longer had access to Starshield, the military branch of the American Starlink satellite network. That system is essential for the military communications of the top of the Ukrainian army. Yesterday Ukrainian president Zelensky asked a group of American senators during a virtual meeting to increase pressure on Trump. The group of politicians consisted of both Republicans and Democrats who support Ukraine. Republican Thom Tillis said afterwards that Congress "remains convinced that it must support Ukraine and our European allies to end Russia's brutal aggression and achieve a lasting peace". Talks in Oslo Today there is a meeting in Oslo with Zelensky and special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, Trump's son-in-law. Norwegian prime minister Jonas Gahr Støre and Finnish president Alexander Stubb are also involved in the meeting. Stubb said that "Russia's illegal war of aggression against Ukraine and the general security situation in Europe" will be discussed. Later today Zelensky, Stubb and Støre will hold a press conference. Meanwhile the attacks in Ukraine continue unabated. In a Russian drone attack on a park in Kharkiv last night, six people were killed, including two children. Fifteen others were injured, including seven children. According to local authorities, it is most likely a Russian jet-powered drone.

title: Amsterdam school does not have to let pupil move up, court rules
lead: A pupil at Fons Vitae Lyceum in Amsterdam does not have to move up to the second year of havo. The court ruled this in a case brought by the boy's mother. According to the mother, the school should have offered him more support, but the court does not go along with that. Last school year, according to the school, the first-year pupil's results were not sufficient to move up to the second year. Because Fons Vitae Lyceum does not have a vmbo department, the boy had to go to another school. His mother wanted to put a stop to that through the court. The boy mostly speaks English at home and Dutch is not his mother tongue. The school admitted him while that information was known, she said. 'Careful and understandable' According to the mother, insufficient help was provided to help the boy with his language delay. In addition, she argued that he had a difficult year mentally. All of this would have led to his results lagging behind. The court sees it differently: the school has sufficiently substantiated why the boy could not move up to 2 havo, city broadcaster AT5 writes. Teachers looked not only at grades, but also at work pace, demonstrated understanding of the course material and the speed with which new course material was acquired. The pupil was also, according to the court, sufficiently supported with his language delay. 'A careful and understandable assessment was made', the ruling states. On the school It is always up to a school to decide whether a pupil does or does not move up. The court can only intervene if the decision is manifestly incorrect or incomprehensible, or if the decision was taken carelessly. It is not yet known whether the mother will appeal the ruling.

title: 160 dead in drone attacks in Sudan, including in relatively safe Khartoum
lead: In a wave of drone attacks in Sudan in recent days, more than 160 people have died according to medical staff and human rights organizations. Deaths also occurred in the capital Khartoum. There, three children died in a drone attack by the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF). In Khartoum, it had recently been relatively safe and there were not often drone attacks. The city is in the hands of the government army and the front line is quite far away. But the RSF has drones that can cover long distances. Most of the fatal casualties fell in the city of Abyei in southwestern Sudan. At least 80 people lost their lives there when a drone hit a traffic junction. People were waiting there for transport home after going to the market. At least 19 people were also injured. This attack is attributed to the government because it took place in an area controlled by the RSF. More deadly and unpredictable. In Sudan, the government army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) have been fighting each other for well over three years. The civil war broke out after the leaders of both parties jointly carried out a coup and afterwards failed to agree on the division of power. With the arrival of drones, the attacks have become deadlier and more unpredictable. Drones are used in many ways. To attack infrastructure, for example, water and electricity plants, dams. But many civilian targets are also hit, such as refugee camps. According to a recent report from the United Nations, about 1,000 people in Sudan have lost their lives in drone attacks in the first five months of this year. Entire lives disrupted. The two parties obtain the drones from abroad. The government army's come from Iran and Turkey, and according to Sudanese media recently also from Pakistan. The paramilitaries use Chinese drones that reportedly enter the country via smuggling routes through the United Arab Emirates. The arrival of drones means for the population of Sudan that their entire lives are disrupted. On the front line where most drones are deployed, people have sometimes dug their own bunkers next to their homes, they also have to constantly flee and lose their shelter. People sometimes no longer dare to go to the market or to their land to farm it. And this has already lasted 3.5 years.

title: NS train tickets once again much more expensive, an increase of 4.7 percent on average
lead: Next year, travelling by train will once again become a good deal more expensive. On average, the price of a train ticket at NS will rise by 4.7 percent. "The revenue from train tickets is needed to purchase new comfortable trains, to pay the increased costs and to keep investing in good facilities," says Daan Schut, who is responsible for fares on the NS executive board. Travelling during off-peak hours will, however, become cheaper. Travellers can get up to 80 percent discount instead of 60 percent on a train ticket with so-called PrijsTijd Deals, NS reports. Later next year, these train tickets will become available on the day itself. Currently, travellers still have to book at least one day in advance. The railway operator also wants to talk with the government about an "possible follow-up" to the summer subscription, with which travellers could travel unlimited during off-peak hours and weekends in the summer months for 49 euros per month. Railrunner The prices of not all products are going up. For example, the price of a Railrunner, with which children can travel unlimited for 2.50 euros, remains the same. The Kids Vrij subscription, with which children up to and including 11 years old travel free, and the Dal Voordeel subscription for young people between 12 and 17 years old, also remain free. Prices have been rising for years This year, train ticket prices rose by 6.52 percent on average, about the same as in 2025. The year before, in 2024, prices did not go up thanks to government compensation (120 million euros). Last year, NS made a profit for the first time in years. More people took the train, allowing the rail operator to return to the black with a net profit of 380 million euros. NS still had a loss of 141 million euros in 2024. NS struggled for years with disappointing results. After the coronavirus pandemic, not all train travellers returned, because of the widespread working from home. Costs also rose faster than revenues. Among other things, wages and the costs of rolling stock went up. Subscription holders The traveller organisation Rover is enthusiastic about the discount deals with which travellers can now get up to 80 percent off. Rover is also pleased that NS is adopting its advice to offer these tickets with substantial discounts on the day of departure as well. This is mainly good news for travellers who only take the train now and then, says Rover director Daan Zieren. "People very often decide only on the day itself when they travel from A to B. If there is still enough room on a quiet train at that moment, it makes sense to reward that traveller with a cheaper fare as well." But Rover is annoyed that subscription holders cannot benefit from these large discounts, even though they have been facing higher costs for years. Inflation The new ticket prices that apply from 2027 include, among other things, a previously agreed so-called catch-up indexation for inflation in the years 2020 to 2023. At the time, tariffs rose less than inflation. For example, inflation over the whole of 2022 was set at 10 percent, while the price of a train ticket rose by 1.8 percent on average. The traveller organisation is not happy about the so-called catch-up indexation. "Now that NS is finally seeing growth in travellers again, the traveller is once again being punished with a large fare increase," says Rover director Zieren. "By consistently making maximum use of the room NS is given to raise fares, the company itself is holding back further growth in travellers."

title: Cyclist falls into sewer hole on street in Eindhoven
lead: A cyclist fell into a concrete hole on the street in Eindhoven this morning. Sewer work is being carried out on the street. The road was therefore cordoned off with signs. The woman was brought out of the hole by emergency services and taken to hospital with unknown injuries. How she is doing now is unknown. Signs: The road is closed to traffic for several weeks due to the works. Motorists currently cannot drive through the street. According to Omroep Brabant, however, dozens of cyclists ignore the signs and cycle across the street or via the cycle path around the opened holes. According to the broadcaster, the holes had previously been cordoned off with extra construction fencing. That fencing had just been removed because the street is being closed again today. The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> and municipality are investigating the accident. Hole under container: Yesterday a man fell into a hole several metres deep under an underground container in Den Bosch. The elderly man was injured in the process. It is not known how he is doing now.

title: Gas storage 64 percent full, minimum target reached
lead: The Netherlands has reached the minimum target for gas to get through the winter. State-owned company Energiebeheer Nederland (<entity id="org:zbo-economie-bedrijven-en-nationale-rekeningen">EBN</entity>) reports that the gas storage is 64 percent full. This means the Netherlands meets the minimum European requirement. Two months ago, EBN was asked by the ministry of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-economische-zaken-en-klimaat">Economische Zaken en Klimaat</entity> to help replenish the gas supply. Normally this is done by commercial energy companies in the summer, when the gas price is low. But because of the war in the Middle East, gas prices had risen to record highs. The Netherlands wanted the gas storage to be 80 percent full this winter. But in August it turned out that this was no longer achievable with a fill level of 45 percent. Therefore the target was lowered to the 64 percent requirement that the European Union imposes on member states. Presumably filling the storage will continue. Gasunie reports today that the supply has already risen to 65.5 percent.

title: Man arrested for fire at Limoges town hall, known to French police
lead: In France a man has been arrested on suspicion of setting fire to the town hall of Limoges last Saturday. French media report, based on a source close to the investigation, that he is on a list of the French security service because of ties to a left-wing extremist movement. The man is known to the police because he has committed violence against officers in the past. According to some French media the man is 34 years old, while other media write that he is 40. Disturbances: Protests against the high cost of living led to major disturbances in many places in France last weekend. Violence also broke out in the Limoges city centre. Some rioters entered the town hall and set it on fire. A bell tower listed as a monument collapsed as a result. The French anti-terrorism unit is investigating the fire at the town hall.

title: Pro councillor must retract statements about amusement park owner Wim Beelen
lead: Rotterdam Pro councillor Kevin van Eikeren must retract several statements about entrepreneur Wim Beelen. The court in <entity id="org:gemeente-s-gravenhage">Den Haag</entity> has ruled so. Van Eikeren called Beelen, among other things, a 'proleet' and a 'patjepeeër'. Multimillionaire Beelen, known among other things from the Rotterdam amusement park Spelen bij Beelen, then brought a case. Van Eikeren had said on radio at the regional broadcaster Rijnmond, among other things, that Beelen with his amusement park "plays the good Samaritan" while it is "purely about the money". In addition, Van Eikeren said that Beelen tried to buy political parties in <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">Amsterdam</entity> by making high donations. Within 72 hours, the councillor must, according to the judge, post a message on Instagram and LinkedIn acknowledging that his statements were unlawful. 1850 euros: Beelen had sued the councillor because the statements would damage his reputation and business contacts. The court considers that the Pro councillor has insufficiently substantiated that Beelen would be a speculator. In the judge's view, Van Eikeren presented personal opinions as facts. Because Beelen has been found right, Van Eikeren must pay the costs of the proceedings. These amount to more than 1850 euros. During the hearing in the summary proceedings, earlier this month, the judge still expressed the hope that the men could sort things out between themselves, but that did not succeed. The judge has therefore now delivered a ruling. Penalty payment: Beelen also demanded that Van Eikeren refrain from similar comments in the future. For each violation he wanted a penalty payment of 17,500 euros to be imposed. The court does not go along with this. Entrepreneur and millionaire Wim Beelen took over the struggling amusement park Rivoli in <entity id="org:gemeente-rotterdam">Rotterdam</entity>-Zuid from Hennie van der Most. The park was first called Spelen bij Beelen, but has since been renamed Zuidyard.

title: Churches join forces to temporarily house status holders
lead: The combined churches have started an action to temporarily take in refugees. They call on local churches and parishes to offer status holders accommodation in, for example, an annex of the church or an empty parsonage. Actie Onderdak is an initiative of the Raad van Kerken in Nederland. Nineteen Christian churches and organisations are affiliated with it, including the Roman Catholic Church, the Protestant PKN and the Reformed NGK. The Raad van Kerken speaks of "an interchurch action in the full breadth". The action focuses on status holders. They do have a residence permit, but they often do not get a home in the municipality assigned to them. That is partly due to the stagnant housing market. As a result, status holders are forced to live in an asylum seekers' centre for longer, which in turn leads to a shortage of places for new asylum seekers. According to the Raad van Kerken, the initiative is therefore intended to create room for people who are newly arriving at azc's. Accommodation for three months All local church councils and parish boards received a letter today. It asks whether they can offer a place for a period of three months to families with status holders who are waiting for housing in the place concerned. Five churches announced today that they want to join the action. The idea is that the status holders get to know their new surroundings in advance, says the Raad van Kerken. According to the council, it arose "out of hospitality, mercy and solidarity". 'Minister is enthusiastic' The Raad van Kerken says it discussed the plan with asylum minister Van den Brink. According to the council, he gives the plan "a warm heart". The plan was developed in cooperation with the ministry and the <entity id="org:zbo-centraal-orgaan-opvang-asielzoekers">Centraal Orgaan opvang asielzoekers</entity> (COA). According to the council, the COA ensures that status holders can move on to a new place after three months.

title: Gerard Joling leaves after 21 years at De Toppers: 'I enjoyed it'
lead: Gerard Joling is stopping after more than 21 years of performances with De Toppers in Concert. The singer announced this on Instagram. According to the singer, it feels like "the right decision". The 66-year-old artist says he will focus on his television work and his own performances. According to Joling, it has not been an easy decision. "I am incredibly proud and grateful that I was able to do this for years. It will probably never happen to me again that I stand in such a big arena, but I have enjoyed it." The De Toppers concerts in the Johan Cruyff Arena in Amsterdam are sold out every year. The idea arose when René Froger brought his colleagues Gordon and Gerard Joling onto the stage during a performance. That was remarkable, because Gordon and Joling had a feud, which they fought out publicly. Autoimmune disease In 2005 the first official edition of De Toppers in Concert followed, in which Gordon, Joling and Froger stood in the Arena for two days in a row. The group's lineup has changed here and there over the past years, but since 2017 the formation has consisted of Jeroen van der Boom, René Froger, Gerard Joling and Jan Smit. Founder Froger has always been part of it. Froger recently announced that he suffers from an autoimmune disease, for which he is being treated. It is not yet known whether Froger's illness will affect the upcoming concert series of the Toppers next May. The lineup of the Toppers through 2025 : The organisation behind the group reports that "hard work" is currently being done behind the scenes on the "artistic and musical content" of the concert series in May. Who will succeed Joling will be announced soon. "We will reveal the brand-new Toppers lineup very shortly", said the organisation. What do you think of the NOS app and website? What do we do well? What could be better? We are curious about your opinion. Fill in the survey via this link .

title: British fighter jets to Saudi Arabia to fight the Houthis
lead: The British Air Force will protect Saudi airspace against attacks by the Houthis. The country is sending, among other things, a number of Typhoon fighter jets to Saudi Arabia. According to the Ministry of Defence, it is a mission with a defensive purpose: the fighter jets will not carry out any attacks. The support follows a request from the Saudi government. Besides combat aircraft, the British are also sending a transport aircraft and an unknown number of military advisers to Saudi Arabia. The aim is for Houthi attacks from neighbouring Yemen on infrastructure and cities to be repelled. Situation escalated Saudi Arabia supports the internationally recognised government in Yemen and is therefore being attacked by the Yemeni Houthi fighters. Recently the Houthis have stepped up the violence, by their own account as retaliation for attacks on Houthi targets in Yemen. In an attack yesterday on a military camp in southern Yemen, 73 people were killed. That makes it the deadliest attack since the recent escalation in the country. The victims are all new recruits aged between 18 and 20. Among other things, airports in Saudi Arabia and power plants were targeted by the Houthis this month, with deaths as a result. Those recent attacks from Yemen prove that the British mission is necessary, says Defence Minister Streeting. "This shows that the Houthis are letting the situation escalate in the region." 'Intervention also useful for the British' Streeting points out that an escalation of violence in the oil-rich Middle East can also have consequences for the United Kingdom. "It drives up the cost of living, disrupts the energy supply and causes higher costs for British businesses." The United Kingdom has for some time been giving Saudi Arabia defensive support in the fight against the Houthis. For example, Saudi combat aircraft can use British tanker aircraft to refuel in the air. That support has been extended by ninety days, effective from today. What do you think of the NOS app and website? What do we do well? What could be better? We are curious about your opinion. Fill in the survey via this link .

title: Podcast De Dag: what is now wise for President Zelensky?
lead: Relations between U.S. President Trump and Ukrainian President Zelensky have reached a new low, and U.S. support for Ukraine in the war is crumbling fast. After the diesel deal with Putin last week, Trump scrapped a large sanctions package against Russia this weekend, and meanwhile the Starlink system is working at half capacity. Listening? You can listen to this episode of De Dag via NPO Luister and all other podcast apps. Like it? Don't forget to subscribe. What is now wise for President Zelensky, who is also increasingly openly distancing himself from Trump? Bob Deen, Eastern Europe expert and director of the Clingendael Institute, gives his analysis in the podcast. Reactions? Email dedag@nos.nl Presentation and editing: Elisabeth Steinz Editorial: IJsbrand Terpstra Final editing: Judith van de Hulsbeek

title: In a Zeeland village, residents have been waiting for weeks for mail, and three postal carriers have quit
lead: Residents of the Zeeland village of Rilland have been complaining for weeks about mail delivery in their village. Some have not had a letter in their letterbox for three weeks, while others are only receiving the wrong mail. PostNL recognises the problems and is working on a solution. For some, mainly older residents of the village, it is a difficult situation. A woman who had her car repaired in North Brabant received the bill but not in her letterbox. She then drove to Bergen op Zoom to pay in person. "Those people also want their money. I don't know how much longer it will take before I get post", the woman tells Omroep Zeeland. Another resident mainly misses her TV guide and the Libelle. "You pay for all of that", the woman says. Some are worried. "Is my post with other people? Is it somewhere in a depot? I don't know anything at all", says another. Three postal carriers gone. Since July of this year, PostNL has delivered letterbox mail within two working days, instead of the next working day. Therefore, many smaller depots across the country have been merged or closed. The local depot in Rilland also disappeared, so the three regular carriers in the village now have to go to the depot in the more distant Krabbendijke to collect the post. According to Omroep Zeeland, that means about 20 minutes of extra cycling there and back with heavy post on an ordinary bicycle. The carriers would also not be entitled to an electric bicycle because the distances are too short for that. As a result, all three regular carriers stopped working in Rilland at the same time, the broadcaster writes. A PostNL spokesperson cannot comment on the personal situation of the three carriers, but says, among other things: "Extra travel time during the delivery route, for example to pick up extra mail bags, is working time and is compensated". 'Not as it should be' The spokesperson acknowledges that signals are indeed coming in about the poor mail delivery in Rilland. "That is unpleasant for the residents involved and not as it should be." PostNL promises improvement and says extra checks are being carried out. Another carrier is also being deployed. "We are staying on top of this and paying extra attention to delivery, so that it runs smoothly again and according to plan."

title: Maastricht student from Gaza did not say 'This is me' in video
lead: The student at Maastricht University who was previously thought to have acknowledged involvement in the Hamas attacks of 7 October 2023 in a video turns out to have been misquoted. In the Instagram video he appears to say " This is me ", pointing at masked jihadists on a television. The NOS now establishes that in the video he speaks Arabic, not English, and also that he does not acknowledge any involvement. Many media reported at the end of September that the student had been suspended by Maastricht University. The trigger was a video, since removed from Instagram, in which the NOS also reported the words " This is me " could be heard. The student points at images from news channel Al Jazeera on television, gives a thumbs up and speaks to someone sitting next to him on the couch. Arabic dialect Anthropologist and Arabic translator Rahma Bavelaar was the first to report, in early October via the Limburg broadcaster L1, that she hears Arabic in the footage, not English. The student would not be saying " This is me ", but " tasheshni ", which according to her means in a local dialect something like 'take me outside'. According to Bavelaar, it is a specific Arabic dialect spoken among others in Gaza. Further study of the footage also led the NOS to conclude that the student does not speak English in the video. Sources in Gaza, who speak the Gazan dialect, have no doubt. They hear Arabic, not " This is me ". And therefore no acknowledgement by the student that he was involved with Hamas or the attacks of 7 October 2023. Partly because of the poor sound quality, it remains difficult for Arabic speakers with whom the NOS watched the footage to determine what the student does say. According to the European Legal Support Center, which represents the student, the student himself categorically denies saying " This is me ". He does, he says, indeed use the Arabic word " tasheshni ", an expression which he says is widely used locally. Security check The video was picked up by media after the Centre for Information and Documentation Israel (CIDI) shared the student's Instagram video. CIDI advocates for the interests of Israel and the Jewish community. On X the organisation expressed concerns about the security checks students undergo when coming to the Netherlands to study. CIDI wrote that the student glorifies terrorism in the video. After a conversation with the student, Maastricht University lifted the suspension and spoke of a misunderstanding. The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> also concluded after investigation in early October that there is no reason to assume the student was involved in the attacks of 7 October. Parliamentary questions MPs from the Groep Markuszower asked parliamentary questions about the student's presence in the Netherlands. In reply, Minister Van den Brink of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-am">Asiel en Migratie</entity> referred to the opinion of the Public Prosecution Service. The student came to the Netherlands in June this year as a member of a group of 47 Palestinians who were able to leave Gaza for the Netherlands with a work or study visa. To make this journey, Gazans must also travel through Israel and have Israel's permission to cross the Gaza border. Israel carries out heavy security checks before Gazans receive this permission.

title: Indonesia is choking in smoke from huge wildfires, and the fire could last for months
lead: A thick layer of toxic smoke hangs over western Indonesia. On social media, residents of Palangkaraya, in Kalimantan, share images of their city wrapped in an orange blanket. People on the street wear face masks, and a few walk around with a gas mask. Nearly 2 million hectares of nature have already gone up in flames in Indonesia this year. The fires started in June, are incredibly large, and the smoke clouds are turning a considerable part of Southeast Asia 'blue'. Emergency services have been trying for months to tame the flames, but without success. Only the monsoon rains can still put out the wildfires, and that may take a while. 'We think it will stay dry for a few more weeks,' says professor of wildfires Guido van der Werf of Wageningen University. Somewhere in November or perhaps only in December it will start raining hard, he thinks. 'Then it will stop too. The peat fires will smoulder on for a few more weeks, but then the large-scale burning will stop.' The current fires in Indonesia have everything to do with El Niño. Because of this weather phenomenon the trade winds change, which normally blow from east to west across the equator. That has major consequences for rainfall in Indonesia. This year there is a historically severe El Niño, fairly comparable to or even stronger than that of 1997-1998. 'Normally the air comes from the Pacific Ocean towards Indonesia. So it is fairly humid,' Van der Werf continues. 'That is why it rains a lot in Indonesia. During El Niño that trade wind actually stops. That means this humid air is no longer brought in, and therefore it stays very dry in Indonesia for a long time.' That drought offers ideal conditions for huge fires. Fires are common in Indonesia around this time of year. Farmers burn patches of land bare to clear the ground for agriculture. Originally a traditional way of land management for small farmers. Only now that it is so dry, the fires spread to, for example, the neighbouring forest. The raging fires can no longer be controlled. Van der Werf: 'You have tropical forest. People want to get rid of it, and the cheapest way is to set it on fire. We see fire as a danger, but for them fire is a means of deforestation.' At the same time, the farmers also see that the consequences are very great. 'Those farmers are caught in a double bind. On the one hand they need it as a means to deforest. On the other hand they also see how the population suffers because of it.' Not only farmers use fire. Slash-and-burn, as it is called, is also widely used by large palm oil companies to clear land for new plantations. It is officially banned, but enforcement is lacking. Toxic blanket: The fires are a problem, and the smoke they produce is just as big a problem. Air traffic is disrupted, schools are closed, and in Makassar hundreds of students took to the streets because they want the government to do more. It is not only in Indonesia that there is dissatisfaction about this. Singapore and Malaysia have been in the smoke for months, to the great anger of neighbouring countries, who want the Indonesian government to intervene. Under pressure from protests at home and abroad, a number of people and companies have been charged with causing the fires. 'These are very large concentrations of smoke. It is very bad for people's health,' explains professor Van der Werf. 'Your eyes water, you get nauseous.' He experienced this himself years ago during fieldwork in Indonesia. Then he could not see across the street because of the density of the smoke. 'We could leave then, but the local population is stuck there for months.' Air quality above Singapore, Kuala Lumpur and Borneo is now in the dangerous category. Singapore has been the city with the worst air quality in the world several times in recent weeks. In Indonesia alone, around 300,000 people have reported respiratory infections in recent weeks. The fires are taking the region back to 2015, when nearly 3 million hectares of nature went up in flames. Although little can be done about the fires in the short term, measures can certainly be taken in the long term. 'A lot of new rules have been added since 2015,' says Van der Werf. 'That regulation is not yet very effective, but more can still be done.' Rules and enforcement will not stop the current fires. Only the monsoon can do that. For now, Indonesians and their neighbours can do nothing but wait for the rain to come.

title: Five years in prison demanded against man for serious child abuse via livestream
lead: A prison sentence of five years has been demanded against a 55-year-old man from Rijen for the serious sexual abuse of young children on camera. The man allegedly paid to watch live the abuse of children from poor countries, which was committed at his request. A special investigation team of the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> received a report in March this year from the United States that a Dutch user was searching for livestreams of child abuse through multiple accounts on online platforms. Between July and October 2025, the suspect allegedly sought contact with 1369 other accounts. According to the OM, the chats and video conversations collected by the Americans show that in August, sexual acts were actually carried out on two children on the suspect's orders. 'Daughter' Livestreams of child abuse that men from Western countries watch (live distant abuse) are an increasing and worrying phenomenon, the <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> writes. The investigation shows that the suspect allegedly has 25 accounts. Via those accounts he asks his contacts for "video contact via an 'exclusive' environment", according to the OM. The man asks whether they have a daughter and whether they would want to do a show with her. He reportedly has a preference for young girls between 0 and 8 years old. The police were able to determine the identity of the suspect from Rijen via the IP address. He was arrested at the end of April. Imagery The man also stands trial for possessing images of child sexual abuse. On seized data carriers, not only images of sexual abuse of children can be seen, but also with life-like dolls of children. Those dolls and images are also punishable, the OM says. The Public Prosecution Service describes the abuse as far-reaching. In one of the chats the suspect allegedly urged a woman to perform sexual acts on a very young boy, "and that she had to show it properly for the camera". The public prosecutor calls the images and texts shocking. "The suspect has for about 6 months repeatedly tried to satisfy his sexual urges at the expense of young, defenceless children", according to the prosecutor. Real victims In the case, the suspect is seen as the perpetrator of the abuse because, although it happened at a distance, it allegedly took place on his instructions. The prosecutor emphasises that the abuse actually took place. "Children in the world have actually become victims of serious sexual abuse. That we do not know the child's name and that we do not know where it lives makes no difference to that." The man was already convicted in 2001 for possessing images of child abuse. That counts as aggravating circumstances in the demand. In addition to the prison sentence, the OM asks for treatment for the man. NOS asked the suspect's lawyer for a response, but he says that in the interest of his client he will not comment on the criminal case. The judge will rule in two weeks.

title: After riots, the streets of Amsterdam's Floradorp are clean again, but the debate over the bonfire continues
lead: In the middle of the Sneeuwbalstraat in <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">Amsterdam</entity>-Noord a large patch of burn damage is still visible. Pallets were set on fire here last night. Municipal cleaners are busy erasing the traces of another evening full of unrest. Last night stones and glass bottles were thrown at the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> and small fires were started on the street and in waste containers. Three suspects have been arrested. The unrest began last Wednesday after residents received a letter from <entity id="person:femke-halsema">burgemeester Halsema</entity>. It stated that their alternative plan for the traditional bonfire on New Year's Eve had been rejected. The bonfire, which had been a tradition in the neighbourhood for more than 70 years, was banned last year due to safety risks. Residents then proposed lighting a smaller fire in a professional container. The mayor does not favour that either. "The fire brigade still maintains that open fires within the built-up area are too dangerous. A fire in an open container is also an open fire", Halsema wrote. Angela Kraan is watching the cleaners. She has lived in the area for 32 years and has already been experiencing nuisance for a week from young people playing a cat-and-mouse game with the fire brigade. "It's simply a disaster. It starts in the afternoon with noise and smell nuisance. I can't go outside anymore with my dog because it starts trembling all over." She understands there is a lot of anger about the disappearance of the years-long tradition, but she also has understanding for Halsema. "On New Year's Eve a small fire on the field with some fire baskets around it should be possible, but the mayor doesn't want that because she can't assume it will stay small. That, in my view, is the problem." Tradition Not everyone thinks the bonfire should disappear. Some point to the long tradition and want the municipality to allow a smaller fire after all. "Otherwise it will take months here. The mayor has to allow the alternative." An older man says: "It's simply the Amsterdam identity that is being destroyed." Not everyone thinks this way. Gerard Kampstra believes mayor Halsema should stand behind the ban. "It's far too dangerous. At first it went well on the field a bit further away, but it kept getting bigger. Everyone came, and it was no longer a small neighbourhood party. Until about midnight it stayed quiet, but after that it was a disaster." He does not favour a small alternative fire in a container either. "Lighting a little fire, it's over. There's no time for that anymore."

title: France announces major police deployment for demonstrations on Saturday, army also deployed
lead: French authorities are sending an extensive police force onto the streets on Saturday due to announced demonstrations. Prime Minister Lecornu spoke today in parliament of a "strong" deployment. In addition, the government wants to deploy soldiers to relieve police officers from fixed guard duties. The police forces will then be freed up for maintaining public order. The government is also considering banning certain demonstrations. Minister of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> Nuñez said today that this concerns unregistered demonstrations and demonstrations "that could cause disorder". The announcements follow the disorder during the nationwide protests last weekend. Riots broke out at protests against government policy and rising costs of living. Last night remained quiet. A curfew was in force in various cities. Curfews Prime Minister Lecornu earlier said the curfew contributed to the quiet night. The curfew will therefore also be in force again tonight in places where local authorities deem it necessary. In central Lyon a curfew applies again from 21.00 to 06.00. The ban on going out also remains in force in Lille and surrounding municipalities. In Bordeaux the restrictions apply in the neighborhoods hit hardest by the looting of 17 October. In Paris the curfew was in force last night in parts of the centre, around among others Place de la République and Les Halles.

title: US envoy Witkoff to St. Petersburg with proposals for Ukraine, Norway and Finland
lead: The American envoy Witkoff travels to St. Petersburg tomorrow with proposals to end the war in Ukraine. That is what Norwegian Prime Minister Store said after a meeting between Witkoff and Ukrainian President Zelensky in Oslo. The Ukrainian president was assisted during the conversation by Store himself and Finnish President Stubb. "We are trying to encourage the dialogue between Ukraine and the US but also with Russia", said Store. "We have our own interest, because we share a border with Russia. It is better to talk than not to talk." Meeting of leaders One of the proposals Witkoff is bringing to Russia is a meeting between President Trump, Putin and Zelensky. "You cannot talk about the future of Ukraine without Ukraine being at the table", said Zelensky. Prime Minister Store said that Europe will also have to be at the table if you want a lasting and fair peace. According to Norwegian Prime Minister Store, the conversation with Witkoff "went well and was constructive". Finnish President Stubb said that in the week before the meeting in Oslo, much progress had already been made toward a peaceful resolution of the war. To the question put to Zelensky, Stubb and Store about what they think of the signals that the American government increasingly seems to be siding with Russia, Store said: "We must now look forward, not at what was said yesterday or last week. The fact that Witkoff is going to Russia means that something is happening." Intelligence resumed Zelensky spoke by phone this morning with US Secretary of State Rubio of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-buitenlandse-zaken">Buitenlandse Zaken</entity>. That conversation covered, among other things, Ukraine's complaint that the US had for a week no longer warned Ukraine about incoming ballistic missiles from Russia. Rubio called the accusation that Ukrainians were dying as a result "shameful" and "offensive". The problem has now been resolved, Zelensky said in Oslo. "We are grateful that this information is now available again. I am talking about early warnings, which are very important for our children and citizens. So we are grateful to the Americans that it is working now." Other complaints It is unknown whether the US has responded to other Ukrainian complaints. For example, since last week the army has not been able to make optimal use of the military version of the Starlink satellite system, which makes it difficult to intercept Russian drones. In addition, there is also a delay in the delivery of American air defense equipment paid for by other NATO countries. According to the news agency Reuters and other media, the cause of the delay lies with Rubio's colleague, Defense Secretary Hegseth. He still has to approve the delivery. Why he has not yet done so is not clear.

title: Woman (34) sentenced to seven years in prison for manslaughter of her baby
lead: In The Hague, a 34-year-old woman has been sentenced to seven years in prison for manslaughter of her ten-month-old son. The court considers it proven that the woman used such severe violence that the boy suffered serious brain injury and died as a result. On 14 April 2023 the child was admitted to hospital with very severe brain injury, after the suspect and her husband had called emergency services because their son had become unwell. Three weeks later he died. The woman was identified as a suspect a year later and arrested. She has always denied having had anything to do with the death of her son. According to the suspect, the child sustained the injury from a fall. Violence as the only cause According to several experts who examined the victim, a fall onto the floor, where a thick carpet lay, cannot explain the fatal injury. They concluded that violence must have been the cause of the brain injury. A German forensic expert stated two weeks ago that repeated hard shaking is the only option, writes Omroep West . The court relies on the experts' judgment that the child could only have sustained his brain injury through violence. The court holds that the woman was the one who used the violence. At the moment it arose, she was the only one near the child, as has become clear from the statements of the woman and her partner, according to the court. No openness about the case It has not become clear to the court how the woman applied the violence to her child.
