lead: The former head of the Hungarian central bank has been arrested on suspicion of financial fraud. György Matolcsy was for years an important confidant of former prime minister Orbán, whose government has repeatedly been accused of large-scale corruption. The current prime minister of Hungary, Magyar, announced the arrest of Matolcsy via Facebook . Matolcsy was head of the Hungarian central bank from 2013 to 2025. Before that, he was minister of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-ez">Economische Zaken</entity> under Orbán from 2010 to 2013. Since Magyar won the Hungarian elections in April, one of his priorities has been to combat corruption and put an end to the political system that his predecessor Orbán had built over sixteen years. Shortly after taking office, Magyar already announced that he wanted to have alleged misconduct from the Orbán era investigated. Forged document Magyar's Facebook post follows a statement from the Hungarian Public Prosecutor's Office reporting that 'coordinated investigative actions' took place at various locations in the country as part of an investigation into the embezzlement of central bank money. Matolcsy's lawyer tells the Hungarian medium Telex that his client is suspected of economic fraud, in which considerable financial damage is said to have been caused. He is also reportedly accused of using a forged private document. The lawyer has objected to the detention. Hundreds of millions of euros During Matolcsy's tenure as head of the central bank, he was already embroiled in controversy several times over possible corruption. Under his leadership, the bank set up foundations in which hundreds of millions of euros of public money were placed. Part of that money was invested in real estate. An investigation by the current leadership of the central bank found that five properties were considerably less valuable than the amounts at which they were recorded in the books. The bank subsequently filed a report, including on suspected fraud and mismanagement. It is also being investigated whether public money was siphoned off and whether family members of Matolcsy enriched themselves. Matolcsy has always denied earlier allegations of corruption. In May a parliamentary inquiry committee was established to investigate the misconduct at the Hungarian central bank.

title: Heineken must pay over 111 million for malpractices of Greek subsidiary
lead: Brewer Heineken must pay damages of more than one hundred million euros to Greek beer producer Macedonian Thrace Brewery (MTB). The court in Amsterdam has ruled this. According to the court, Heineken is responsible for the malpractices of its Greek subsidiary Athenian Brewery (AB). With the ruling, an end appears to be coming to a long-running lawsuit that Heineken has been embroiled in since 2014. The Greek competition authority then established that AB abused its dominant position on the Greek beer market between 1998 and 2014. In 2024 the court already ruled that Heineken is responsible for that abuse of market power, and now the brewer is getting the fine of 111.2 million euros. Athenian Brewery sells, among other brands, the Greek brand Alfa, alongside Heineken and Amstel. Heineken's Athens subsidiary had a strategy of keeping competitors' beer out of supermarkets and hotel and restaurant chains. The company did this by insisting on exclusivity contracts. Lost profits For these practices, the Dutch head in Athens and his successor were also previously punished with a fine. Since that conviction, competitors, including the relatively small Greek MTB, have demanded a total of 478 million euros in damages. According to the Amsterdam court, Greek MTB has lost profits for years. The extent of the damage amounts to 43.3 million euros according to the court, and on top of that comes another 67.9 million in interest. MTB initially demanded 160 million euros. Danish beer giant Carlsberg also claimed a multi-million amount due to lost income from its Greek subsidiary Olympic Brewery, known for Mythos beer. That lawsuit is still at an early stage. In this lawsuit against MTB, Heineken says it will appeal. According to the brewer, the amount of the damages does not match "the economic evidence, the business situation of MTB and the Greek beer market in that period".

title: Empty shelves in Italy due to truck driver road blockades
lead: All roads lead to Rome, but not right now. For more than a week, truck drivers in southern Italy have been blocking motorways and ports because of the higher diesel price. The supply of products to supermarkets is being squeezed as a result; Italians are facing empty shelves. The protests began in the region of Apulia - the heel of Italy - but have since grown into nationwide protests. The port of Naples has been blocked, and there is traffic disruption around the port of Gioia Tauro in the southern region of Calabria. That disruption can also be seen at one of Italy's most important fruit and vegetable auctions in the municipality of Fondi. In the town of Benevento, a pasta factory has halted production because no more grain is being delivered. Elsewhere in the country, manufacturers have also closed their doors. More expensive full tank The protests are mainly aimed at the diesel price, which has risen sharply since the attacks by the United States and Israel on Iran in February. In less than eight months, the price in Italy has risen by 60 cents per litre. For a truck driver, that soon means a full tank costs 250 to 400 euros more. Drivers are also dissatisfied with the high toll charges they have to pay. Moreover, in their view, the payment of the promised government support is too slow. Southern Italy protests Drivers are blocking roads, mainly in the south of the country. In southern Italy it is easier to block things, because the road network is less extensive than in the north. The south also has relatively many important junctions, such as Naples and Gioia Tauro, which the demonstrators are now exploiting. Another factor is that the south is poorer than the north. When prices rise in southern Italy, people there get into difficulty more quickly. That does not mean that truck drivers in the north do not face the same problems. The Ministry of Transport is announcing measures. The government is making one billion euros available to help drivers. Money will go, among other things, to operators of ferries to and from the Italian islands. Still, there will be no excise cut, and therefore the end of the protests does not seem to be in sight for now. Protests across Italy Farmers and transport companies have now also joined the protests. They demand that the government of Prime Minister Meloni commit to immediate tax relief on agricultural diesel. The protests of recent days are rooted in dissatisfaction with the cost of living. Last weekend, people in northern Italy also took to the streets out of dissatisfaction with rising costs. This led to riots, in which hundreds of demonstrators were arrested.

title: Podcast De Dag: beyond the 1,5 degree warming
lead: The earth is certain to warm by more than 1,5 degrees, the UN states today in a report. The figure has for ten years been the holy grail for tackling climate change. And although it is certain that we will not achieve that goal, policymakers keep holding on to it. Listen here: You can listen to this episode of De Dag via NPO Luister and all other podcast apps. Do you like it? Then don't forget to subscribe. Climate scientist Leo Meyer was at the 2015 climate summit in Paris and explains in the podcast De Dag how it was agreed back then that the earth may warm by at most 2 degrees, but that countries strive for a maximum of 1,5 degrees. But even then it was already clear that this would require big steps. Climate editor Rob Ramaker sees that those steps have not been taken in recent years and that the US pulled out of nearly every climate meeting after President Trump took office. The UN now outlines a plan to return below 1,5 degrees. But to achieve that, enormous steps are needed. For now we are heading towards other figures and thus other consequences of climate change. Reactions: mail to dedag@nos.nl Presentation & editing: Marco Geijtenbeek Editorial: Wouter Sloekers & Judith van de Hulsbeek

title: Strikes in regional transport suspended for two weeks, negotiations resumed
lead: Actions in regional transport have been suspended for two weeks. Trade unions FNV and CNV say they have received a letter from employers' organisations that gives them confidence in new talks on a collective labour agreement (cao) for employees in regional transport. Because the unions and employers are sitting down together again, the planned strikes are for now off the table, FNV and CNV announce in a press release. That also applies to the strike that was due to take place tomorrow. At the beginning of October, the unions announced they would strike one day a week due to failed cao negotiations. Last week it happened for the first time. Employees of carriers such as Arriva, Keolis and Qbuzz, among others, laid down their work. As a result, many buses and regional trains did not run in various regions. 'Important commitments' Yesterday the employers' association for public transport (VWOV) had already sent a letter with an invitation to renegotiate. According to the unions, the letter was still too vague. This morning FNV and CNV received a new letter, in which, according to a CNV negotiator, "all proposals to worsen the cao have been taken off the table". According to the unions, the letter contains "important concrete commitments" that provide a sufficient basis to restart the negotiations. The unions demand, among other things, 9.5 percent extra salary over a period of two years and better working conditions for older staff.

title: So many sites down at once: how is that possible? And is your data safe?
lead: Various websites are going offline as a precaution , from RTL Nieuws, DigiD and MijnOverheid to the website of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>. What exactly is going on and where does this major security vulnerability suddenly come from? How did this leak come to light? Yesterday the organisation behind PHP, a programming language on which many websites are built, made an announcement, as software makers often do: on Wednesday a solution would be released for a problem with PHP. Software makers do this so that everyone can prepare for a solution. In this case, however, hackers seized on that announcement to pinpoint the exact leak and make information about it public. With that information it is relatively easy to exploit the leak. What is PHP? PHP is a programming language. It is one of the original languages of the worldwide web; the first version came out as early as 1995. Although its popularity has declined because newer programming languages with a hipper image have appeared, it is still one of the silent driving forces behind the web. Liveblog Follow the latest developments about the leak in our liveblog . Today's software leak is in the so-called interpreter, a piece of software that translates the commands written by programmers into something the computer understands. How serious is this leak? It concerns two weaknesses in PHP. Because many websites use PHP, many websites are therefore also immediately vulnerable. How seriously a site is affected varies from case to case. In themselves these are already two relatively serious leaks. All software leaks receive a score on a scale from 0 to 10, a so-called CVE score. These two leaks both receive a 9,2. Anyone who can exploit these weaknesses can worm their way into a website and, for example, steal customer data, break further into the company behind the website or open new attacks on visitors. What makes it more serious is that a solution only came around 4 p.m., while the leak had already apparently been exploited for hours. A permanent solution simply did not exist until the makers of PHP released a new version; all that time websites were vulnerable. Is it an overreaction to take websites offline as a precaution? What makes this leak serious is that there was no real solution. Website owners could do their best to block suspicious traffic, but that did not work completely: hacking attempts could always get through and succeed. Because there was no watertight solution, many website owners chose to play it safe. Still, taking sites offline is not the only solution. Another is to switch off all interactive functions, so that a visitor, for example, can no longer log in, leave comments or upload files. For a site like DigiD that has little use, but a site with only information could, for example, stay online this way. Whether that is possible in practice in the short term is another matter. Has my data been stolen now? There are no concrete examples of exploitation yet, but the chance is high that they will follow. So there are no indications that websites have already been affected, let alone that they then leak private data of their users, but it is certainly not ruled out. And the chance that it will happen is even greater, because many website owners update their software far too late. Especially sites of smaller companies and hobby sites sometimes run versions that are years old. In the coming period those are therefore extra vulnerable. What does this say about the vulnerability of the internet? However large the internet is, ultimately a relatively small collection of programming languages and software is the driving force behind it. A serious software leak can therefore mean that many websites or other computer systems are affected at once, and this is not happening for the first time today. AI also makes it increasingly easy to find leaks in software, and it can do so ever faster. The ethical hackers who originally found the leaks and reported them to the makers of PHP also used AI. Whether the malicious hackers who published the code for everyone did so too is unknown. How long will it take before the affected websites are back online? The so-called patch for PHP is now online, so in principle it is now a matter of updating. If all goes well, websites should work again relatively soon afterwards. Still, problems can always occur. For example, many more people than usual might suddenly want to download a PHP update, causing the servers to become overloaded. Software updates can also always go wrong. The chance that the sites in question are still offline later this evening or even tomorrow, however, seems small.

title: Two Dutch nationals arrested in Colombia for cocaine trafficking
lead: In an international drugs investigation, two Dutch men have been arrested in Colombia at the request of the Dutch <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> (OM). A spokesperson for the OM confirms this after reporting by AD . The men are suspected of involvement in large-scale cocaine trafficking. They are a 36-year-old and a 65-year-old Dutch national. They were arrested in recent days in the cities of Cali and Medellín. The arrests are connected to two separate Dutch investigations into cocaine trafficking. Both investigations started earlier this year, the OM spokesperson says when asked. According to the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>, the youngest suspect was directly involved in loading containers and selling cocaine. The oldest man is said to have mainly been occupied with the administrative processes involved in arranging shipments in which cocaine was hidden in containers. Encrypted messages The suspects used Sky ECC, an encrypted messaging service on modified smartphones. Through intercepted messages, the men came into view of the Dutch investigative services. About the cracking of Sky ECC, we wrote this article at the time: According to the politie and the OM, those messages show that the two were already involved for several years in the trade in cocaine from South America to Europe. Colombian media write that the men formed a link between European criminal organisations and the Colombian drug trade. The cocaine was reportedly intended, among other places, for the Netherlands and Belgium. The police investigation is ongoing. Under the authority of the Landelijk Parket of the OM, further investigation is being carried out into data carriers seized during the arrest of the men. A decision still has to be made about possible extradition to the Netherlands. Earlier arrests This is not the first time Dutch suspects of drug trafficking have been arrested in Colombia. Earlier this year, six Dutch men were already arrested in that South American country in investigations by the Landelijk Parket. According to the politie and the OM, the arrests show that international cooperation with Colombia is paying off. Criminals who operate from abroad in serious crime, such as importing drugs into the Netherlands, are sooner or later arrested, the politie writes in a press release .

title: Amsterdam Dance Event turns 30: 'Night culture is much more than raving'
lead: The Swan Lake, Beethoven's Fifth, and art and light installations: it can all be seen during the Amsterdam Dance Event (ADE), which began today. The largest event for electronic music in the world is celebrating its 30th anniversary this year. Tens of thousands of music professionals and DJs are in Amsterdam these days to meet, do business and perform. What once began as a conference on dance music for a few hundred experts in debate centre De Balie has grown into a cultural event with panels, festivals and parties throughout the city, among other things. More than 300 venues take part, from large festival venues such as the Johan Cruijff Arena to small clubs, vinyl shops, theatres, cafés, hockey clubs and even care homes. The spread of venues has increased over the years. Thirty years ago, ADE took place only in clubs and venues in the city centre, such as Paradiso, the Melkweg and Escape. Now something happens in every district of Amsterdam, and even beyond. For example, the organisation behind Awakenings is for the second year in a row holding all its parties at the SugarFactory, the former sugar factory in Halfweg. 72 venues: That broadening is also visible in the art and culture programme. For example, the Nationale Ballet and the Concertgebouw Orchestra perform, and there are dance performances, art projects and audiovisual installations to see, for example in the Oude Kerk. Anne van der Weijden is curator of this part of ADE. 'When I started in 2023, about twenty venues spread across the city took part and I was responsible for the programme on my own. This year there are 72 venues, often with daily performances or shows, and I have a team behind me. As a result, we can not only programme more, but also come up with a broader and more diverse offering.' Where funds previously ignored night culture, Van der Weijden sees more and more willingness to invest in ADE's art and culture programme, which is a foundation. 'That has made it possible for the programme to grow this much.' According to Wiecher Troost, responsible for programming the event, electronic music and night culture are increasingly taken seriously, especially by policymakers. The coronavirus period has been an important turning point in this, he says. 'Since then, funds have had a much better sense of what is going on among young people in nightlife. Young and diverse policymakers have been important drivers in this.' Not staying up all night: Electronic dance music moved from the US to Europe a little over thirty years ago and originated in clubs. But around it exists a much broader culture, according to Troost. 'Think of dance, video art, light art, set construction and other art forms. Night culture is much more than raving.' Slowly but surely, the image that ADE is only about drugs and parties lasting deep into the night is disappearing. The black and yellow ADE flags that hang throughout Amsterdam today were unthinkable in the early years. That was mainly reserved for other cultural events. Moreover, many people who grew up with dance no longer want to stay up all night in a club, but do want to stay connected to nightlife and the culture around it, Troost sees. 'That is a development we also see in other target groups.' Two care homes in the Jordaan are taking part in ADE for the first time this year. 'We wanted to do something different for once,' says activity supervisor Chiara Cherillo of De Rietvinck. This afternoon a 'ravebingo' takes place there. 'We have arranged a DJ who plays a mild form of techno, alternated with Jordaan classics,' says Cherillo. 'We have linked a bingo to that. The winner gets a new rollator and a festival ticket.' At another location, at the Makroon, a Rollator Rave is on the schedule for tomorrow. This is what that Rollator Rave looked like: With flyers at cafés in the Jordaan, Cherillo recruited volunteers for the two events. The idea behind it was to bring the younger and older generations into contact. 'We want our residents to remain part of society and involved in what is happening in Amsterdam.' The world of residents of a care home is often small, says Cherillo. 'When people from outside come by, that brings extra attention. That means a lot to our residents. We also want to project a certain image: a care home can take part in ADE too.' Limit reached: More and more often, Amsterdam venues with their own following join ADE, from a yoga studio organising a special techno session to a family rave for parents and children, or a newly completed, leading building that opens its doors to the public. Troost understands this trend. 'You are part of something bigger happening in the city.' According to him, that broadening should remain central over the next thirty years as well. 'We are already at our limit of 600,000 visitors per year. Our goal is not to become even bigger, but precisely to involve more communities in ADE.'

title: Websites slowly come back online after security update in PHP programming language
lead: Websites that were taken offline as a precaution are slowly coming back online. Shortly before 16.00, the organisation behind the PHP programming language carried out a security update that users could install. As a result, websites can start up safely again. In recent hours, many organisations took their websites offline because of two major leaks in the PHP programming language, which is used for many websites worldwide. A programming language is a language with which you tell a computer what to do. Programmers use the languages to build websites, apps and software. Where did this security leak suddenly come from, and is your data safe? Read more in the article below by our tech editor: Shortly before 17.00, the website of RTL, on which RTL Nieuws among others publishes, was back online. Tech website Tweakers was also reachable again around that time. Websites of various hospitals and municipalities were also offline and are gradually coming back online. Governments The important Dutch government website mijn.overheid.nl was reachable again shortly after 18.00. The DigiD site was back online around 20.30. DigiD could still be used to log in on other sites, even though its website was offline. Internationally, various government websites were temporarily taken offline, such as in Belgium, Finland, France and Germany. Shortly before 17.00, the website of the Finnish government was reachable again. Liveblog Follow the latest developments about the leak in our liveblog. Despite the security update, new problems may still occur. For example, it could be that many more people than usual suddenly want to download a PHP update, causing the servers to become overloaded. Software updates can also always go wrong. The chance that the websites in question will still be offline later tonight or even tomorrow seems small, however. According to the American organisation behind the PHP programming language, the PHP Foundation, there are so far no signs that the vulnerabilities in the programming language have led to misuse of companies through their websites. The Dutch <entity id="org:nationaal-cyber-security-centrum">NCSC</entity> and the American CISA, both specialised in cybersecurity, confirm this. They say they have seen no active misuse of the leak. PHP The PHP Foundation announced yesterday that it would carry out a security update today. Hackers seized on the announcement to locate the leak and spread information about it. Malicious actors may misuse that information, for example by breaking into websites that use the programming language and stealing customer data.

title: Limited group of regular customers can place orders with AH again after cyberattack
lead: A limited group of people can place orders with Albert Heijn again. The company reports this on its website. Earlier, the supermarket chain said it could not deliver groceries until today. On Sunday, it said that delivery drivers would not be back on the road until Friday. It concerns customers with a so-called delivery bundle and business customers. They were informed about this today. The supermarket writes that it is restarting the systems "step by step". Still, the situation is far from what it was. Albert Heijn stresses that only a third of the usual delivery capacity is available. The customer service is partly available. At the beginning of last week, Ahold Delhaize, the parent company of Albert Heijn, was hit by a cyberattack. For this reason, the company took its systems offline. This quickly led to empty shelves in the supermarkets. On Monday, the company filed a report with the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>. Internet leak The news comes on the day that many websites have been taken offline due to a leak in PHP. This is one of the most widely used programming languages. As a precaution, the sites of DigiD, MijnOverheid and RTL Nieuws went offline. Schiphol also temporarily took its app offline. A spokesperson for Ahold Delhaize tells the ANP that, at this time, they see no connection with the recent cyberattack on the supermarket chain. "As far as we can currently tell, there is no reason to assume this." The investigation into the cyberattack is still ongoing.

title: Mexico wants to know whether cartel members are fighting in Ukraine to gain drone expertise
lead: The Mexican government has launched an investigation into the possible participation of members of Mexican drug cartels in the war in Ukraine. The reason is a video circulating on social media in which men fighting in the Ukrainian army name two of the best-known Mexican cartels. According to President Sheinbaum, her government will "try to find out how Mexicans, in this case persons who may belong to a criminal group, became involved in an armed conflict in Europe". The men could "have been recruited by a private company that takes part in such conflicts, by an army or by a government", she says. Sinaloa and Jalisco cartels. In the video a group of armed men can be seen in a forest. According to the man filming, they are returning from a mission. Another man says that the person filming is part of La Chapiza. That is the faction of the Sinaloa cartel led by the sons of drug lord Joaquín 'El Chapo' Guzmán. He then also chants the name of the Jalisco cartel. Since the summer of 2025, several research platforms have reported that Mexican intelligence has warned Ukraine that cartel members have signed up for the International Legion of the Ukrainian army. Volunteers from other countries can enlist there to fight against Russia. But until now, no videos of cartel members at the Ukrainian front had actually surfaced. Special drones. Cartels are said to mainly send people to Ukraine to train them in the use of so-called first-person view drones (FPV drones). The pilot of the drone then sees live images from the drone's camera, so it looks as if they are flying along themselves. In Mexico, criminal organisations are increasingly using such drones to smuggle drugs or to attack rivals' territories with explosives attached to these drones. The Jalisco cartel even has its own unit focused on the use of drones, research platform InSight Crime reported last year. Since the war in Ukraine, the number of attacks with explosive drones in Mexico has increased: besides rival groups, government buildings and police patrols have also been targets. An estimated 120 drone attacks were carried out in Mexico last year. Hundreds of people died as a result. In the state of Michoacán, chemicals are even being attached to explosives on drones, the local police showed the NOS. Mexican officers told the following about the weapons used last year: At the border, people smugglers use drones to monitor patrols of the US border guard before groups of migrants are led through irregular tunnels and other border crossings. Drones are also used there to fly doses of the addictive painkiller fentanyl to the US. Last Friday the US government announced an all-out drone ban at the border with Mexico to combat this people and drug smuggling. Strategy from Ukraine? The Mexican authorities have invested heavily in recent years in technology to bring drones out of the sky, for example with signal jammers. Cartels seem to be anticipating this by using drones with fibre-optic cables, a strategy that appears to have been taken over one-to-one from Ukraine. Earlier this month, fifteen FPV drones along with fifteen rolls of fibre-optic cable were seized in the state of Sinaloa. Drones with fibre-optic cables had never before been found in Mexico. The possible participation of Mexican cartel members is grist to Russia's mill. The Russian intelligence service SVR claimed yesterday on Telegram that the US is now investigating whether there are links between Ukrainian and Mexican drug cartels. Russia states that at least eighty Mexicans have been identified who are gaining combat experience with the Ukrainian armed forces. Ukraine has not responded to the reports about Mexicans who reportedly fought on the Ukrainian side.

title: VGZ wants 34 municipalities to (re)introduce policy for people on low incomes
lead: Health insurer VGZ has sent a letter to the mayors of the 34 municipalities in the Netherlands that do not offer a municipal policy. The health insurer wants to discuss this with them. Some municipalities have abolished the scheme, while others never had it. VGZ believes that all municipalities should offer the municipal policy. The municipal policy is a basic insurance with a supplementary insurance that municipalities offer together with a health insurer to people on low incomes. The municipality pays part of the costs. Among others, <entity id="org:gemeente-utrecht">Utrecht</entity>, Breda and <entity id="org:gemeente-groningen">Groningen</entity> already abolished the municipal policy because of the high costs. People who used that scheme now have to insure themselves 'normally'. If they want the same care, they have to pay a higher premium. Usually they cannot or do not want to do that. As a result, they are not insured for healthcare costs outside the basic insurance, such as dental care and physiotherapy. They then avoid that kind of care. For example, people sometimes do not go to the dentist despite problems with their teeth. This can ultimately lead to higher costs. The Institute for Public Economics (IPE) therefore recently called for a national scheme in a report to protect people on low incomes from high healthcare costs. The institute advises replacing the more than three hundred local schemes with one national approach. This is meant to prevent avoidance of care and to ensure that all low incomes receive protection. In the Netherlands, 580,000 people use a municipal policy. 90,000 people would also benefit from it, but they live in a municipality that does not offer the policy. Another 70,000 people could apply for the policy in their municipality, but they do not because the municipality contributes too little to the premium. VGZ wants to keep the municipal policy VGZ sees more value in keeping the municipal policy than in a national scheme. That is why the health insurer is calling on municipalities that do not offer the policy to look again at the options. "We want to prevent the government from creating an entirely separate scheme," says a VGZ spokesperson. "That would cost a lot of work, while many municipalities still have a municipal policy that does its job well." According to VGZ, municipalities should offer several packages. Not everyone uses the same amount of care, and if only one package is offered in a municipality, it often does not match all target groups. As a result, many residents who use the municipal policy are overinsured. The scheme falls under the Participation Act, and municipalities decide for themselves whether to take part. Because many municipalities have to cut spending, they choose expenditures they can get rid of, such as the municipal policy. This produces a gain in the short term. However, a cost-benefit analysis by research bureau Rebel shows that a decent contribution to the municipal policy is cheaper for municipalities in the long run than covering the debts that arise from, for example, long-term avoidance of care. Dental bus Preventive actions are not part of the municipal policy, but VGZ says it does see the municipal policy as a way to do more on prevention. "We actually want to focus more on prevention, so that we can ultimately relieve pressure on healthcare." The health insurer cites as examples special prevention actions for people with overweight in Brabant and a dental bus in <entity id="org:gemeente-s-gravenhage">Den Haag</entity>, where people can have their teeth checked free of charge. Health insurers CZ and Menzis are also in favour of the municipal policy. "In municipalities that have stopped the scheme, we see that debts are increasing and that there is avoidance of care out of fear of unexpected extra costs," says a spokesperson for Menzis. Health insurer CZ says it will also send a letter to all municipalities without a municipal policy. Zilveren Kruis, on the other hand, sees more value in a national scheme. According to the insurer, the municipal policy offers insufficient certainty because not every municipality has the scheme and the content differs per municipality. Zilveren Kruis does say it will continue to offer the municipal policy as long as there is no national statutory scheme. Postcode discrimination The differences in contribution between municipalities are considerable. How much residents themselves pay for their health insurance partly depends on their postcode. For example, an episode of Pointer showed that a resident of the <entity id="org:gemeente-diemen">gemeente Diemen</entity> pays 64 euros per month for a municipal policy. In the neighbouring <entity id="org:gemeente-ouder-amstel">gemeente Ouder-Amstel</entity>, the same policy costs only 33 euros per month. There, the municipality therefore contributes more. 84 municipalities contribute at least 40 euros per month, while 53 municipalities contribute less than 20 euros. The other 167 municipalities fall in between. It is not yet clear whether the 34 municipalities that do not offer a municipal policy will respond to VGZ's call.

title: American politician and dozens of others arrested during olive harvest on West Bank
lead: The Israeli army has arrested dozens of volunteers who were helping Palestinians with the olive harvest in the occupied West Bank, according to American and Israeli human rights organisations. Around eighty volunteers were picking olives with Palestinian farmers in Nahalin, near Bethlehem, when the Israeli army and police arrested them, says Rabbis for Human Rights, one of the human rights organisations that was present. One of those arrested is the Jewish-American politician Brad Lander, an ally of the mayor of New York, Zohran Mamdani. He is the Democratic candidate for the House of Representatives. Lander says on social media that they were "simply harvesting olives in an orchard" in the occupied West Bank. "The occupation is a crime under international law. Harvesting olives is not a crime under any law I am aware of." The group was taken to the police station in two buses. Lander says on social media that he was released with a "warning", but that other volunteers are still being detained. According to the Israeli authorities, the volunteers were in a "closed military zone". Rabbis for Human Rights says it was not aware of this. It has not been made public why the area was declared a closed military zone. One of the volunteers says on Instagram that settlers from the nearby illegal settlement of Beitar Illit had called in the Israeli army and police. Settler violence The volunteers, including American, British and Israeli nationals, were there to protect Palestinians from the violence of Israeli settlers. The annual olive harvest is an important source of income for the Palestinian residents of the West Bank. Last week Friday, dozens of Israeli settlers attacked Palestinians during the harvest in an olive grove in the village of Abu Falah. They also set olive trees on fire and threw stones at Palestinians. American photojournalist Heidi Levine of The Washington Post was assaulted by a group of settlers. Her belongings were also stolen. A day later, Israeli settlers attacked Palestinians and European diplomats in the Palestinian village of Taybeh. Representatives of the Catholic Church were also attacked at that time.

title: Police: Hajar presumably killed in anti-squatting building in Amsterdam
lead: Police believe that 29-year-old Hajar from Amsterdam was killed in an anti-squatting building in the Amsterdam neighbourhood of Buitenveldert. Officers are investigating the building today. In front of the door stands a container of the police forensic investigation unit. The 29-year-old woman was found dead in the water at the Amsteldijk in Amsterdam last Friday, after having been missing for almost two weeks. Shortly after she went missing, the police and her family already said they were seriously worried about her well-being. Yesterday a suspect was arrested. He is a 23-year-old man of Somali nationality with no fixed residence. He came to the Netherlands at the age of six and has a residence permit for an indefinite period. According to Het Parool, this concerns Abdi A. Officers found A. yesterday morning at his parents' home in the North Holland <entity id="org:gemeente-koggenland">gemeente Koggenland</entity>, where they had gone in response to a report of assault. The suspect's foster father turned out to have been assaulted there. An officer recognised A. from the search notice in the Hajar case that had been circulated among all police forces that same morning. Neighbours: According to a neighbour with whom NOS spoke in the village of Spierdijk, A. already came to the houses in which his foster parents now live separately from each other on the night from Monday to Tuesday. The foster mother's boyfriend confirms that the suspect was standing on the doorstep at night. Afterwards he left, say he and a neighbour. In the morning A. was back, with a hammer. He came to "settle a score" with his foster parents, says the neighbour. Traces of this can still be seen from the road. The smashed windows of both houses have been covered with wooden boards. The windscreens of cars on the property were also destroyed. After those vandalisms, the suspect's foster father was next. According to the neighbour, the man was attacked by his foster son with that same hammer. The suspect's younger brother was also at home, the neighbour says. Outside mortal danger: Not only the broken windows are a reminder of what happened here yesterday. After the police investigation, the neighbour went inside the foster father's house, he says. "I should not have done that. There was blood everywhere." When police arrived yesterday morning to arrest the suspect, the foster father was taken to hospital injured. There, according to the neighbour, he received fourteen stitches in his head. The man is still in hospital, but is now out of mortal danger, says the mayor, who visited the foster mother this morning to offer her support. The woman is very shocked, says the mayor. House search in Amsterdam: She and her ex took the suspect, his sister and brother into their home long ago, according to conversations with neighbours. "He was still a little kid," says a female neighbour. The suspect was born in Somalia and came to the Netherlands at the age of six. Why the suspect was placed in the foster family with his younger brother and sister is not clear from conversations with neighbours. Eventually he left the family at the age of sixteen. Whether that was forced or not is not clear. "After that he lived somewhere else and then he dropped out of sight", says a neighbour. According to the police, the suspect has no fixed residence. The suspect is in custody and may only have contact with his lawyer. He will be brought before the judge this week.

title: Russia and Ukraine appear willing to resume negotiations
lead: Russia and Ukraine have today shown willingness to resume negotiations with each other, with the US as mediator. A meeting could be planned within a few weeks, but no firm agreements have been made yet and much remains unclear. US top diplomat Witkoff held talks with President Poetin in Sint-Petersburg for over three hours. Afterwards the Kremlin said that Russia is "in principle" ready to resume talks with Kyiv and Washington. These negotiations could take place around 10 November, diplomat Oesjakov said according to Russian state media. He named Abu Dhabi as a possible location. According to the Russians, Witkoff proposed that a team of diplomats sit down together. The American diplomat himself has not said anything about this yet. New missile attack on Kyiv Ukrainian President Zelensky has responded positively to the American proposal, news agency Reuters reports. He expresses the hope that a meeting for negotiators of the three countries will be held as soon as possible. At such a meeting, peace proposals could be discussed and the possibility of organising a summit for leaders, Zelensky tells journalists via WhatsApp. Shortly after Zelensky's response, air raid sirens sounded in the Ukrainian capital Kyiv. According to mayor Klitsjko, Russia is again carrying out a heavy air attack with ballistic missiles. Nothing is yet known about casualties. Although the official aim of the talks is to end the war in Ukraine, Witkoff and Poetin also spoke about trade: The wording "in principle" indicates that the Kremlin is keeping its options open. It is still a question whether the three parties can agree on the details of a meeting. Relations between Ukrainian President Zelensky and US President Trump have recently reached a new low. Zelensky has repeatedly insisted that, in his view, only a direct meeting between him and Poetin can break the impasse. The Russian president has so far repeatedly said he will only meet Zelensky if an agreement has already been reached. President Zelensky said today to Fox News that he is willing to freeze the war along the current front line, if that could mean an end to the war. He repeated that in return strong security guarantees for Ukraine would then have to be put in place. Release of 74-year-old American Following the talks in Sint-Petersburg, Russia has released 74-year-old Stephen Hubbard. He was captured by the Russian army in 2022. Russia accuses Hubbard of fighting as a mercenary in the Ukrainian army. Hubbard's lawyers deny this. According to The New York Times, the 74-year-old man is very weakened. He is said to have been tortured and malnourished. Hubbard is now on his way to Texas, where his health will be further examined. Trump posted on his platform Truth Social that the release took place at his request and that Russia did not have to receive anything in return "out of respect for President Trump". Hubbard's release would not have been possible, however, if sanctions against Russia had continued, the American president wrote in his next post. Last Friday Trump temporarily suspended an American sanctions package against Russia. Those sanctions had already been adopted a month ago and signed by himself. Diesel deal It was also announced today that the first tanker with 40.000 tonnes of Russian diesel will depart for the US tomorrow. Russian deputy prime minister Novak said this via Russian media. "Subsequent shipments will certainly follow," he said. President Poetin also emphasised in the talks with Witkoff that Russia could supply large quantities of fertiliser to the American market. On 9 October Russia lifted its self-imposed ban on diesel exports, after an agreement with Trump had been concluded to supply diesel to the international market.

title: EU demands Musk lift restrictions on Starlink for Ukraine
lead: The European Union considers The Wall Street Journal's reporting that Elon Musk is responsible for the reduced functioning of Starlink in Ukraine "extremely worrying" and demands an immediate restoration of full functionality. "Ukraine needs satellite internet for communication between its soldiers, to protect its citizens and to operate the drones it needs to defend its territory", said a spokesperson for EU Commission President Von der Leyen. The Ukrainian army noticed last week that its military version of Starlink suddenly worked less well. Among other things, this meant Ukrainian military drones cannot fly faster than 160 kilometers per hour. Kyiv Post heard from sources that they must reach at least 450 kilometers per hour to intercept Russian Shahed drones. The Ukrainian army also lost the connection with drones used for attacks on Russian targets. Musk's reaction: Starlink owner Elon Musk referred questions for explanation to President Trump. The military version of Starlink falls under the authority of the US Department of Defense; Trump is commander-in-chief of the US armed forces. But The Wall Street Journal writes, based on US officials and other sources, that Musk himself made the decision to restrict Starlink's capabilities for Ukraine. He reportedly did consult Trump about it. CBS News confirms based on its own research that this is what happened. Musk did not respond to CBS's request for comment. US Secretary of State Rubio said yesterday that neither Trump nor anyone else in the US government has ordered the restriction of Starlink's capabilities for Ukraine. IRIS2: The EU is working on a satellite network similar to Starlink, called IRIS2. It is to consist of more than 300 satellites and be used for both civilian and military purposes. "Ukraine can fully join it", said Von der Leyen's spokesperson.

title: Cameras to prevent new riots in Amsterdam's Floradorp neighbourhood
lead: To prevent further riots in the Amsterdam neighbourhood of Floradorp, mayor <entity id="person:femke-halsema">Femke Halsema</entity> has introduced camera surveillance. Since the municipality rejected the annual bonfire on New Year's Eve last week, unrest has reigned in the neighbourhood. There were riots and the riot police (ME) had to be deployed several times. The cameras will remain in place until 7 January. Residents were angry last week when they heard that their alternative plan for a smaller bonfire on New Year's Eve was not allowed to go ahead. Last year the New Year's Eve bonfire was banned for safety reasons. Therefore residents proposed to light a smaller fire in an open container this year. According to the fire service this would still be too dangerous. Halsema adopted the fire service's advice, which led to anger among residents. People then gathered on the street and started several small fires. They also pelted the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> with fireworks. On Monday things went wrong again in the neighbourhood and the mobile unit (ME) had to be deployed. Two suspects were arrested. Feelings of insecurity: The regional broadcaster NH writes that the cameras have been placed both in and around the neighbourhood. Residents are said to feel unsafe. "The incidents pose a threat to public order", the municipality writes. "As a result, feelings of insecurity have arisen among residents. There is also fear of further disturbances in this area." The police said earlier that residents were worried. Officers and youth workers have been present in the neighbourhood in recent days to make contact with residents.

title: Woman gives birth to child on moving train in the city of Groningen
lead: In a train in the city of Groningen, a woman gave birth to a child this morning. Het Dagblad van het Noorden spoke with a witness who boarded at Groningen Europapark station around 08.00. The train had barely left when the witness heard a woman groaning. "Then two loud screams and a sort of 'klonk', the sound of a bag with two bottles falling," the newspaper quotes her as saying. "Someone shouted: 'There's a baby on the ground!' And that was true, there was a little baby on the ground." Fellow passengers called the emergency services and asked whether there was a doctor on the train. Someone said: "The baby is okay, I think that was to reassure the mother," the witness said. The train was met at Groningen's main station by emergency services, who took the mother and child with them. Transport operator Arriva does not want to say, out of concern for the privacy of those involved, how they are doing. Dagblad van het Noorden heard from a second witness that they are doing well.

title: Don't Stop Believin': popular musical series Glee makes a comeback on Disney+
lead: The musical series Glee is definitively getting a comeback. This is confirmed by the American streaming services Disney+ and Hulu. The series was a big hit between 2009 and 2015. Creator Ryan Murphy already said last month that he had written a new script. In the series, which is set at a school in Ohio, students set up a new choir: New Directions . Under the guidance of their teacher, they try to become successful with the choir. Meanwhile, the choir members face, among other things, romance, bullying and all kinds of personal problems. Of course, there is also a lot of singing in the musical series. For example, the Glee version of Don't Stop Believin' by Journey grew into an international hit. In the Netherlands, the series aired on RTL 5. Last month, Murphy told the TV programme Entertainment Tonight that he has been in contact with ten members of the original cast. "It was very heartwarming and they had many questions, but they were all very enthusiastic." Deceased actors More than ten years after the last season, three actors from the series have died. One of the lead actors, Cory Monteith, died in 2013 of an overdose of alcohol and drugs. Mark Salling took his own life in 2018, just before he was due to stand trial for possession of child pornography. Naya Rivera drowned in 2020 while swimming with her young son. Much is still unclear about the precise storyline and cast of the comeback. The details are still being kept secret. 113 Are you thinking about suicide or worried about someone? Talking about it helps and can be done anonymously via the chat at www.113.nl or by phone on 113 or 0800-0113.

title: Arab parties in Israel could play a key role in the elections, but cooperation is sensitive
lead: The Arab parties in Israel could play a decisive role in forming a government without Prime Minister Netanyahu after next week's elections. Jewish opposition leaders would then have to be willing to work with them. Such cooperation has been extra sensitive since the Hamas terror attack of 7 October 2023. Still, the United Arab List is making an effort. At a small parking lot in the center of the Bedouin town of Lakiya in the south of Israel, residents are getting ready for a campaign gathering of the United Arab List. Some banners are quickly being hung on trees and cars. Party leader Mansour Abbas could arrive at any moment. The Palestinian residents here have very different concerns than their Jewish fellow citizens. "We have suffered enormously under this racist government," says Ismail Abli. "Our homes are being demolished and we are dealing with violence." Ayoub al-Baz points to the rise in crime within the Arab community. "This government has failed to deal with this." 'Your vote can make a difference' The banners are up now and a few cars have just been quickly moved aside. Mansour Abbas arrives ten minutes later than planned. Some of the roughly thirty residents who came to the gathering sit down on white plastic chairs. "Your vote for the United Arab List can make the difference," Abbas calls out. He does not use the microphone. "Your vote can bring down this racist government." Abbas hopes that he will end up in the coalition and that the situation for Palestinian residents in Israel can be improved. But most Jewish opposition leaders rule out cooperation with Arab parties. "All political leaders, both in the coalition and in the opposition, say one thing before the elections and then do something completely different afterwards," Abbas tells the NOS. "We are citizens with full political rights. We will not accept anyone excluding us." Arik Rudnitzky of the think tank Israel Democracy Institute explains that the Jewish opposition leaders are taking into account the sensitive and tense situation within the Jewish community after the terror of 7 October. "A majority of the population still lives with that trauma." Still, the Arab parties could be an important partner for the Jewish opposition leaders in defeating Prime Minister Netanyahu. The Knesset, the Israeli parliament, has 120 seats. A majority coalition therefore requires at least 61 seats. According to recent polls, neither Netanyahu with his coalition nor the opposition bloc reaches that majority. With the seats of the United Arab List added, that picture could change. The other Arab parties, united in the Joint List, do not want to be part of the new government themselves. But they do not rule out supporting a government from outside, by voting along on certain bills. Rudnitzky thinks that excluding Arab parties is mainly political campaigning. He points to 2021, when Mansour Abbas's party joined the coalition of Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid. There was also a lot of resistance to cooperation with an Arab party then, but in the end that coalition came about anyway. Turnout becomes crucial According to Rudnitzky, turnout among Palestinian residents of Israel in particular plays an important role. "If the United Arab List wins 7 or 8 seats, for example, it is hard to imagine how Jewish parties could keep ruling out considering them as a potential coalition partner." The big question is whether Abbas will manage to get enough people to the ballot box. Turnout among Palestinian Israelis was relatively low in previous elections. It often hovers around 50 percent. Nationally, turnout at the last elections was 70 percent. Still, the party leader thinks it will be different this time. "We see more enthusiasm and a stronger will among residents to go out and vote." The residents who came to the gathering agree. "The discriminatory policy of this government has created social awareness," says Ismail Abli. "People now realise that if they remain politically indifferent, Israel could ultimately end up with governments that are even more extreme than this one." Ayoub al-Baz thinks the same. He refers to the far-right ministers Ben-Gvir and Smotrich from the current government. "We are more aware of the situation and more motivated to vote and to remove them from their posts."

title: Meta fined 25 billion dollars after lying about user data
lead: Meta, the parent company of Facebook, must pay 25 billion dollars because it misled users about how and by whom their data is used. Facebook knew that other parties could access user data, but denied this. The judge in the American state of New Mexico has therefore imposed the billion-dollar fine on the social media company today. The ruling follows a case surrounding the scandal at data company Cambridge Analytica. That company misused tens of millions of user data via Facebook to help President Trump in the 2016 elections. The data made it possible to place targeted advertisements that Americans saw. It was the biggest violation of privacy in Facebook's history. Although the social network knew about this, it hardly took any action. Cambridge Analytica shut down in 2018 because of this scandal. Violations of legislation. Years later, the state of New Mexico sued Facebook. In September a jury ruled that Meta had made misleading claims about access to user data. The tech company committed more than 43 million violations of consumer legislation in New Mexico. Meta's money is intended to go to education in the American state.

title: Offices of dissolved far-right group in EU Parliament searched
lead: Searches were carried out this morning at offices of the European Parliament in Strasbourg and Brussels. The raids are part of the ongoing investigation into possible misuse of EU money by the dissolved far-right group Identity and Democracy (ID). This group was dissolved in 2024 and succeeded by Patriots for Europe (PfE). According to PfE, searches were carried out in administrative offices of the dissolved ID group. The PfE leadership says in a statement that the new group is completely unconnected to the investigation. The investigation is being carried out by EPPO, the European <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity>. This body confirmed to NOS that searches were carried out on "the premises of the European Parliament in France and Belgium", but gave no further details. Raids last summer as well. Last summer, raids were carried out in the same investigation in Spain, France, Italy and Belgium. Members of the ID group are accused of improperly using more than 4 million euros of community money. For example, companies linked to confidants are said to have received contracts without the tendering procedures. The fraud is said to have taken place between 2019 and 2024. During that period, the Dutch PVV, the French Rassemblement National and the Italian Lega were among the members of ID. Le Pen conviction. French presidential candidate Marine Le Pen has been convicted of fraud involving EU money. Initially she was not allowed to run in next year's elections, but that penalty was reversed on appeal last July. Le Pen remains guilty of illegally funnelling millions of European money into her party's coffers. That happened between 2006 and 2014, when she was a member of the European Parliament. Le Pen has consistently dismissed the case against her as a politically motivated trial.

title: Pope Leo does not need further treatment after cancer operation
lead: Pope Leo XIV does not need any further treatment after his operation last week. His doctors state this in a statement to the Vatican. Tissue was taken from the Pope for research. The structure, composition and any abnormalities of his body tissues were examined. The research showed that his illness remained limited to the original site. The 71-year-old Leo was found to have lung cancer during an operation last week. He was operated on for a small lung nodule, which was discovered during a medical check-up. The nodule proved to be malignant. The operation was successful and without complications. The lower part of the Pope's right lung was removed. Mass in hospital His recovery is also going well. Last week it was already clear that the Pope can eat well again and that he is doing breathing exercises. Last Friday the Pope celebrated a mass in the hospital and distributed communion. During the mass, Pope Leo thanked the healthcare workers for the care they provide "for vulnerable patients, and especially for what they have done and continue to do for him". Last Saturday he was discharged from the hospital. By then, the results of blood tests and scans of his chest were already good, and the Pope was in a "suitable" overall clinical condition.

title: Former Northern Irish politician suspected of raping woman in British House of Commons
lead: London police are investigating the suspected rape of a woman in the buildings of the British parliament. The suspect is a former leader of the Northern Irish party DUP, Jeffrey Donaldson (63), who sat in the House of Commons between 2015 and 2024. Last week he was already sentenced to fifteen years in prison for rape and sexual abuse of two girls between 1985 and 2008. The new suspicion concerns the accusation of rape in 2016. The alleged victim is a Northern Irish woman whom Donaldson showed around the House of Commons. "Donaldson introduced her to influential people, took her to a dinner in the members' restaurant and then took her to the DUP offices in the same building", writes Belfast Telegraph . Initially indecent assault The newspaper already reported on this in July. At that time the accusation was that Donaldson had tried to kiss her and that he had placed his hand on her skirt. The police now tell the newspaper and the BBC that the suspicion is that he raped her. The case was initially investigated by the police in Northern Ireland, but on 13 October it was transferred to the London police, because the rape is said to have taken place there. The London police say the investigation is at an early stage. Donaldson has not yet been arrested or questioned. Wife In the case for which Donaldson was sentenced last week, his wife was also found guilty by a jury. She helped her husband with the rape and the abuse of the two minors. The court still has to pass the sentence she receives. Donaldson and his wife are appealing against the convictions.

title: Iconic Apekop train (now really) runs its last passenger service
lead: For years the Mat '64, also known as Apekop, was a symbol of the train in the Netherlands. Today the iconic train ran a regular passenger service for the last time. In fact, the train had already said goodbye to the track in 2016. At that time the NS removed the last train sets from the timetable. Last year the Apekop unexpectedly returned to the route between Amersfoort and Ede-Barneveld Zuid. Operator Keolis had a shortage of trains because part of the existing rolling stock was being refurbished. The company therefore rented a Mat '64 from Stichting 2454CRW, a group of volunteers who manage and maintain old trains. When the trains returned to the timetable, this led to enthusiastic reactions: Today the Apekop departed at 12.25 for its last regular trip from Barneveld Zuid. At the end of this year the foundation will take the museum train back under its own management. The Mat '64 (Materieel '64) was the last train type built in the Netherlands. The first units ran on the tracks in 1961. At its peak, hundreds ran, mainly as stopping trains. The trains got the nickname 'Apekop' because of their striking nose. The design with a rounded nose looks somewhat like the Hondekop, which is ten years older.

title: Criticism of Republican who uses opponent's mother in campaign ad
lead: The battle between Republicans and Democrats in the United States has reached a new low. Republican gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy in the state of Ohio is under fire for deploying the biological mother of his Democratic opponent Amy Acton to smear her. In the video, Donna Arthur, Acton's mother, accuses her daughter, among other things, of being a liar and of having lied about her entire life. Arthur also says that the 60-year-old Acton needs help and calls on people not to vote for her. The video lasts one minute and was first shared on social media by a local political blogger. The campaign ad went online yesterday and is drawing criticism from both Republican and Democratic quarters, because Acton is being confronted with her painful youth. The gubernatorial candidate has in fact had no contact with her biological mother since her youth. Rape Acton was removed from her mother together with her brother at the age of 12 due to severe abuse, neglect and sexual abuse. She was reportedly raped by her stepfather. Acton's campaign team has shared court documents with American media confirming her account. The documents, which were also viewed by news agency Associated Press (AP), show that Acton's stepfather was charged in 1978 with raping Acton. According to the documents, the rapes took place between 1976 and 1978. The report was filed by Acton's biological father. For a time it was unclear who had financed the ad. The video did not carry the required "paid for" notice showing who paid for the advertisement. Acton quickly pointed to Ramaswamy. The campaign team of the 41-year-old Ramaswamy confirmed today that it is behind the controversial video. The Republican has let it be known that he will set aside 4 million dollars to spread the ad further, despite the criticism. Even before Ramaswamy confirmed the video, his spokesperson told American media that he did not know what had happened between Acton and her biological mother. "But we do know that Amy Acton is a pathological liar. She has a serious problem with the truth." Political gain Acton reacted furiously to the ad. "I am not going to normalise someone who claims that my youth is just something I am complaining about." On social media, Acton shared a statement from her brother in which he accuses Ramaswamy of using his sister's sexual abuse for his own political gain. "This desperate, disgusting attack reveals exactly who Vivek Ramaswamy is at his core: a miserable man, who is willing to hurt anyone as long as he gets what he wants", says brother Philip Stearns. 'Stop complaining' The video was widely shared on social media, including by the son of President Trump, Donald Trump Jr., and far-right conspiracy theorist Laura Loomer. Prominent Republicans such as Nikki Haley and Meghan McCain criticised the campaign ad and considered it to go too far. Vice President JD Vance warned Republicans to "stop complaining" about the ad. During a campaign visit to Ohio he said that he is "disgusted" by the criticism from Republican quarters and that "politics is a tough world". He called on his fellow Republicans to focus on winning the midterm elections. It is not known whether the campaign ad will cost Ramaswamy votes. According to American polls, it is a neck-and-neck race in Ohio.

title: Still websites unreachable after leak, international problems too
lead: Websites are still unreachable after being taken offline as a precaution. This happened after a leak in the programming language PHP. For example, the website overheid.nl is still unreachable, as is the site of Meld Misdaad Anoniem. The sites of 113 and Centrum Seksueel Geweld were offline until late, but became reachable again during the night. A spokesperson for the <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> ministry says it is not yet clear when overheid.nl will be available again. Some sites take longer to update their systems and are therefore not yet online. More than a hundred municipalities, provinces and water boards use the council system Notubiz for distributing official letters. That organisation's website is online, but not every component can be used by municipalities or provinces. Official documents from, among others, the municipalities <entity id="org:gemeente-s-gravenhage">Den Haag</entity>, <entity id="org:gemeente-almere">Almere</entity>, Breda, <entity id="org:gemeente-haarlem">Haarlem</entity>, Den Bosch and Delft, and of the provinces <entity id="org:provincie-overijssel">Overijssel</entity>, <entity id="org:provincie-gelderland">Gelderland</entity> and <entity id="org:provincie-fryslan">Friesland</entity>, cannot be viewed. NotuBiz wants to test tonight first whether the updates have been applied properly and expects all pages to be available again tomorrow morning. Update A programming language is a language with which programmers can build websites, apps and software. Around 70 percent of all websites worldwide use the programming language PHP or a variation of it. That is why so many websites went offline today, including internationally. At 16.00 yesterday afternoon the organisation behind the programming language PHP carried out a security update that users could install. As a result, websites could start up safely again. Many sites are back online, but for some others that is not the case. Internationally too, websites went offline as a precaution. Besides the Netherlands, government websites in Belgium, Finland, Germany and France could not be used. For Belgium and France that is still the case. After the American organisation behind PHP, the PHP Foundation, announced yesterday that it would carry out a security update today, hackers seized on the announcement to locate the vulnerability and spread information about it. The information could have been misused; malicious people could have broken into websites using the programming language to steal customer data. In 2024 there were already signs that something was wrong with the PHP programming language. But other, more concrete problems overshadowed the signs, the PHP Foundation writes on its own site. Then the first vulnerability was found on 11 August by researchers from the security company Calif in cooperation with OpenAI. A special AI model was used for that. The second vulnerability was discovered on 24 August by security company Wiz, which is owned by Google. No indication of misuse According to the PHP Foundation, there are for now no signals that the vulnerabilities in the programming language have led to misuse of companies via their websites. The Dutch <entity id="org:nationaal-cyber-security-centrum">NCSC</entity> and the American CISA, both specialised in cybersecurity, confirm this. They say they have seen no active misuse of the vulnerability.

title: US withdraws part of embassy staff from Saudi Arabia after deadly Houthi attacks
lead: The American Department of State has ordered part of the diplomatic staff and their family members to leave Saudi Arabia. This concerns 'non-essential personnel' of the American embassy in the capital Riyadh and the consulates in the country. This decision follows a series of deadly attacks in the country by the Iran-backed Houthi rebels from neighbouring Yemen. There is fear that the conflict that flared up again this summer will escalate further. Civilian casualties Saudi Arabia supports the internationally recognised government in Yemen and is therefore targeted by the Yemeni Houthi fighters. Recently the Houthis have stepped up the violence, by their own account as retaliation for attacks on Houthi targets in Yemen. In a new travel advice the American Department of State says: "Iran-backed Houthis are carrying out hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure. This has led to civilian casualties and serious disruptions to travel. There is a risk that these hostilities will quickly escalate beyond the immediate area." According to American government sources of news agency Reuters, family members of embassy staff in other Gulf states will also have to leave. The ministry said nothing about that. International airport Among other things, airports in Saudi Arabia and power plants were targeted by the Houthis this month, with deaths as a result. For example, last night at an attack on an airfield in Dammam one person died and eight others were injured. The international airport in Riyadh was also hit this month. News agency AP reports that yesterday planes again took off and landed at the airport in the capital Riyadh. Major airlines such as Lufthansa and Air France have for now cancelled their flights to Riyadh until mid-November. Saudi airlines did operate flights yesterday. British fighter jets This week it became known that the United Kingdom is coming to Saudi Arabia's aid. The British Air Force will protect Saudi airspace against Houthi attacks. The country is sending, among other things, several Typhoon fighter jets. According to the British Ministry of Defence, this is a mission with a defensive purpose: the fighter jets will not carry out attacks. The support follows a request from the Saudi government. The United Kingdom has for some time been giving Saudi Arabia defensive support in the fight against the Houthis. For example, Saudi combat aircraft can use British tanker aircraft to refuel in the air.

title: North Korea warns South Korea: propaganda loudspeakers at the border almost ready
lead: North Korea says it has loudspeakers ready along the entire border with South Korea within a few days. That announcement was made by Kim Yo-jong, sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong-un. The threat of new propaganda speakers seems to undo the progress the South Korean president has made in reducing tensions with the neighboring country. Reducing those tensions was an election promise of Lee Jae-myung, who has been president of South Korea since June last year. K-pop and crying animals: Until early August 2025, loudspeakers stood on both sides of the border, used for psychological warfare. From South Korea, criticism of the North Korean regime and K-pop music blared. In response, sounds of crying animals and banging gongs came from the North Korean speakers. To reduce tensions, South Korea switched off the loudspeakers on 11 June last year. A day later North Korea did the same. Then South Korea began removing the speakers at the border in August. North Korea again followed that example. Landmines: Now those speakers are partly returning and tensions have risen again. Kim responded with her statement to remarks by a special adviser to President Lee. This adviser on defense policy had accused North Korea of planting landmines that injured South Korean soldiers, and had called on the country not to escalate further with loudspeaker broadcasts. Kim spoke of "new countermeasures" along the entire border and added that North Korea will continue strengthening the border. North Korea's warning does not necessarily mean the loudspeakers will be switched back on, says Lim Eul-chul of Kyungnam University in Seoul to news agency Reuters. However, he says this raises the question for the South Korean <entity id="org:regering">regering</entity> of whether the rapprochement policy should be continued.

title: Three dead in storms and flooding in southern France
lead: Three people have died and one person has been injured in heavy rainfall and flooding near Marseille in southern France. The authorities of the Bouches-du-Rhône department announced this. The storm hit the region on Tuesday. According to the regional authorities, the water level has risen to "unprecedented levels". The municipalities of Saint-Martin-de-Crau and Arles have been hit by a power outage since the storm, which may last a long time, the regional government warns. In addition, several roads in the region remain closed and rail traffic is still disrupted in some places. There are also faults in the telephone network, making communication difficult in areas without power. In Saint-Martin-de-Crau, 250 people have been housed in emergency shelters. Drowned Among the victims who died, according to the newspaper La Provence, are an 86-year-old woman and a 26-year-old woman. They reportedly drowned in a basement in Lançon-Provence. In addition, a 75-year-old man died in Saint-Mitre-les-Remparts. According to the mayor of the town, he was swept away by the current and his body was found later that morning. The authorities speak of "considerable material damage". An assessment of this is still ongoing.

title: Number of new businesses rises sharply, over 8 in 10 are zzp'ers
lead: The <entity id="org:zbo-kamer-van-koophandel">Kamer van Koophandel</entity> (KVK) recorded the number of startups in the Netherlands in the third quarter of this year rising by over 15 percent compared with the same period last year. This is the strongest increase in years. Mainly the number of sole proprietorships increased. Of all 62.395 'starters', as the KVK calls them, over eight in ten are zzp'ers. The number of self-employed people without staff is therefore 20 percent higher than a year earlier. "Despite discussions about bogus self-employment and measures to curb the use of zzp'ers, this form of entrepreneurship remains an important part of the economy", the KVK writes. Bogus self-employment occurs when someone is a zzp'er on paper but in practice does the same work as an employee. Bankruptcies At the same time, fewer businesses stopped. In the third quarter, 36.610 businesses were dissolved, 4,3 percent fewer than a year earlier. The number of bankruptcies rose slightly, by just under one percent. In total, on 1 October over 2,6 million businesses were registered with the KVK. That is 1,5 percent more than a year ago. For ten years politics has struggled with the zzp rules. The new Zelfstandigenwet, due to take effect in 2028, is meant to put an end to this. Five questions and answers on this:

title: Tensions rise between the Philippines and China over the South China Sea
lead: The Philippines and China are on a collision course over claims to island groups and reefs in the South China Sea. China claims almost the entire area and regularly has collisions with neighbouring countries that also claim parts of it on the basis of the law of the sea. Manila and Beijing have been quarrelling for years over the Spratly Islands and Scarborough Shoal. Now a new potential conflict zone seems to be emerging: the Batanes Islands, the northernmost province of the Philippines. The location is strategic, about 200 kilometres from Taiwan. Diplomatically, tensions are also rising, after statements by the Chinese ambassador last week. Ambassador Jing Quan said China could "easily win" a war, which Filipinos see as a threat. Quan has since been called in by the Philippine Department of Foreign Affairs. Claims to the Batanes Islands This summer a group of Chinese scientists concluded that the Batanes Islands "are a natural geographical extension of the island of Taiwan". Beijing sees Taiwan as part of China and is therefore now also claiming the Batanes Islands. The islands are not particularly impressive. Only three of the ten are inhabited, with just over 19,000 residents. Among them are mainly fishers, farmers who grow sweet potatoes and some hotel owners serving the roughly 13,000 tourists per year. It is mainly the location that makes a geopolitical impression: in the Luzon Strait, which would give the Chinese navy direct access to the Pacific Ocean, military experts say. The Chinese scientific claim was immediately rejected by the Philippines. According to the Department of Foreign Affairs, sovereignty over the Batanes Islands is "settled and the discussion is closed". Filipino historians stress that the islands have been part of the archipelago since the 18th century, when the Spanish colonised them. In 2016 the Permanent Court of Arbitration in <entity id="org:gemeente-s-gravenhage">Den Haag</entity> rejected Chinese claims in the South China Sea, after the Philippines had brought a case. China refuses to recognise the ruling. There is no legal basis for China to claim the Batanes Islands, but by raising it, the claim can start to sound legitimate, says Harvard scholar of Taiwan Studies Felix Brender to Channel News Asia.
