In the evening the family informed the police about the messages. Hajar's body was found last Friday evening in a suitcase in the water at Amsteldijk in Amsterdam-Zuid. The exact circumstances are still unclear, but the police are certain it was a crime. Vulnerable person: It is now clear that Hajar was a vulnerable person who often left home and was untraceable for long periods. On the weekend she was killed, she left with a suitcase. She did that more often, reports Het Parool. Hajar was also reportedly found at night last May in the porch of a house in the Amsterdam neighbourhood De Pijp. According to the resident, Hajar then made a "psychotic impression". On that occasion too she had a suitcase with her. Earlier this year Hajar was also missing for a time, after which she later turned up in Portugal. Suspect arrested: The man with whom Hajar cycled towards Buitenveldert on Sunday 4 October was arrested on Tuesday in the North Holland village of Spierdijk after he had abused his foster father, possibly with a hammer. Abdi A. is of Somali origin and has lived in the Netherlands since he was six. He now has a residence permit for an indefinite period. He grew up with a family in the North Holland <entity id="org:gemeente-koggenland">gemeente Koggenland</entity>, where the village of Spierdijk also lies. He had not lived with that family for some time. According to the police, A. had no fixed residence or place of stay. Today A. was brought before the investigating judge at the Amsterdam court. He will remain in custody for another fourteen days. The Somali is suspected of the murder or manslaughter of Hajar, of concealing her body, of attempted murder or manslaughter of his foster father, and of threatening a woman in Spierdijk. 'Leave the family alone': The family's lawyer says the bereaved wish to be left alone and asks that their privacy be respected so they can grieve. For now they also do not want to answer questions, because the investigation is still ongoing and they do not want to disrupt it. "If the family in the future feels the need to come out with a statement, it will take that initiative itself," said the lawyer. Urgent disappearance: Hajar's disappearance was initially not classified as urgent. One day after the report, on Monday evening 5 October, the police decided to do so after all. At that point there had still been no contact with Hajar since her messages, so the family's concern had grown, the police write. To protect the privacy of the bereaved, the police do not comment on why the disappearance on Sunday 4 October was not immediately classified as urgent. In an internal email from police chief Peter Holla, which AD first published, it says that the police acted "carefully and thoroughly" in the case. Holla stands behind the decision to classify the disappearance as urgent only a day later. In the email he emphasises that Hajar had already died when the police were informed.

title: First cargo of Trump and Putin's diesel deal on its way to New York
lead: A tanker carrying 40,000 tonnes of Russian diesel is on its way to the United States. The tanker Agioi Fanendes, sailing under the flag of Malta, is still in the Baltic Sea. The ship left the Russian port of Primorsk yesterday and is expected to arrive in New York on 7 November. The diesel on board is the first cargo of the hundreds of thousands of tonnes of diesel that Russian President Putin promised President Trump on 9 October. Trump hopes that the supply of diesel from Russia will bring down diesel prices in the US, preferably before 3 November, when interim elections will be held there. Due to the high diesel prices worldwide, farmers and transport companies in the US have been hit hard in particular. The prices are so high because of the war in the Middle East, which began in February with Israeli and American attacks on Iran. Americans are currently paying 5.61 euros per gallon (3.79 liters) at the motorway. That is 2.43 euros more than two years ago. Two days after the diesel deal became known, analysts in the British newspaper The Guardian said that the Russian diesel will have "little effect" on American motorists and businesses. The quantity would be too small for that. Furthermore, it is a question whether Putin can keep his promise, given the damage that oil refineries there have suffered in the war. 3 million tonnes per month With the American-Russian 'diesel deal' a line was drawn through the ban on importing Russian oil products that Trump's predecessor Biden had introduced in 2022. Biden wanted to punish Russia for the Russian invasion of Ukraine that year and the subsequent war. It has been agreed that Russia will supply 800,000 tonnes of diesel until the end of next month. The Russian deputy minister of Defence Novak said that Russia is capable of supplying the US 3 to 3.5 million tonnes per month by the end of the year. Gift Ukrainian President Zelensky called the diesel deal a gift for Putin, because Russia can make good use of the oil dollars for the war against Ukraine. According to him, the deal is harmful for Ukraine, the US and the rest of the world. "Every easing of sanctions against Russia without a clear and lasting de-escalation agreement is a weakness," he said. According to him, Russia will respect America less, fight on longer against Ukraine and cause more damage to the world.

title: Truck with breakdown on A67 turns out to be carrying a stolen load of toothbrushes
lead: The Royal Marechaussee found a stolen load of electric toothbrushes and shavers in a truck on the A67 near Venlo last week. The stolen goods, with an estimated value of 90,000 euros, had been stolen earlier that night from another truck. Marechaussee officers saw a truck standing on the hard shoulder at junction Zaarderheiken on the night of 12 to 13 October. When an employee of the marechaussee came to check and offered help, the driver and his co-driver fled, L1 Nieuws reports. "They left the truck behind with its engine running. A search for the suspects yielded nothing," the marechaussee writes in a message on social media. False number plate The truck was taken to a safe location with the help of <entity id="org:rijkswaterstaat">Rijkswaterstaat</entity>. Further investigation revealed that the vehicle had false French number plates. It also became clear that the goods in the trailer had been stolen from another truck in Venlo that same night. The truck with the false plate, trailer and load have been seized. Because the vehicles turned out not to be officially registered, they have been declared forfeited. The rightful owner has filed a report and has since recovered the stolen goods.

title: Nepal becomes the first country to receive millions from climate damage fund after mountain disaster
lead: Nepal is the first country to receive money from a fund set up by the United Nations for poor countries suffering damage from climate disasters. The fund has pledged 20 million dollars (almost 18 million euros) in support to the country in South Asia, which was hit in August by a landslide in the mountains, followed by a devastating flood wave. More than 1400 people died in the disaster and more than 5000 are missing. The damage in the affected area runs into the billions. Nepal itself estimates it will need nearly 5 billion dollars for reconstruction. The pledged amount from the fund is therefore less than 0.5 percent of what the country thinks it needs. The pledged millions are nevertheless seen as a big step. It is the first request that has led to a pledge from the fund, which came into being between 2022 and 2024 with great pain and effort under pressure from the poorest countries, which are often hit hard by climate change. The maximum amount that can be paid out has also been pledged immediately. High costs The dissatisfaction with the climate damage fund has been great for some time. The poorer countries have been pointing out for years that the fund falls short. Rich countries have pledged only a relatively small amount, which adds up to around 822 million dollars. The World Bank, which manages the fund, reports that around 516.5 million dollars of this has now been received. That sounds like a substantial amount, but experts warn that it is far too little if the fund is to be tapped consistently after disasters in poorer countries. The damage, as also seen in Nepal, quickly becomes very large after a serious natural disaster. Moreover, the 20 million that can be paid out at most is rarely sufficient to do more than make a small contribution to reconstruction. 2.8 billion dollars "The tragedy in Nepal shows us in a devastating way that events caused by climate change are becoming more complex and more severe", says Georg Børsting, co-chair of the fund's board. He refers to findings from scientists who also see the hand of climate change in the natural disaster in Nepal. "Unfortunately, these challenges will only grow in the future." Since its establishment, developing countries have submitted around 176 requests to the fund, together worth around 2.8 billion dollars. So far, not a cent has been transferred to affected countries. Incidentally, that is not yet the case for Nepal with the pledge either. However, the country can now submit an official application for the pledged amount.

title: France deploys 70,000 police officers tomorrow as new protests are announced
lead: The French authorities will deploy 70,000 police officers tomorrow to keep order in the country now that new demonstrations have been announced. The trade unions are once again taking to the streets to protest against government policy, the state of education and the rising cost of living. The government wants to prevent last week's situation from happening again. Demonstrations in several cities then escalated into riots, looting and arson. There is fear that other groups may also take to the streets. The yellow vests, a protest movement that arose in 2018 out of discontent with rising fuel prices, have said they will be taking part. Yesterday President Macron said that protests not organised by the trade unions are banned. 'We tolerate nothing' The French Minister of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> Nuñez says today that calls for looting and violence have come from the far-left fringe. According to him, that group is mainly targeting government buildings. "We are prepared to act extremely hard tomorrow and we tolerate nothing." To relieve the police at certain moments, the army will also be deployed on the streets. Trainee officers will also be deployed. Several cities have also announced area bans. A curfew also applies in several places. Many shopkeepers are taking measures and preparing for another weekend of chaos and vandalism. In Paris, among other places, shopkeepers are deciding to close their shops and board them up. Various cultural institutions such as the Louvre have also been closed. Marine Le Pen congress The authorities are also concerned about the annual congress of Marine Le Pen's far-right Rassemblement National in Orléans this weekend. Left-wing and anti-racist groups have announced counter-demonstrations. Because of the recent violence, Le Pen has risen in the polls. Presidential elections will be held in France next year. In France people have been protesting against government policy for weeks now. Last Saturday the protests completely got out of hand. Riots broke out across the country, including in Paris, Lyon, Lille, Nice, Bordeaux and Marseille. At least 1,500 shops were looted, there were arson attacks, and confrontations took place between masked youths and the police. In the end more than 2,300 people were arrested. A day later President Macron lashed out hard at the rioters. He said that anyone who wants to bring down the Republic will be held to account. Italy also preparing Authorities in Italian cities are also preparing for new protests and possibly new riots. In Milan, Rome and Turin among others, security measures have been stepped up. Protests against the high cost of living also got out of hand in Italy in recent days, with vandalism and looting. According to Italian media, the train stations around Milan are being closely guarded and monitored. The aim is to prevent young people from flocking to the city en masse. In addition, demonstrations in the city centre are banned and the army will be deployed. Some 500 soldiers will travel to Milan.

title: Ebola appears in Nigeria: infection via Uganda's airport under investigation
lead: The African Union's public health organisation CDC is investigating how the Ebola virus ended up in Nigeria. The West African country reported this week its first Ebola infection . Until now, only Central and East Africa had been affected on the African continent, with the Democratic Republic of Congo as the epicentre. The infected woman now in a hospital in the Nigerian city of Abuja appears never to have been in the Democratic Republic of Congo. She was in Uganda, however, but there the authorities declared the country Ebola-free at the end of July, after she had had twenty infections at the start of the outbreak. To find out how the woman became ill, the African public health organisation is now investigating whether the infection could have occurred at Uganda's international airport. Via that airport in Entebbe, earlier this month a Kenyan who had worked in the Democratic Republic of Congo travelled to the Kenyan capital Nairobi. He died there a few days later of Ebola. Contact at Entebbe airport? According to epidemiologist Dr. Mankoula of the CDC, the patient from Nigeria and the Kenyan man were both travelling through the Ugandan airport on 3 October. "Was there any touching or contact between the two at the airport? That is one of the theories currently being investigated", said Mankoula. Uganda is not happy about this. The country depends to a large extent on tourism, and it was precisely a positive moment that the outbreak there had ended a few months ago. The country earlier said the patient had not caught the virus in Uganda, but that the woman had also been in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Today the <entity id="org:ministerie-van-buitenlandse-zaken">ministerie van Buitenlandse Zaken</entity> in Switzerland stated that this is not correct and that she was only in Uganda. Switzerland is involved because the woman has Ugandan nationality but is married to a Swiss diplomat stationed in Nigeria. The couple travelled to Uganda for a visit. New infections in Kenya: Nigeria immediately began tracing at least 44 contacts of the woman, to prevent further spread. The Nigerian Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) stated that genetic research is also being carried out to help understand whether the infection is linked to other cases. In Kenya there are now eight new infections: four family members and four healthcare workers who had been in contact with the patient who died. The Kenyan <entity id="org:regering">regering</entity> says there is no spread in the community. This variant of Ebola has thus now appeared in four African countries. Isolated cases have also occurred in Europe, such as an aid worker in France and an aid worker in the Netherlands who had worked in East Congo. Temperature checks: African ministers of the affected countries meet next week to discuss how they can cooperate to stop the spread. At airports in the countries, travellers' temperatures are already being checked and people must wash their hands and fill in health declarations. Even so, the sick Kenyan got through. He had already been treated in eastern Congo, but it is unknown whether he knew he had Ebola when he travelled. In Congo, since mid-May, at least 9500 infections have been confirmed and more than 4600 Ebola patients have died. This makes it the deadliest outbreak ever in the country. There is not yet an approved vaccine or medication for the current Bundibugyo variant of the highly contagious infectious disease.

title: Ceasefire in Ukrainian city Olesjky, arranged by Melania Trump
lead: A ceasefire is coming into effect in the Ukrainian city of Olesjky and its surroundings. The ceasefire is intended to give non-military personnel from Ukraine and Russia the opportunity to offer help to civilians who are trapped there and to evacuate them if they wish. The ceasefire takes effect on 27 October. Two days later the humanitarian operation begins, for which several days have been set aside. The White House says that President Trump's wife Melania brought about the ceasefire. "The situation in Olesjky is appalling," the First Lady says in a statement from the White House. "Olesjky is a front-line city that is facing a disaster. The people who stayed behind are mainly elderly people who urgently need medical help, medicines, food and clean water." The Ukrainian ombudsman has confirmed the agreement. In a video message he says the operation will proceed in three steps: first a ceasefire, then the delivery of humanitarian aid and then the evacuation of civilians who wish to leave the city. Russia confirms agreement <entity id="org:nationale-ombudsman">De ombudsman</entity> describes the implementation as "extremely challenging". Russia has also confirmed the operation. The Russian army commander Gerasimov said that Russian troops will temporarily stop firing along the front in the Kherson region and will grant safe passage to humanitarian aid convoys. Last week President Trump said that Ukraine and Russia had agreed not to attack each other's energy installations any more. Ukraine knew nothing about this, and Russian attacks on installations in Ukraine continued. Olesjky has been a front-line area since the start of the war in Ukraine in 2022. The city has been occupied by Russia and most of the residents have fled. Famine threatens the approximately 6,000 civilians who have stayed behind. The Russians have placed landmines around the city and on the access roads, making supplies impossible. The residents have been short of food and medicines for months. The city is also suffering from a lack of electricity, heating and running water. American media organisation to monitor According to the First Lady, teams of non-military personnel will go from door to door to determine what help is needed, under the supervision of an "impartial" American media organisation. It must ensure that "the wishes of every family" are respected. She does not say which organisation that is. According to Melania, it is obvious that without her intervention it would have been impossible to bring humanitarian aid and evacuate the elderly. She used the contacts she made through the reunification of Ukrainian children with their parents for the agreement. Russia had abducted those children. In the statement the First Lady says she expects residents to want to leave both for areas controlled by Russia and for Ukraine. Kremlin spokesman Peskov also says that residents who wish to leave will have that opportunity. He just would not say whether they will be taken to Russian or Ukrainian territory. Plea from the Pope Pope Leo XIV also called for a ceasefire in Olesjky. Last week, while he was still in hospital, he telephoned President Putin. He expressed his concern about the humanitarian situation and called for a truce so that humanitarian aid such as food and medication can be delivered. Putin reportedly responded positively to the Pope's words. "It has been agreed to work together on this," the Kremlin said at the time.

title: Racially motivated attack in France under investigation, Macron speaks of terrorism
lead: France has reacted with horror to the attack in the Parisian suburb of Trappes. The 39-year-old gunman Kevin T. opened fire there this morning on passersby at random. Minister Nuñez of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> calls the shooting a "terrorist crime". One person died and five others were injured. Three of them are in life-threatening condition. The gunman may have had a racist motive. The terrorism department of the French Public Prosecution Service (OM) says it is investigating this. According to the OM, a second suspect has been arrested alongside the suspected gunman. It concerns a direct family member of T. Girl hit eight times The suspect opened fire on passersby in Trappes, southwest of Paris, from his grey Renault Clio around 10 a.m. In about twenty minutes he first made victims in Trappes and then, a little further on, also in La Verrière, after which he was boxed in and arrested around 10:20 a.m. in the town of Coignières. At the arrest, the police found the machine gun, tear gas grenades and gloves in his car. According to the French newspaper Le Monde, he has thirteen convictions to his name, for various offences, including shoplifting, drug use and driving under the influence. The most recent conviction dates from 2013. He was not registered on the so-called Fiche S, the French list for radicalised and state-dangerous persons. He was also not known to the domestic security services. Among the victims was a 12-year-old girl who was hit by eight bullets. The victim who was shot dead was a 26-year-old man. The mayor of Trappes, Ali Rabeh, points to the background of the victims: the girl was, according to him, shot "because she is a person of colour". The man who was killed was of African descent. Mayor Rabeh told the press that the attack was "probably Islamophobic". He also spoke of "racist undertones". 'A turning point in the Republic' French President Macron visited Trappes this afternoon. There he spoke with eyewitnesses, police officers who arrested the suspected gunman, and firefighters who had still tried to resuscitate the fatal victim. Macron expressed his horror at the intentions and deeds of the suspect: "A man was killed this morning by one of our fellow citizens on the basis of a racist ideology." And: "This is the first time that a planned terrorist attack has been carried out to kill our compatriots, our children, because of their skin colour or the faith they adhere to. This is a turning point in our Republic." He also referred to the tensions the country has been struggling with for some time. "Let us not allow this terrorist attack to divide us." The French OM stated in a press release that when the police wanted to enter T.'s house to search it, officers came across gas cylinders and electricity wires, possibly to cause an explosion. The house search has not yet been completed, according to French media. 'Shot by a coward' The French TV channel RTL spoke with the mother of the 12-year-old girl who was fired upon. She said she was "in shock". "How can anyone do this to a child? My daughter is 12 years old. She went to the swimming pool and was shot by a coward." At the moment RTL spoke to the mother, her daughter was being operated on. Before she went into the operating room, the mother was able to see her briefly. "She was conscious. She is strong. We are going to pray for her. She has injuries to her liver, kidneys, arms and thighs. Her condition is serious." The girl was wearing a headscarf when she was shot, according to the mother. "Maybe that is why he attacked her. She is a child who was born in France, in Trappes. She has the right to build her life here." Her condition is now stable, French media write. Warning against incitement More politicians have spoken out. Minister Darmanin of Justice speaks of a "horrific attack". François Hollande, former president of France, wrote on social media about "an atrocious act that bears the stamp of racist hatred". The Council of Muslims calls it a "horrific attack", but warns of the consequences of "ongoing inflammatory statements".

title: Police start investigation into possible hack at parent company of Albert Heijn
lead: The police this week started a criminal investigation into the cyberattack at Ahold Delhaize, the parent company of Albert Heijn. The police confirmed this to NOS. The retail group filed a report last week, after the police and the <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> had urged the company to do so. Ahold Delhaize took its systems offline as a precaution this month after a hack. That led to empty shelves. Several distribution centres came to a standstill. There were also problems with home deliveries, and the website and apps were unreachable for days. Today it became known that customers can have their groceries delivered to their homes again. A few days ago this was already possible for a limited group of regular customers. Investigation ongoing According to Ahold Delhaize, so far there are no indications that sensitive information has been stolen from customers, employees or suppliers. However, its own investigation reportedly showed that "malicious actions by third parties" took place. The police make no statements about the criminal investigation "because it is still ongoing". A spokesperson does not want to say on which day the investigation started, as he sees no "added value" in it.

title: Building under construction of more than ten floors collapses in central Nairobi
lead: A building of more than ten floors that was under construction has collapsed in the Kenyan capital Nairobi. Almost nothing is left of it, apart from stacked slabs of concrete and rubble. People are feared dead. Residents say they have been in phone contact with people who are trapped. News agency AP spoke with a plasterer who was working on the fourth floor of the building. He heard screaming and saw other construction workers rushing outside, shouting that the building was going to collapse. "I was the last one to get out before it collapsed and the whole area was filled with dust." He thinks not all of his colleagues could escape. It is unknown how many people were inside. The residential tower collapsed out of nowhere: It happened around 1 p.m. local time. An AP reporter saw that rescue workers initially had to do the work without heavy machinery. Only after an excavator arrived could they reach the ground floor and the basement. An electronics shop, a butcher and a greengrocer were already located there, while construction was still continuing higher up. It is not yet known how the building could collapse. The regional <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> is investigating, reports the Kenyan news website The Star. "The owner and those who gave permission for the construction will all be properly prosecuted," says the police. Looters: The building stood on a busy shopping street. Rescue work is being hampered by looters who want to profit from shops in the area. The police are using tear gas to drive them away. A police commissioner says the collapsed remains of the building are pressing against a building next to it. That may therefore cause that one to collapse as well. According to AP, buildings under construction collapse more often in Nairobi. Supervision of compliance with building regulations is said to be falling short.

title: Stormy weather mainly causes disruption in the south of the country
lead: The forecast stormy weather has so far led to only limited nuisance in the Netherlands. In Limburg, weather institute <entity id="org:koninklijk-nederlands-meteorologisch-instituut">KNMI</entity> has issued code yellow due to severe gusts of wind. These are expected from this evening and have speeds of 75 to 90 kilometres per hour. The ANWB says that due to the stormy weather the evening rush hour was very busy, with a lot of recreational traffic. There were 330 kilometres of traffic jams. In various places across the country, the severe gusts caused damage to vehicles and trees. For example, in the centre of <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">Amsterdam</entity> a tree blew over and landed on a driving car. Because the driver became trapped, emergency services were called. The driver has since been freed from the car unharmed, reports Het Parool. Most reports of wind nuisance came from the south of the country. The Limburg broadcaster L1 reports that in Nuth a large tree fell on a car. One person was injured and the road has been closed. In <entity id="org:gemeente-maastricht">Maastricht</entity>, cars were damaged this afternoon when a tree toppled over. In Wittem, in the same province, a tree also blew onto a road. A woman on a moped reportedly was hit in the process. She has been taken to hospital. In Breda, a tree fell onto a lorry that was standing at a traffic light. Strong wind expected The KNMI expects the gusts in the southeast and southwest to move later this evening to the east and west of the country. The Wadden Islands and the IJsselmeer area will probably face the strong wind tonight. In Limburg the wind is already decreasing this evening, and in the southwest and west this will happen tomorrow morning. During the course of Saturday evening, the KNMI expects new gusts of 75 to 90 kilometres per hour, particularly in South Limburg and the coastal areas. Because tree branches may break off, this could possibly lead to traffic disruption. Nuisance in Belgium In Belgium the wind has already caused more damage. Trees blew over in various places there and damage occurred to homes, reports the Belgian broadcaster VRT. In Brussels three people were injured when a tree fell on a terrace. In a place nearby, someone was hit on the head by a branch. In a number of provinces in Belgium code orange applies due to the severe gusts of wind. There are delays on various train routes, and because of the storm the Flemish Traffic Centre said traffic was "exceptionally" busy during the evening rush hour. Around 17.00 there were nearly 400 kilometres of traffic jams, mainly around Antwerp and Brussels. According to the centre, countless reports are coming in of uprooted traffic signs and fallen trees. The storm is also causing disruption in the air. A flight that was on its way from Marseille in France to Brussels was diverted to Schiphol. France and England Storm Austen has already caused problems in France this afternoon. The storm made landfall in Brittany this morning, where local weather stations measured gusts of up to 160 kilometres per hour. In several French coastal regions the power went out and code orange applied until 20.00 this evening. In England, code orange has also been issued for Cornwall and Devon, in the southwest of the country. There, gusts of 130 kilometres per hour were measured. In Cornwall, just over 13,000 addresses were without power as a result of the stormy weather.

title: Are smart devices still safe to use after the PHP flaw?
lead: Questions about cybersecurity have been pouring in since the vulnerabilities in the PHP programming language became known. Through the PHP flaw, servers and websites could be taken over and misused. PHP may also be present in a doorbell with a camera, a smart washing machine or a robot vacuum cleaner, warns the <entity id="org:nationaal-cyber-security-centrum">NCSC</entity>. Think carefully about whether it is really necessary to connect all those devices to the internet, advises Juriaan Spierenburg of the NCSC. Around 30 percent of Dutch homes have one or more household appliances that can connect to the internet, according to market research agency Multicsope. Are these devices still safe to use? Install updates According to the NCSC, the risk that the PHP flaw will be misused on a large scale is smaller than initially thought; it is difficult to simply misuse it. Even so, the advice remains to update your devices, apps and websites regularly. The risk that smart household devices will be hacked is not very high, experts say. The attacker would need to be able to make a connection with the product. "You could say that most smart devices have a phone to call out, but they don't have a number that can be called, so you run little risk", says Daan Keuper of security company Computest. Most smart devices are not directly connected to the internet. "They hang on the wifi and there is a router in between", says cybersecurity expert Ralph Moonen. So with those products you can only connect if you are logged in to the same wifi network. Breaking into a smart washing machine via the router seems unlikely to Michel van Eeten of TU Delft. "There is almost no PHP in routers." Obligation of the supplier According to Moonen, smart doorbells can almost not be hacked via the consumer's network. "It is more likely that the hack runs via a server of the manufacturer. Then the vulnerability does not lie with the consumer", he says. Responsibility for that lies with the manufacturer, Spierenburg of the NCSC knows. "Suppliers have an obligation to keep their own systems secure. There is new legislation for that too, the Cyber Resilience Act." He expects that most suppliers will comply with it. "But I don't know whether all suppliers from all kinds of countries will be updated in the short term." Switching off devices What can pose a risk at home is so-called Network Attached Storage (NAS), a hard drive connected to your network. "With that you can log in from your holiday address via your computer or phone to upload photos", says Moonen. "So with that you can connect from outside." Spierenburg of the NCSC warns about outdated devices. "They may use an old version of PHP and they no longer receive updates." It is almost impossible for consumers to find out whether their products were made with PHP, the experts state. "It is very technical", says Moonen. "Many companies don't even know themselves where they use PHP." If you still want to take security measures, make sure you install all updates. "And that all smart devices are only reachable via your own home network. Otherwise, consider setting up your own firewall or VPN for them", says Spierenberg. If necessary, you can switch off a device that is reachable via the internet for a few days, says Van Eeten. "And wait and see what the supplier does."

title: Meghan Markle's brother finds child pornography at their father's, police start investigation
lead: Meghan Markle says she is "deeply saddened" by the allegations that her father possesses hundreds and possibly even thousands of images of child abuse. The police in the Philippines have started an investigation into Thomas Markle senior, after the authorities received a tip from one of his sons. The British newspaper The Sun writes that this 60-year-old son, Thomas Markle junior, was searching for a phone in his father's house in the Philippine city of Cebu. He went through all kinds of boxes and found a phone with a 15-minute video of naked young girls. The son kept searching and found more shocking material: video footage showing sexual acts and also books full of photos of undressed girls. Among other things, he saw those images on a laptop in a room he recognised from his father's house in Rosario, Mexico, where his father lived between 2016 and 2025. According to him, the victims were often no older than 10 or 11. Completely upset The Sun writes that the son told friends he was completely upset by his discoveries. He had looked after his father for years after his father was struck by a stroke in 2022. Markle junior adds to The Sun: "I had no choice but to report my father." He went to the police in the Philippines and also reported his discovery to the FBI and the police in Pennsylvania, where his father had lived. He also contacted an American non-profit organisation whose aim is to track down missing children. He says he does not want to speak to his father anymore in any case. "I supported him, cared for him and helped him for years, but now it's over. I will never speak to my father again, unless I am called to testify against him." Meghan broke with him earlier Thomas senior can also expect little support from his daughter Meghan. Through a spokesperson, the wife of the British Prince Harry says she has been affected by the news about her father. "My thoughts go out to all children who may have suffered harm." She also says she hopes people now understand why she broke with her father earlier and why he is not allowed to see her two children. In her statement she points out that in 2018 the British police had already informed her of "disturbing and shocking allegations against my father". What those allegations were at the time is not clear. 'Sick lies' Other family members are reacting furiously to the allegations against Thomas Markle senior. A 61-year-old half-sister of Meghan has spoken to The Daily Mail about "sick lies". According to Samantha, her brother Thomas is after money and has been carrying on a vendetta against their father for years. "There is absolutely no basis for these disgusting allegations. My brother wants to ruin our father. Shame on you, brother." Thomas senior is currently staying in a nursing home in Florida, where he is recovering from his stroke. An investigation into him may also follow in America.

title: Number of students at the Frisian teacher training has doubled this year
lead: The number of students starting the Frisian teacher training this school year has more than doubled compared with previous years. According to the university of applied sciences NHL Stenden in <entity id="org:gemeente-leeuwarden">Leeuwarden</entity>, the language policy of the province of <entity id="org:provincie-fryslan">Friesland</entity> is bearing fruit. For a long time it seemed the teacher training would disappear. The Nijmegen researcher Geert Driessen concluded in 2016 in his study of the language that it is 'five minutes to midnight for Frisian'. He feared that Frisian would 'die a slow death'. The province of Friesland did not want this to happen and took action. Together with primary schools, a pilot was started to anchor the language in education again. This resulted in a Taalplan Frysk 2030 that was launched at the beginning of this year. Many career changers: This year 34 students started the Frisian teacher training at the university of applied sciences. According to Omrop Fryslân, that concerns two full-time students, sixteen who take the training part-time, and another sixteen who follow part of the training as a minor. Among the part-time students are many career changers, people who switch to another profession during their career. "When you are 16 or 17, you often don't yet know that you want to become a Frisian teacher", says Babs Gezelle Meerburg of the teacher training, explaining that high number. The doubling of the number of students is a "clear signal that interest in Frisian in education is growing", says Gezelle Meerburg. She attributes this to the province's language policy. All children at primary or secondary schools in Friesland have been learning Frisian since this school year and are encouraged to use it actively. From 2030 it must also be offered as an examination subject at all Frisian secondary schools. More teachers needed: "The province wants a continuous learning line with the Taalplan Frysk for everyone who wants to learn Frisian", says Gezelle Meerburg. "So from two years old until eighty. Teachers are needed for all of that." To ensure this, a recruitment campaign was set up. That campaign will run for several more years. So in a few years there must be dozens of new teachers. This school year also showed that for the first time in fifteen years, three students had started the Frisian programme at the university in <entity id="org:gemeente-groningen">Groningen</entity>. Gezelle Meerburg takes into account dropouts and people who go to work in another sector. Ultimately, perhaps half of the new students will work as teachers, she thinks.

title: Dozens of churches sign up with Actie Onderdak to accommodate status holders
lead: Dozens of churches in the Netherlands have already signed up to temporarily accommodate status holders. They have heeded the call the joint churches in the Netherlands issued last Tuesday. According to Actie Onderdak, twenty churches across the country are working to set up the accommodation. People are already laying flooring there, placing beds and checking the sanitary facilities. Forty other churches have signed up and are still considering taking part. According to the organisation, sign-ups continue to come in. More than a hundred people with a residence permit have already found somewhere to go and are able to leave their asylum reception centre. Soft landing in municipalities The campaign focuses on status holders, asylum seekers with a residence permit who are still in an azc. The intention is for them to be accommodated in the municipality where they are ultimately supposed to get a home. John van Tilborg of Actie Onderdak tells news agency ANP that the churches' accommodation helps with a soft landing in society. In this way, status holders who are still waiting for housing in an azc could be given shelter for three months. Creating space in azc's Under the rules, asylum seekers who have been granted a residence permit should be allocated a home in a municipality. Due to the housing shortage, this often does not succeed, so they stay longer in an azc. As a result, the azc's remain full and there is a shortage of places for new asylum seekers. With the initiative, the churches want to create space in the asylum reception centres. This should help reduce pressure on the overcrowded registration centre in Ter Apel, where people sometimes have to sleep outside. The <entity id="org:zbo-centraal-orgaan-opvang-asielzoekers">Centraal Orgaan opvang asielzoekers</entity> (COA), which is involved in working out the plan, will ensure that status holders can actually move on to a new place after three months, according to the Council of Churches.

title: KLM fined by US government for flying over Iraq
lead: KLM is fined 320,000 dollars by the US Department of Transportation because the airline flew through the airspace over Iraq hundreds of times. This was in breach of the rules the airline had agreed with the American airline Delta Air Lines, with which KLM works closely. So-called codeshare agreements are arrangements in which two or more airlines share flights under different flight numbers. It can mean that a passenger flies under a Delta Air flight number, while on that same flight there are also passengers flying with a KLM flight number. In this kind of codeshare agreement, airlines also make arrangements about restrictions on the use of airspace. Sticking to the rules: The flights for which KLM was fined were operated between January 2022 and May 2025. The aircraft flew lower than 32,000 feet (almost 10 kilometres) above Iraqi territory, while that was not allowed. The US aviation authority FAA has set safety rules for airspace in locations where safety may be at stake due to, for example, military conflicts. "Under the Trump administration, following our safety rules is not optional," says Transport Minister Duffy. "We will not hesitate to hold an airline that does not comply with the rules accountable." It is unclear why KLM did not comply with the rules. Also fine for Air France: Air France, KLM's sister company, has also been fined. That airline flew over the area thirty times while that was not allowed. The fine results from a settlement agreement that AirFrance-KLM reached with the American ministry. The total fine the company must pay is 425,000 dollars. The first part of 265,000 dollars must be transferred within sixty days. The remaining amount only has to be paid if the airlines fly through the prohibited airspace again within a year. "We remain committed to complying with all applicable aviation regulations," says a KLM spokesperson. According to him, "Air France and KLM have taken measures to strengthen compliance with airspace restrictions for the future."

title: Dead and hundreds injured by severe hurricane Champi near Taiwan
lead: Taiwan has been hit by a severe hurricane. It has been named Champi and killed a man on the island. At least 500 people have been injured. Also, 77,500 households were left without power. The dead man was on the beach and was swept away by high waves. Rescue services later found him, but by then he had already died. The waves are said to have reached some 21 meters high. Champi is also called a super typhoon, a hurricane of the highest category with wind speeds of more than 250 kilometers per hour. Wind speeds of about 298 kilometers per hour were measured with Champi, with gusts up to 362 kilometers. Record storm in 2026 The storm grew over the past few days into one of the most powerful of 2026 so far. It also disrupted air traffic in Taiwan. According to local media, nearly a thousand flights were canceled today. Almost all schools and businesses were also closed. Images of the damage from super storm Champi in Taiwan: Although the hurricane has passed Taiwan, the Taiwanese weather service still warns of heavy rainfall. Following the hurricane, some 900 millimeters of precipitation could still fall tomorrow morning. For comparison: in all of 2025, 673 millimeters of rain fell in the Netherlands. Champi is now moving further north and will reach the west coast of China and southern Japan over the course of the weekend. Exceptionally warm seawater Champi was able to grow into such a severe hurricane due to a combination of circumstances. The seawater in the Pacific Ocean is exceptionally warm, there was little wind at various altitudes, and there was little dry air. Those are excellent ingredients for a storm to quickly gain strength.

title: Trump intervenes in Alaska elections because of two Dan Sullivans on the ballot
lead: Even before they have taken place, the upcoming elections in the US are already threatening to cause trouble. The American Department of Justice has filed a lawsuit to be able to block the result in Alaska. President Trump says the lawsuit came about at his request. On the ballot in Alaska, two candidates have almost the same name. They are the sitting Republican senator Dan S. Sullivan and another Republican, Dan J. Sullivan, who is running as an independent candidate. The latter is unlikely to win the election, but could siphon off crucial votes from the sitting senator. The ministry under Trump has no confidence that voters can find the right Republican candidate on the ballot. Voters may get confused, the ministry argues. Dan J. Sullivan has always denied that he is running in order to frustrate his namesake. Neck-and-neck in Alaska From Trump's perspective, that is very undesirable, because Alaska looks set to become a neck-and-neck race between the Republicans and the Democrats. In polls for the elections of 3 November, Senator Sullivan and Democrat Mary Peltola are level. The lawsuit is meant to prevent Republican senator Dan S. Sullivan from losing. If that happens anyway, the ministry wants the certification of the result to be postponed. According to an expert who spoke to The New York Times, Trump's involvement is very unusual in American politics, certainly so shortly before the elections. Republicans have already taken unusual measures this year to keep control of Congress, such as redrawing electoral districts to increase the chance that a party member wins. The result in Alaska could be decisive in the midterm elections and determine which party gets the majority in <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Senaat</entity>. Want to know more about the Congress elections? In the video, our correspondent explains what is at stake. You can also listen to the new episode of the Amerika Kiest podcast via <entity id="org:zbo-nederlandse-publieke-omroep">NPO</entity> Luister or via another audio platform .

title: Seal center postpones planned bankruptcy filing by a week
lead: The Pieterburen Seal Center is postponing its bankruptcy filing by a week. Following the distress call of a week and a half ago, new options have emerged to keep the center open anyway. According to the organization, 1.25 million euros in donations have since come in. A petition to save the center has also been signed more than 100,000 times. The board of the World Heritage Wadden Sea Centre (WEC), of which the well-known seal center has been part since moving to Lauwersoog, stresses that a solution is not yet certain. Next week, talks will be held with various parties in the hope that enough money becomes available to save the seal rescue from ruin. "The financial situation remains fragile", the WEC writes in a statement. The Pieterburen Seal Center was founded in 1971. From 2006 to 2014 it bore the name of its founder Lenie 't Hart. The center takes in sick and weakened seals. Once they have recovered, they are released back into the Wadden Sea. The organization is facing financial problems. Due to the construction of a brand-new facility in Lauwersoog, which turned out much more expensive, the center is almost 3 million euros short. Also, far too few visitors are coming.

title: Israeli army raids several places in the West Bank
lead: The Israeli army has over the past day begun raids in several places in the occupied West Bank. According to the army, soldiers are active at dozens of locations. Israel expects the "anti-terror operation" to last several days. The raids are a response to a shooting yesterday morning. Two Israeli soldiers were killed in it. According to Israel, the perpetrators were Palestinians from the area of Hebron. The Palestinian news agency Wafa reports that soldiers in the west of Hebron have demolished a car parts shop and other business premises. Israel says it is "demolishing illegal structures that may pose a security risk at the place where the confrontation took place". Earlier in the day a Reuters reporter also reported the demolition of buildings. Residents said the premises had nothing to do with the attackers. In a village north of the city, Israeli soldiers have used tear gas against several people, Wafa reports based on local sources. South of Hebron, Israeli forces reportedly invaded a refugee camp. Closure The news agency also reports that the army has entered the city of Nablus. Israeli soldiers reportedly entered the city with a large number of military vehicles and carried out raids in various houses. Earlier in the day roadblocks were already set up around Hebron. Prime Minister Netanyahu had ordered the army to close off the city and prepare for a full closure of the West Bank. According to the Israeli army, residents can leave the area via three designated exits, after they have been questioned. People who "arouse suspicion" will, according to Israel, be handed over to the security forces. Israel has occupied the West Bank since 1967. Around three million Palestinians and 700,000 Israeli settlers live in the area. Parliamentary elections are held in Israel on Tuesday. The main election theme is security.

title: Fire destroys wholesaler in Rotterdam, fire brigade busy for hours
lead: A building on an industrial estate in the northwest of Rotterdam where a fire broke out overnight must be considered a total loss. That is reported by the Rotterdam-Rijnmond safety region. The approximately 4500 square metre building houses, among other things, a wholesaler of food products from the Middle East, Turkey and North Africa. The fire broke out around 01:50, and at 02:15 the fire brigade reported that flames were coming out of the building. According to the fire brigade, the building can no longer be saved. In the course of the morning the fire brigade is mainly still extinguishing around the building that is on fire, where cars and vans are parked and other buildings are located on the Zestienhoven industrial estate, close to Rotterdam The Hague Airport. The fire brigade expects to be busy extinguishing for hours yet, says the safety region . NL-alert A lot of smoke is released by the fire. Around 05:45 an NL-alert was sent with the advice to close windows and doors. The area has also been closed off to traffic. Across Rotterdam, soot and rubber particles are being found due to the shifting wind. The safety region advises that places where children play outside should first be cleaned and that the paws of pets that have been outside should be wiped before they go inside. No one was injured in the fire.

title: Major fire destroys Eagle's Nest, former teahouse of Adolf Hitler
lead: In southern Germany a large fire has raged through the Eagle's Nest, the former teahouse of Adolf Hitler. Flames are no longer visible on the outside of the building, which has been largely destroyed. The building stands at 1834 metres altitude on the Kehlstein, an Alpine mountain near the town of Berchtesgaden. According to the Bavarian broadcaster, the famous structure was already engulfed in flames when the fire brigade arrived at 21.52 hours. At 04.40 hours it was still burning. The cause of the fire is still under investigation. Police suspect the fire was set deliberately and arrested a suspect shortly after it broke out. It is still unclear whether that person has anything to do with the fire. Around 200 emergency workers were involved in fighting the fire, the Bavarian police reported. No one was injured. The Eagle's Nest, actually called Kehlsteinhaus, was built specially for the German dictator. It was completed in 1938 and was intended to receive and impress (diplomatic) guests. Contrary to common belief, the building was not a gift for Hitler's fiftieth birthday. The building offers a panoramic view of part of the Alps and the Austrian city of Salzburg. To make it accessible, a 6.5 kilometre mountain road with five tunnels had to be built. A 124 metre high lift was also installed. Hitler lived nearby, at his country retreat the Berghof. Other prominent Nazis, including Hermann Göring and Albert Speer, also had houses in the area. Hitler himself rarely visited the building. It was mainly used by people from his immediate circle, including his beloved Eva Braun. Unlike the Berghof, the Eagle's Nest was spared from Allied bombing during the Second World War. In 1952 a restaurant opened in the building. There is also an exhibition about its history. The Eagle's Nest remains a popular tourist destination.

title: Pepper spray and wooden boards: Paris braces for new day of action
lead: Today there are again large protests in France. In Paris, where many acts of vandalism were committed last week, shopkeepers are preparing for another day of violence. Along the route of the demonstration the sound of circular saws and screwdrivers can be heard everywhere. Shopkeepers are having their shopfronts covered with wooden boards. A familiar sight in eastern Paris, where there are often demonstrations that frequently get out of hand. "We have been busy for days," says Khaled, who with his colleagues is boarding up a neighbourhood supermarket. "Since Sunday we have boarded up shops that were looted and vandalised last week. After that we could get on with the preparations for the new day of action." Melanie has a kitchen shop close to Place de la Nation. She was able to call in her own installers to board up her shop. That was lucky, because other shopkeepers could not find anyone or could not afford it. Also, the wooden boards are almost impossible to get hold of now. "Very sad that we have to do this to protect our belongings, our work," she says. Disaster prevented The French government is doing everything it can to prevent a disaster like last Saturday. Today 70,000 police officers are on duty. Leave has been cancelled and, according to French media, even trainee officers and border guard staff are being deployed. The police have twenty armoured vehicles and fifteen water cannons ready today. Even so, shopkeepers and hospitality entrepreneurs have no confidence that this can prevent new looting. At the weapons shop on Rue du Faubourg-Saint-Martin there is a constant coming and going of entrepreneurs who want to be prepared themselves. They mainly buy tear gas canisters and pepper spray. "You have to aim straight at the face," the seller advises. Eric comes to collect two canisters to protect his wife's jewellery shop. He would have preferred larger models, but those were sold out. "You try to prevent the worst. The services that should protect us apparently cannot do that. That is why we are looking for other means." The government advises entrepreneurs to hire private security guards. He does not understand that. "Surely the state should protect people's safety and belongings? That is what I have always thought." France Info spoke to the owner of a Vietnamese restaurant who bought a stun gun after she was attacked last week. Eric has heard from colleagues who have hunting rifles ready. You can have those with a hunting licence. "One shot of buckshot, you hit a lot with that. But it is a shame we have to talk about this. Hopefully it won't be necessary this weekend." Banned demonstrations To prevent new unrest, the authorities have banned a large number of demonstrations. In many cities demonstrations are not allowed. In Paris only the demonstration by the trade unions is permitted, because the unions have their own stewards and a lot of experience with demonstrations. The yellow vests movement and the students were not organised or barely organised. What began as protests by students escalated into riots and looting. What exactly happened? Trade unions and left-wing political parties have strongly criticised President Macron's decision. They call it an erosion of the democratic right to demonstrate. "It is an authoritarian flight forward of power. This is typical of a police state. It is not for the government to decide who may demonstrate," writes the radical left party La France Insoumise. The route of the demonstration in Paris is also being debated until the last moment. The route the yellow vests wanted to take was banned. On Thursday the unions appeared to have permission for a march from Place de la Bastille to Place de la Nation. Contractors are still busy boarding up shop fronts there until the last moment. But last night the police also banned this route. The police propose a march along the edges of the city centre, along boulevards with far fewer shops and restaurants, but also far less visibility. The unions are furious about this. They are trying to reverse this with an urgent court case. For Melanie of the kitchen shop it makes no difference whether she had her shop boarded up for a demonstration that will not pass there anyway. "Then we'll just keep the wooden boards for the next day of action."

title: Self-built saloon of Limburg shooting club burns down at opening party
lead: The wooden clubhouse of shooting club Davy Crockett in Meterik was destroyed by fire last night. This happened during the opening party of the saloon, which had been built by the members themselves. Dozens of people were present at the party, according to the Limburg broadcaster L1. Everyone was able to leave the building in time. A local journalist says about one hundred firefighters were deployed to fight the fire. There was no ammunition in the building. The Davy Crockett Saloon had only been handed over two weeks ago. The building had been built by the members over a period of seven months to mark the shooting club's 60th anniversary. "It is something to be proud of that we built this all together," said chairman Jan Joosten. An open day was supposed to take place today.

title: Wake-up call 24/10: Protest day in France • Winter time begins
lead: Good morning! Large protests are expected in France again, and tonight you can sleep an hour longer, because winter time begins. At 03.00 a.m. the clock goes back one hour. As a result, it gets light earlier in the morning and dark earlier in the evening. First, the weather: this morning there will be some showers at first, but they will move north and after that the sun will shine at times. This afternoon the cloud cover will increase again and by the evening there will be more rain and wind. Are you heading out today? Here you can find the overview of traffic jams and roadworks, and here you can see the situation on the railways. What can you expect today? What did you miss? In Germany a fire has broken out at the Eagle's Nest, the well-known teahouse of Adolf Hitler. One person has been arrested. It is unknown whether that person started the fire. The Eagle's Nest was completed in 1938 and was intended to receive (diplomatic) guests. Hitler himself did not often go there, but people in his circle did. Other news from overnight: And then one more thing: Yesterday was 23 October, the day in 1964 when judoka Anton Geesink won Olympic gold in Japan. Footage of that event is iconic, but in the archive of Beeld en Geluid we found more remarkable and rarely shown material from before and after the tournament. In the videos below you can see how Geesink was interviewed just before and just after he became Olympic champion: Have a nice day!

title: Podcast: the revelation of serious child abuse at 'Huize Soria'
lead: A Nieuwsuur report about terrible abuses at a Dutch youth care facility in Spain is causing a great deal of reaction. Besides shocked responses that reach the editorial office, new victims are also coming forward who want to tell their story. "The count is rising," says Lune van der Meulen in the podcast. She worked with her colleague Yoeri Vugts on this file for more than a year. This episode of De Dag can be listened to via NPO Luister and all other podcast apps. Do you like it? Then don't forget to subscribe. Municipalities and child protection agencies for years sent young people to this so-called family home in Spain, Huize Soria, when things were not going well for them in reception places in the Netherlands. Knowing that the treatment methods there were 'different'. But how different, that is now becoming clear. Four young people told their story on camera for Nieuwsuur. Reactions? Email dedag@nos.nl Presentation and editing: Elisabeth Steinz Editorial team and final editing: Judith van de Hulsbeek

title: All hands on deck for Republicans in final stretch before elections
lead: With ten days to go until the Congressional elections, tension is rising in the United States. At stake is a majority in the two chambers of Congress: the House of Representatives and <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Senaat</entity>. The Republicans are doing everything they can to keep their majorities, and the Democrats in turn are going to the limit to win them. And they see an opportunity: in several states, polls suggest a surprise may be possible. These elections are for Democrats the chance to pull power in Washington back toward themselves a little. Over the past two years Donald Trump and his Republican party, with their majorities in Congress, have left their mark on the country and the world. The actions of the president are for many people a reason to go and vote in the midterm elections. Midterm elections are often seen as an indirect referendum on the president. The president's party almost never manages to keep control of Congress. With his low approval ratings, these elections also come at a bad moment for Trump. Listen to our podcasts about the midterms in the US. In the run-up to the midterms on 3 November, NOS colleagues at the Washington bureau are making new episodes of the podcast Amerika Kiest. Listen to them via <entity id="org:zbo-nederlandse-publieke-omroep">NPO</entity> Luister or via another audio platform. The Democrats therefore hope to strike, but getting both the House and the Senate in their hands is a challenge. Especially in the Senate it is far from a foregone race. The Democrats must take a seat from the Republicans in at least four states, including states where Trump won by more than 10 percentage points two years ago. Texas from red to blue? One of those states is Texas. There the Democrats hope to have an asset in 37-year-old James Talarico to turn the always red Texas blue. The former teacher is trying to show that current politics is not there for the ordinary Texan, that the divisive force in politics does not sit in "left or right, but above and below". The upper layer of society earns too much and has too much power, is his story. His opponent Ken Paxton is an example of that, Talarico argues. Paxton, who is backed by Trump, is the state's attorney general and is dogged by scandals. He narrowly survived an impeachment procedure over suspicions of corruption. It does not help Paxton and his fellow Republicans that people see Donald Trump getting ever richer from the presidency. Although the American economy is growing and, for example, a lot of investment is going into artificial intelligence, Americans feel the pain in their wallets. Trump started the war with Iran, for example, which sent fuel prices soaring. Diesel in particular is expensive, and it is felt especially by farmers: their agricultural machinery runs on diesel. That is partly why Republicans in 'red' states with a lot of agriculture, such as Kansas, Iowa and Ohio, suddenly look vulnerable in these elections. The import tariffs Trump introduced and the resulting trade war with Canada are not helping either. For many states Canada is the most important export country. What else is at stake in the elections? Our correspondent explains it in this video: The Republicans have realised that it is all hands on deck. Trump is spending large sums of money to support Republican candidates who are in a tight spot, for example with extra TV spots. In addition, he and Vice President Vance are travelling the country separately to enthuse voters. Trump flew to Kansas, South Carolina, Florida, Iowa and North Carolina this week. He won those states earlier with ease, but now even Trump sees the situation there as gloomy. On the stage in North Carolina, for example, he accidentally admitted that the Democratic candidate would probably win a Senate seat. "And that is bizarre," he said. The Republican candidate Michael Whatley had to listen to it from the hall. Democrats as a bogeyman: To mask those vulnerabilities, the Republicans try to portray their opponents as a radical party with overly liberal ideas. They create a 'woke' bogeyman for conservative voters. In addition, they suggest that if the Democrats gain power, the US will pursue a communist course. That comes out mainly in the tight Senate election in Michigan. There the Republicans hope to defeat progressive Democrat Abdul El-Sayed and so take a seat from the Democrats. The Muslim El-Sayed is being used there as a scapegoat. That is accompanied by personal, Islamophobic and racist attacks. For example, El-Sayed is said to be a terrorist and a 'jihadist fool'. It shows that the Republicans shun no controversy and go to the limit to keep the Senate. The Democrats think they have a good chance of winning one or two majorities in Congress, but it has happened more than once that a predicted landslide did not materialise. The Republicans therefore hope that the results after 3 November will look rosier than the current polls.

title: Sytze Faber (89), former CDA Tweede Kamer member and journalist, has died
lead: Former CDA Tweede Kamer member and journalist Sytze Faber has died at the age of 89 in <entity id="org:gemeente-leeuwarden">Leeuwarden</entity>. His family reports this in an obituary in NRC . Faber grew up in a Frisian, Reformed environment, studied political science at the Vrije Universiteit in <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">Amsterdam</entity> and earned his doctorate in 1974. After working in academia for years, he became a Tweede Kamer member in 1977. The Frisian entered <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> in on behalf of the ARP, which merged into the CDA in 1980. He was regarded as a left-wing CDA member and had major objections to the formation of <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>-Van Agt I, consisting of his CDA and the VVD. Independent spirit Nevertheless, he did not belong to the so-called loyalists, a group of initially six CDA members from the left wing of the party, who took a critical stance toward the coalition agreement with the VVD. As a result, they held an important position of power, since the Van Agt I cabinet had a narrow majority with 77 seats. Faber did not join them, in keeping with his independent spirit of not binding himself to groupthink in advance. Still, he regularly deviated from the party line. He played an important role in the debates on the constitutional revision and in 1979 opposed the placement of American cruise missiles in the Netherlands together with nine other CDA members. He combined his membership of the Tweede Kamer with the shared editor-in-chief position at the Friesch Dagblad. "That combination with politics was completely normal back then: it was the pillar era and a pillar newspaper," Faber said earlier this year in an interview with that newspaper. When Ruud Lubbers became prime minister in 1982, Bert de Vries succeeded him as CDA parliamentary group leader. Within the party, unity was pushed more strongly, so the position of critical Kamer members came under pressure. Faber remained a Tweede Kamer member until January 1985. Mayoralty Afterwards he was appointed mayor of the Drenthe municipality of <entity id="org:gemeente-hoogeveen">Hoogeveen</entity>. In 1988 Faber became involved in an incident in <entity id="org:gemeente-zwolle">Zwolle</entity> after a pub visit. There Faber and the <entity id="pos:burgemeester-smallingerland">burgemeester van Smallingerland</entity>, Bert Smallenbroek, had an argument with a group of young people. Smallenbroek reportedly came to blows with them. The then minister of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> Van Dijk even looked into the matter, also known as "the Zwolle affair". After an investigation by the national police detectives, he concluded that the mayors had not committed any criminal offences. He considered the incident "too trivial, too petty" for dismissal, but did reprimand them because they had damaged the dignity of their office. Smallenbroek, who died last year, resigned. Faber retained the confidence of the municipal council and ultimately remained <entity id="pos:burgemeester-hoogeveen">burgemeester van Hoogeveen</entity> until 1998. After leaving Hoogeveen, Faber returned to the Friesch Dagblad as a political columnist, where he wrote a weekly column. In 2007 he wrote the book De wet van de koestal. Gereformeerden in <entity id="org:gemeente-s-gravenhage">Den Haag</entity>, about the formation of the Balkenende IV cabinet. Faber died last Thursday in Leeuwarden.

title: Former mayor Schuiling files cassation appeal in masturbation case
lead: Former <entity id="pos:burgemeester-groningen">burgemeester van Groningen</entity> Koen Schuiling is appealing to the Supreme Court against his conviction for masturbating in his car. He announced this in a statement on the podcast Belleman & Van Dop. The appeals court in <entity id="org:gemeente-zwolle">Zwolle</entity> last week sentenced Schuiling to a fine of 250 euros for what is officially called public indecency. The appeals court considers it proven that he masturbated in his car in March 2024. Schuiling has always denied this. He claims he had stomach ache and therefore had his trousers open and rubbed his stomach. For that reason he is fighting his conviction again. "I have always been clear about what was going on that evening and what I was suffering from," he says in a statement read out by court reporter Saskia Belleman. "It is incomprehensible to me that the court does not believe that. This case is about a relatively small fine, but the consequences for me are immense." Schuiling says the conviction feels unjust and that he is still determined to get his rights. He also thanks people for "the many expressions of support". Statement by truck driver The former mayor was found guilty of public indecency by the Zwolle district court last year and was fined 250 euros. He appealed that conviction, but the appeals court has now convicted him too. The statement of a truck driver plays a major role in the case. He has stated that on 25 March 2024 he was driving alongside Schuiling on the A7 between Groningen and Hoogezand. There he saw that Schuiling had the interior light of his car on and was masturbating. The truck and the car drove near each other for a while. Both the district court and the appeals court consider the driver's statement reliable because he always testified in detail and consistently. Schuiling, on the other hand, has not always given the same account, the court said last week. First he said he needed to urinate, later he stated that he had stomach ache. Stepped down early Schuiling was mayor of Groningen between 2019 and 2024. He announced his early departure in September 2024, when the suspicion against him was not yet public. About this departure, Dagblad van het Noorden later wrote that minister Uitermark of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> had put pressure on him because of the masturbation case. If he did not step down himself, the ministry would suspend him. The ministry tells the NOS that Schuiling did not leave under duress.

title: Trees blown over by Austen, more strong gusts of wind tonight
lead: The stormy weather of last night has caused damage in many places, especially in the south of the Netherlands. In the provinces of Limburg and <entity id="org:provincie-noord-brabant">Noord-Brabant</entity> there have been many reports of trees and branches blown over onto roads. As far as is known, no one has been injured. The <entity id="org:koninklijk-nederlands-meteorologisch-instituut">KNMI</entity> warning for strong wind has since been lifted. Tonight there is again a chance of strong gusts, this time in the coastal areas. Storm Austen already caused disruption in France and England yesterday morning. In weakened form the low-pressure area then moved over the Netherlands. The strongest gust measured was in <entity id="org:gemeente-vlissingen">Vlissingen</entity>: 91 kilometres per hour. There were also strong gusts along the coast of <entity id="org:provincie-zuid-holland">Zuid-Holland</entity> and in the south of Limburg. Larger incidents occurred in Volkel and <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">Amsterdam</entity>, among other places. In Volkel a falling tree made a large hole in the roof of a farmhouse. A greenhouse also shattered, writes Omroep Brabant. In Amsterdam a tree fell onto a moving car. The driver escaped with a fright. In many places the fire brigade was busy removing trees and branches from roads. In <entity id="org:provincie-gelderland">Gelderland</entity> the fire brigade removed scaffolding sheets in at least two places that threatened to blow away, writes Omroep Gelderland. Code yellow again tonight. The wind has eased in the meantime. A few showers are still passing over the country, after which the sun will regularly shine. Tonight the wind will pick up again. From 22.00 code yellow applies in <entity id="org:provincie-noord-holland">Noord-Holland</entity>, <entity id="org:provincie-fryslan">Friesland</entity>, <entity id="org:gemeente-groningen">Groningen</entity> and the Wadden area. The KNMI warns of strong gusts, on Texel and <entity id="org:gemeente-vlieland">Vlieland</entity> possibly up to 100 kilometres per hour. The gusts will continue throughout Sunday.

title: Mummies no longer displayed in Glasgow museums for privacy reasons
lead: Two museums in Glasgow, Scotland, have stopped displaying mummies. In one case the human remains have been removed from the display entirely, and at the other the mummy is now covered with a cloth. A third museum also plans to make changes. The change came to light when a visitor wanted to show his daughter the mummy of the priest Nekht at the Kelvingrove Museum. They found only a card saying that "human remains have been removed as a sign of respect". A head, foot and hand that were mummified, which had also been on display, turned out to be gone too. "We believe that showing more respect to the deceased individuals means not displaying ancient Egyptian human remains," the museum said in the British press. An exception can be made if there is "consent from the deceased or their next of kin", but of course that is not possible in this case. Hidden under a cloth. A second museum in the city was found to have made changes for the same reasons as long ago as August last year. The mummy of Sjep-En-Hor at the Hunterian had always been displayed in her richly decorated sarcophagus, but is now hidden from view with a cloth. The coffin can still be seen by visitors. The Hunterian says it "aims to become a more ethical institution" and therefore believes that the woman, who died 2600 years ago, "deserves privacy after her death". Sjep-En-Hor had been on display since 1820. The mummy of Nekht, around 4000 years old, was excavated at the beginning of the last century. Museum operator Glasgow Life says it plans to remove some items from the St. Mungo Museum of Religious Life and Art as well. These include a coffin and several mummified remains. 'History hidden'. The changes stem from tightened guidelines from the International Council of Museums, ICOM. These state that, "for the sake of human dignity", the display of body parts should be approached with restraint. "Decisions on this must always be made in consultation with descendants or the communities from which they originate." Critics speak of political correctness gone too far. "History is being hidden," fears Conservative politician Murdo Fraser. "Glasgow's museums should be showing off our history, not secretly removing it because of the latest trend in political correctness." "British museums are too busy censoring and filtering history to meet the demands of woke fanatics," says Chris McGovern, a history adviser under former prime minister Thatcher, speaking to the Daily Mail. "Soon the Bayeux Tapestry won't be allowed to be shown either, because there is too much violence, death and corpses to see." Mummy issues. Other museums say in the British media that they will not follow Glasgow's example. National Museums Scotland, which includes several popular institutions in Edinburgh, has no plans to make any changes. The renowned British Museum also has no "mummy issues", as the Daily Mail puts it. A spokesperson for the London museum says that human remains can be shown "with respect, care and dignity" as long as sufficient context is provided. The museum points to the educational, historical and scientific value of such items. There are therefore no plans to change anything. The Glasgow museums have not yet said what will happen to the mummies. A spokesperson says the museums are open to sending them back to Egypt. 'Choices change'. Museums in the Netherlands are familiar with the debate. The Rijksmuseum van Oudheden in Leiden says that it always handles these objects "carefully, with respect for human dignity", but "considers it important to tell historical stories, not only about life, but also about death and the treatment of the dead body". Allard Pierson in Amsterdam has chosen to display the mummies in such a way that visitors can choose not to look. It admits that "the choices we make today (or yesterday) are not necessarily the choices we will make in the future".

title: One-way traffic on IJssel lifted again after rain in recent days
lead: Ships on the IJssel between IJsselkop and Zutphen can for the time being sail in both directions again.
