In France, demonstrations have taken place in recent weeks over social unrest about President Macron's policies. It began with protests by pupils for improvements in education. Meanwhile the movement has broadened, and trade unions, farmers and the 'yellow vests' have joined.

title: Many dozens of flights from Schiphol cancelled due to strong wind
lead: Many dozens of flights from Schiphol airport have been cancelled due to strong wind. Mainly flights of airline KLM have been cancelled. Flights of Easyjet have also been cancelled. Due to the strong wind not all runways are available and fewer aircraft can take off and land, says a spokesperson for Schiphol. Passengers should therefore take cancellations and delays into account. Until 17.00 this afternoon it concerns nearly eighty cancelled flights, according to data on the Schiphol website. It mainly concerns European flights, for example to Paris, Manchester, Hamburg and Stockholm. Flights to Schiphol have also been cancelled, although a number is missing. On the website of the Stockholm airport, for example, it can be read that a KLM flight to Amsterdam has been cancelled. Nuisance and damage Last evening and overnight the strong wind, caused by the low-pressure system Boelo, led to nuisance and damage in several places, including fallen trees. For example, a tree fell onto the railway between Lochem (Gelderland) and Goor (Overijssel). No trains are running there this morning. In central Amsterdam a tree fell onto a moving car. The driver remained unharmed. Boelo Boelo is the second storm of this season after Austen. It is one of seven names that the weather institute <entity id="org:koninklijk-nederlands-meteorologisch-instituut">KNMI</entity> provided, selected from the names that were submitted. The East Groningen name Boelo was submitted by a Groninger "in whose family this name has existed for generations", the KNMI reports.

title: Will Brazilians choose Lula after all, or will the Bolsonaros expand their power further?
lead: The second and decisive round of the election in Brazil today is a tense contest between sitting leftist president Lula da Silva (80) and radical right-wing candidate Flávio Bolsonaro (45), son of convicted former president Jair Bolsonaro. But whoever becomes Brazil's new president after today, the power of the Bolsonaro family has already grown considerably. After the first round of the election three weeks ago, not only Bolsonaro's radical right Partido Liberal ( PL) gained considerably in the National Congress, several family members also personally won seats. The wife of former president Bolsonaro, Michelle, gained a seat in <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Senaat</entity>. Bolsonaro's son Carlos also won a seat there. The former president's youngest son, Jair Renan, won in the Chamber of Deputies. And Jair Bolsonaro's younger brother, Renato, also won a seat there. What does this mean when so much power lies with one family? Military dictatorship Former journalist Ricardo Moraes (74) experienced up close the repression that prevailed during the military dictatorship in Brazil, which lasted from 1964 to 1985. "There was no freedom back then. During my student days the military had all the power and they had surrounded our university. They wanted to arrest the students because we were demonstrating. We wanted free elections and a return to democracy. I then fled and went into hiding for a while," he recounts. With the prospect of a possible victory for Flávio Bolsonaro and the strong political power of his family, he is worried about democracy in his country. Bolsonaro has announced that he will pardon his father, former president Jair Bolsonaro, if he wins. He also wants to amend the constitution and carry out reforms within the Supreme Court. "That is why Lula must win, because it is dangerous if this family becomes so powerful, they could ruin everything in Brazil," says Vinicius Portella, the 25-year-old son of Ricardo Moraes. Electric shocks He grew up with his father's stories and photos from the dictatorship era. After his studies Ricardo Moraes became a journalist and worked for Brazilian newspapers. Press censorship prevailed and he was eventually arrested by the army and tortured for ten days. "I still remember how I was forcibly brought into one of the military's torture centres. I was put on a chair, the so-called dragon chair. A wooden chair, but the seat was covered with metal plates. I received electric shocks. An unbearable pain through my whole body," Moraes says. It is his father's experiences that made son Vinicius aware from an early age of the value of democracy. That was put at stake again in Brazil four years ago, after the 2022 elections. Storming of government buildings Bolsonaro then narrowly lost to the current president Lula da Silva, but refused to accept his defeat. Together with a number of senior officers he planned a coup, which was eventually called off at the last moment, as the Federal <entity id="org:politie">Politie</entity> discovered in an in-depth investigation. Supporters of Bolsonaro then stormed government buildings in the capital Brasilia and caused damage at, among other places, the Supreme Court. They received heavy sentences for this. Bolsonaro himself was eventually sentenced to 27 years in prison, which he is serving under house arrest for health reasons. A lot at stake That president Lula da Silva lost the first round was a shock for Vinicius. In all the polls Lula was actually ahead of Flávio Bolsonaro. "But we have now been woken up, because a lot is at stake. Young people are campaigning en masse. We talk in groups of five or six people with people on the street who are still undecided about who to vote for. Hopefully we can get them to vote for Lula," he says. Whether that will succeed is still an open question. Although Lula rose in the polls in recent days, Bolsonaro still appears to be the favourite of many Brazilians. They have placed their hopes precisely on the Bolsonaros and want to be rid of Lula and the Workers' Party. The result of the Brazilian election is likely to be known around 23.00 (Dutch time).

title: Groups of minors were deliberately out to cause unrest and violence, says Walibi
lead: The disturbances at the Walibi amusement park during the Fright Nights were, according to Walibi, caused by young people who had the deliberate aim of creating unrest. Last night groups of young people came to blows with each other and vandalism was committed. Footage circulating on social media shows groups fighting with each other and throwing things. The mobile unit (ME) was deployed to restore calm. The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> says when asked that no one has been arrested. People involved in the disturbances were, according to Walibi, taken outside with the help of the police. Calm then returned, the amusement park in Biddinghuizen reports. Walibi had specifically taken new safety measures this year to prevent disturbances like last year. Fights also broke out then. In the past, costumed actors have also had to deal with violence and boundary-crossing behaviour from visitors. Minors The disturbances of last night are, according to Walibi, mostly the work of "minors who deliberately come to provoke in places where many people gather, as we unfortunately also see happening in other parts of the Netherlands and Europe". The Fright Nights is an annual Halloween event that draws thousands of visitors. There are haunted houses and Scare Zones where costumed actors try to frighten visitors. Last night 20,000 visitors attended the sold-out event. Scare Zones closed The mood turned last night one hour before closing time, at 22.00 hours. The incidents began at the main stage by the Ferris wheel and moved toward the Hall of Fame at the entrance. Because of the fights, the Scare Zones were closed. "The emergency lighting came on and the actors were taken to the back," says the spokesperson. Walibi's Fright Nights continue today and next weekend. The spokesperson says when asked that the event is going ahead as normal today. When asked whether actors have withdrawn and visitors have asked for their money back, the spokesperson cannot give an answer. What do you think of the NOS app and website? What do we do well? What could be better? We would like to hear your opinion. Fill in the survey via this link.

title: Japanese prosecutors charge US serviceman with murder of 39-year-old woman
lead: A US serviceman has been officially charged with the murder and robbery of a woman on Okinawa. The woman was reportedly strangled with a telephone cord, Japanese media write. The 20-year-old Devin Jacob Ballard was arrested on Sunday 4 October. He allegedly strangled the 39-year-old Anna Yagi the day before in a hotel in Naha, the capital of the Japanese island. He is also said to have stolen her wallet and backpack. The marine was arrested after an officer saw him walking in a nightlife area in Okinawa City, about 25 kilometers northeast of Naha, that same day. His shaved head and the tattoos on his arms matched those of the man on the security footage, news agency Kyodo News reports. The serviceman is stationed at the US Futenma air base on the southern Japanese island chain. Because the American acted outside duty hours and was arrested outside the American base, the case is being handled by the Japanese authorities. According to Japanese media, the marine denied involvement in the case when he was arrested. Anger The case has caused great anger on Okinawa. Residents have long opposed the US military presence on the island chain, partly because of crimes that US servicemen are said to have been involved in. According to local authorities, the number of criminal cases related to US military personnel rose from about 40 in 2020 to 101 last year. This is not the first case of its kind. In 1995, a 12-year-old girl was raped by three US servicemen. This led to large demonstrations against the US military presence on the island. The three US servicemen received prison sentences of 6.5 to 7 years. There was also anger over the rape of a minor by a US serviceman in 2024 and how little was made public about the crime. The man was sentenced to five years in prison. The anger is not only directed at the US military, but also at the Japanese government. Critics accuse Tokyo of doing too little to prevent crimes by US servicemen, out of fear of damaging the important security relationship with Washington. The newly installed governor of Okinawa is also under close scrutiny. He travelled to Tokyo to express his displeasure, but has not yet announced any concrete measures himself. The governor is not a member of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP), but he does have ties to the party. US military The US military has announced new restrictions for servicemembers in response to the case, including a curfew. But on Okinawa, confidence in such measures is low. After earlier serious crimes, curfews, alcohol bans and stricter conduct rules were also introduced. These were often temporary and could not prevent new incidents. For many residents, the new case therefore underlines a problem that, in their view, has been inadequately addressed for decades.

title: Libris History Prize 2026 goes to Maite Karssenberg for the book Dubbelleven
lead: Writer Maite Karssenberg receives the Libris History Prize for her biography Dubbelleven. Geertruida Kapteyn-Muysken en haar rebelse levensfilosofie. The prize for the best history book of the year was presented by jury chair Frits Spits in a special broadcast of the VPRO radio programme OVT. Karssenberg receives 20,000 euros. 'Shockingly subordinate' The book exposes the "shockingly subordinate role of women in the 19th century", says the jury. Geertruida Kapteyn-Muysken lived from 1855 to 1920. She philosophised about a better world, but at the same time was a married woman with children who had to do the housework. The main character wanted to study and improve the world, but had to fight for her opportunities. Eventually she joined an international group of idealists, feminists and anarchists and rediscovered herself. What the jury finds especially fascinating about the book is the "completely original way" in which Karssenberg has shaped the biography, says Spits. According to the jury, the reader is taken along in her search for the radical thinker and feminist and in doing so gets to know not only Kapteyn-Muysken but also Karssenberg herself. Diaries and letters Maite Karssenberg (1989) is a writer and historian who works as a programme maker and interviewer. For the book she conducted extensive archival research, during which she came across three diaries and hundreds of letters that Kapteyn-Muysken left behind. "After her death she was praised as 'one of the most free and unprejudiced spirits' of the Dutch revolutionary movement, with an 'almost universal knowledge of the spiritual and social currents of our time'", Karssenberg writes about Kapteyn-Muysken on her website. Earlier she wrote the book Snijpunt Isfahan. Een zoektocht van vader en dochter. In it she travels with her father, who is obsessed with Islamic mosaics, to Iran. In Isfahan, the centre of Persian mosaic art, they search for a small factory that will carry out her father's design. On the journey, different worlds come together. Karssenberg received the VPRO Bagagedragerprijs for the idea for this journey. For a broad audience The annual Libris History Prize is intended for history books that appeal to a broad audience and is part of the Month of History. The prize is an initiative of, among others, Historisch Nieuwsblad and the Nederlands Openluchtmuseum. The other nominees were Isabel Casteels with De kronieken van de dood. Opstand en executies in de Nederlanden, Maarten Van Ginderachter with Arm Vlaanderen. Een wereldgeschiedenis. Honger, ziekte en globalisering in het midden van de 19de eeuw, Dik van der Meulen with Meester in het paradijs. Jac. P. Thijsse en het landschap, and Dik Verkuil with De ongenaakbare Bolkestein (1933-2025). Last year the prize went to Janna Coomans for her book Dievenland. Overleven in de Middeleeuwen.

title: Sinkholes in Rotterdam Crooswijk caused by underground leak
lead: Sinkholes have formed in pavements and streets at several locations in the Rotterdam neighbourhood of Crooswijk due to a water leak underground. According to the safety region, the leak has also flooded the crawl spaces of homes. The problems are occurring on the Crooswijksestraat and the Hendrikstraat. Due to the leak, sand is washing away, which has created the holes in the streets and pavements. The streets have been cordoned off. Drinking water shut off. Water has been cut off at several homes on the Crooswijksestraat so that water company Evides can repair the leak. The water in the crawl spaces must first be pumped out before the leak can be repaired, the safety region reports. Once that has happened, the homes will be supplied with drinking water again. Evides cannot yet estimate how long this shutoff will last. The work is expected to be finished this evening, writes regional broadcaster Rijnmond. The safety region advises residents to turn off all their taps. "This prevents possible leaks when you have water again."

title: Seat belts on several US roller coasters after fatal accident
lead: Amusement park operator Six Flags will install seat belts in three roller coasters at the company's amusement parks. One of those roller coasters is the Goliath near Atlanta in the US state of Georgia. Early October, a 42-year-old man died when he was thrown out of the roller coaster. Other people who were in the roller coaster were injured when they were hit by the man who fell out of it. At its highest point the attraction is 60 meters tall and goes 113 kilometers per hour. The other roller coasters where belts are being fitted are Nitro at Six Flags Great Adventure in the state of New Jersey and Raging Bull at Six Flags Great America in the state of Illinois. The belts supplement the existing safety restraints on the rides. Inspection reports The Goliath roller coaster, where the accident happened, is still closed. The same applies to other attractions in the company's parks. Six Flags says this is a precautionary measure. The company has not yet said when the roller coasters will reopen. After the fatal accident, Six Flags hired independent engineers and specialists to carry out inspections. They must also assess the safety procedures. The company says that the staff who operate the attraction are always trained in a classroom and on location. The Goliath also passed the annual inspection, according to reports from the authorities of the state of Georgia. Worn parts American media write about a report from this year that does mention a worn part on the Goliath. A shock absorber reportedly needed replacement. CNN reported this month that Six Flags has been accused in recent years of falling short in maintaining its amusement parks. The news organization saw in public documents and court files that there had been reports of a train derailment, defective safety restraints and injuries to visitors. Further investigation must establish what exactly caused the accident at the park in Georgia. Brain injury The incident this month was not the first time the company's roller coasters had been in the news. In September, Six Flags was sued by visitors who described brain damage after a ride on the X2 roller coaster. The company has since closed that roller coaster.

title: Voters queue for hours at embassy in The Hague: 'Want a new future for Serbia'
lead: Lines are long at the Serbian embassy in The Hague due to the parliamentary elections in Serbia. Eligible voters can vote at the embassy and thereby help determine whether autocratic leader Aleksandar Vucic must step down after more than ten years in power. The long queue in The Hague does not bother voters. "I waited three hours and it was worth it," says a woman. "If it were necessary, I would do it again." A mother and daughter from Nootdorp think some people may have to wait four or five hours. "But nobody considers that a problem," says the woman who is voting for family and friends in Serbia "who are still fighting hard for freedom of expression and more". Until ten years ago she lived in the Serbian capital Belgrade. "I hope that everyone I love in Serbia no longer has to be afraid or uncertain about his or her future." Although a man from Rotterdam finds every election important, this one is especially special for him. "I am so looking forward to these elections. This is now our only chance for a new future for Serbia." Voters from all over the Netherlands The voters have come to The Hague from all over the Netherlands. A woman from Groningen is also in line. "I travelled for three hours and am now standing in line for three hours." She wants change in her homeland. "Serbia is so corrupt now." A woman from Apeldoorn who sat on the train for an hour and a half agrees. "Young people eventually see no future in Serbia because of the corruption and cronyism." As a result they leave, she says. "Then a country empties out, and that is good for no one." Besides in the Netherlands, lines also form in, for example, Switzerland and Bosnia and Herzegovina. Early elections The 56-year-old Vucic held several ministerial posts on behalf of the Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) before he became prime minister in 2014. In 2017 he became president of Serbia. Last June he announced his resignation. A tactical step, because next year Vucic's second and final term as president would end. Vucic hopes that with early parliamentary elections he can become prime minister again, and thus stay in power after all. Long queues in The Hague: Opponents of Vucic have been calling for his resignation for more than a year and a half. The protests started after part of the roof of the station in the Serbian city of Novi Sad collapsed. Sixteen people died as a result. Demonstrators blame the accident on corruption within the government. Opponents also say that Vucic intimidates political opponents and restricts press freedom. Under Vucic's rule, Serbia has made hardly any progress toward joining the European Union. Student list Today's parliamentary elections are, according to polls, a neck-and-neck race between Vucic's SNS and the Student List, a party that emerged from the protests against the current <entity id="org:regering">regering</entity>. Turnout is so far higher than at the previous elections in 2023. At 14.00 hours, 46.4 percent of eligible voters had cast their vote, reports the Serbian public broadcaster <entity id="org:zbo-registratiecommissie-tandheelkundige-specialismen">RTS</entity> . In 2023 turnout at the same time was 32.2 percent. Long queues at polling stations in Serbia: What do you think of the NOS app and website? What are we doing well? What could be better? title: Cargo ship almost out of control north of Schiermonnikoog, three injured
lead: A heavy cargo ship was almost out of control in the North Sea north of Schiermonnikoog around 13.30 hours this afternoon. Three of the 25 crew members were injured, the Coast Guard says. Earlier, the Coast Guard and the Royal Dutch Sea Rescue Society (KNRM) spoke of five injured. At 16.55 hours, that number was adjusted to three. Two injured people were winched aboard a Coast Guard helicopter. They were flown to Groningen Aiport Eelde. They were then taken to hospital by ambulance. How serious their injuries are has not been announced. A so-called SAR nurse (ambulance nurse) was earlier lowered onto the ship from the Coast Guard helicopter. The Coast Guard aircraft was also deployed. Heavy transport ship: It concerns the UHL Freedom, almost 150 metres long, sailing under the Portuguese flag. The ship is designed for transporting very heavy cargo, such as large machines or parts for wind farms, for example. The ship ran into trouble 29 kilometres off the coast of Schiermonnikoog. According to the Coast Guard, the UHL Freedom got a "dragging anchor". That means the anchor no longer held on the seabed. As a result, it drifted. The ship therefore raised the anchor, but then had engine problems, according to the Coast Guard. The UHL Freedom now has limited engine capacity again. The Coast Guard spokesperson cannot say when exactly that happened. Currently the wind force is 9 at the location of the cargo ship. According to news agency ANP, the waves there are 4.5 metres high. Large rescue operation: According to the KNRM spokesperson, three KNRM rescue boats from Eemshaven, Schiermonnikoog and Ameland have come to assist. Two emergency towing vessels have also been deployed. These are the Coast Guard's Guardian and the German tug Nordic. According to the Coast Guard, it will still take "several hours" before the tugs reach the ship.

title: Woman seriously injured after assault at party in Amsterdam
lead: In Amsterdam, a woman was seriously assaulted during an argument early yesterday morning. That is reported by the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>. The woman suffered serious injuries and has been taken to hospital. The argument broke out around 05.40 hours between two women at a party on Rhôneweg in Amsterdam. A man then struck one of the women on the head with an object. The police arrived on the scene because of the unrest that then arose. The suspect was able to flee at that time. The police are still searching for him. He is a tall man of about 30 years old with a dark skin tone. He was wearing a white T-shirt and dark denim jeans, according to the police. A police spokesperson tells NOS that it was not a party of the Amsterdam Dance Event. What do you think of the NOS app and website? What do we do well? What could be better? title: Gadi Eisenkot: the general who became a politician and then Netanyahu's biggest challenger
lead: He could well become the next prime minister of Israel, Gadi Eisenkot. Although his party Yashar is only one year old, he is the main challenger to incumbent prime minister Netanyahu, with whom Eisenkot has been in a neck-and-neck race for months. According to the latest polls, Israelis now prefer him over Netanyahu. The two are not strangers to each other. Eisenkot served in the Israeli army for decades and eventually became chief of staff. After the terrorist attack by Hamas in October 2023, Eisenkot joined Netanyahu's war cabinet as a minister. After disagreement over which strategy Israel should adopt, Eisenkot decided to leave. 'The anti-Bibi' Eisenkot has a Moroccan-Jewish background and therefore belongs to the Mizrahi Jews. If he is elected, he would be the first prime minister with that background. Analysts describe him as 'the anti-Bibi', referring to Benjamin 'Bibi' Netanyahu. Eisenkot grew up in a working-class family in Eilat and worked his way up to a top position in the army. His English is poor and his appearance is unpolished: a big contrast with the charisma and sleek haircut of Netanyahu. Also, many Israelis are familiar with Eisenkot's personal story. In December 2023 his son was killed in the Gaza war, and his funeral was broadcast live on television. That personal connection weighs heavily with voters, says Bart Wallet, professor of Jewish studies at the University of Amsterdam. "They see in him someone they can trust, someone who also knows war victims", he explains. "For them, Eisenkot in a way represents the situation the country of Israel is in now." That goes down well with Israeli voters, a large part of whom are disappointed in the leadership of Netanyahu, who has been accused of corruption. "Many of his voters are disillusioned, they simply don't want Netanyahu anymore", says Wallet. Erella Grassiani, anthropologist at the University of Amsterdam, agrees: "Many voters are pragmatic and see in Eisenkot a great chance to get rid of Netanyahu. He has gathered a lot of support around him, so they will go for whoever comes close to winning". Eisenkot likes to make use of this. He strongly criticises Netanyahu's war strategy and accuses him of evading his responsibilities. Not for nothing is Eisenkot's party called Yashar, which means just or fair. One of his main priorities is therefore setting up a large investigation into the 2023 Hamas attack. Netanyahu is opposing that investigation, even now that there are increasingly more reports showing that Netanyahu was warned before the attack but did nothing. Eisenkot is also a strong supporter of military conscription for all Israelis, including the ultra-Orthodox Jews. Their exemption from conscription was revoked in 2024, but Netanyahu is doing everything to regulate it by law after all. No 'government of doves' But when it comes to the approach to the Palestinians, Eisenkot and Netanyahu do not differ that much. Last week Eisenkot said at a press conference that, if elected, he wants to destroy Hamas's military wing within eighteen months. "He may seem somewhat more moderate, but it is not as if he will end the occupation, or that he is necessarily against the settlers", says Grassiani. It has also long been known that Eisenkot does not shy away from excessive violence. As a military man he was the brains behind the notorious Dahiya doctrine, in which entire neighbourhoods are bombed flat and residential areas are destroyed to such an extent that they become uninhabitable. "A government under Eisenkot will not be one of doves", says Wallet. "For him too, the security issue has the highest priority." Still, both Wallet and Grassiani see how Eisenkot takes a different tone from the current prime minister. "You can see that Eisenkot responds strongly to settler violence, something Netanyahu does not really distance himself from", says Wallet. "I do expect that the international community will find it easier to work with Eisenkot than with Netanyahu's government, certainly if far-right ministers such as Smotrich and Ben-Gvir have disappeared." That offers the Palestinians, however small, a bit of hope: "The Palestinians know very well that the difference will not be large, but they are tired of Israeli violence", says Grassiani. "In daily life this can certainly make a small difference." But real change is probably not going to come for the Palestinians, says Wallet. "Israel's security is number one. No compromises will be made on that under Eisenkot either." What do you think of the NOS app and website? What do we do well? What could be better? We are curious about your opinion. title: Opposition leader María Corina Machado back in Venezuela
lead: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado has returned to Venezuela. She wrote this on X. "I am here. With you", Machado writes. The opposition leader, who is also a Nobel Prize winner, had spent almost a year abroad after secretly travelling to Norway to receive the Nobel Peace Prize. Recently she was in Panama. She then made several attempts to return to her country, but according to international media those attempts were blocked by the United States. Opposition leader Machado receives a warm welcome after returning to Venezuela: Machado's return increases pressure on the country to hold new elections. That call has been around for a while. Thousands of Venezuelans also took to the streets last week. After the US abducted then Venezuelan president Nicolás Maduro last January, US president Trump chose vice president Delcy Rodriguez to lead the country. Both Rodríguez and the Trump administration then promised that new elections would be held, but a date for them has still not been set. Rodríguez maintains good ties with Washington. According to several American media, she even asks the US for permission for certain posts on social media. In addition, the US has been able to conclude a major oil deal with Venezuela. In August Trump announced that the US is taking control of 65 billion barrels from Venezuela's oil reserves. Although Machado praises Trump a great deal, the White House also sees her as a potential troublemaker. Trump says he did not know about Machado's return, news agency Reuters writes. He also says he hopes she is safe. "But things are going very well for us in Venezuela", he adds. According to foreign minister Rubio, Machado's return is a "direct result" of reconciliation talks in which the US was involved. In hiding: before travelling to Norway, Machado had been in hiding in Venezuela for about eleven months, after she was briefly detained in January 2025 over a protest. Opposition leader Edmundo González writes on X that he is pleased about her return and that he will be with her "soon". "Today is a very important day for Venezuelans. Our sovereign voice returns with her to lead and guide this process!" Nobel Peace Prize: Machado received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2025 for her work for democracy in Venezuela and her peaceful resistance to Maduro's authoritarian government. Last January she offered her Nobel medal to the American president, after she had been invited to Washington to talk about Venezuela's future. Trump had previously said that he did not see Machado as a suitable successor to Maduro. "She does not have the support or respect within the country", he said. He also made clear that he thought he deserved the Nobel Prize. Trump called offering the prize "a beautiful gesture of mutual respect". The Nobel Prize can, however, not be withdrawn, shared or passed on to others.

title: Stormy weather moves away, calm autumn weather next week
lead: This weekend autumn was fully upon us. No less than two storms that had been given names brought drenched and turbulent weather. Storm Austen passed over the Netherlands on Friday. In our country it was not an official storm, as the wind was not strong enough for that. Austen mainly caused a lot of disruption and power outages in France and the United Kingdom. However, we did get an enormous downpour of rainwater here. From Friday evening through yesterday morning, almost 50 millimeters of rain were measured in some places. That is about half of what normally falls in an entire month. Yesterday and today storm Boelo followed. This was an official storm, with an hourly average wind force of 9 on Vlieland. The highest gusts were measured in Den Helder and IJmuiden at 111 and 115 kilometers per hour. Transition to calmer weather The wind is now easing, and that trend continues over the coming days. Tomorrow is the most changeable day of the week, with quite a bit of wind and rain in the course of the afternoon. It will then be 12 to 14 degrees. On Tuesday the wind comes from the south and brings briefly but powerfully warm air. It will be 15 degrees in the afternoon in the north and nearly 20 degrees in the south. That is very warm for late October. Only at the end of the day may some rain fall, but until then it is lovely weather to be outside. From Wednesday we get a few days of much calmer autumn weather. The sun shines and it stays dry. During the day it is 13 to 15 degrees. At night and in the morning it is considerably fresher and it may become misty.

title: Doctors fear that caregiver at Beekse Bergen panther attack will not survive
lead: The condition of the caregiver at safari park Beekse Bergen, who was seriously injured yesterday in a panther attack, has deteriorated. A spokesperson for the park in Hilvarenbeek says in a statement that she is so seriously ill that doctors fear she will not survive. The woman sustained serious injuries to her head and neck in the attack. She was able to raise the alarm herself with her radio. She was working alone in the enclosure of two Persian panthers. Those animals were indoors yesterday because of the bad weather, when the attack happened. Normally, staff are kept from being in the same space as the predators. Kept asleep The woman was taken to hospital after the panther attack, where she underwent surgery. According to the park, the operation went well, but her condition nonetheless remains "worrying". She got through the night, but has since been kept asleep and is unresponsive, Omroep Brabant writes. The woman's condition is critical and the chance of recovery is very small, the park says. Investigation "We are of course deeply saddened by this news and are doing everything we can to support her family, colleagues and other close ones as much as possible and to provide extra care where needed", Beekse Bergen says. It is not yet clear exactly what happened in the enclosure. According to the park, there are no cameras in the enclosure. Both the park and the Labour Inspectorate have started an investigation into the attack. No consequences for the panthers The park says nothing about the care of the panthers will change. The animals live outdoors and are looked after as usual. In principle the animals have shown natural behaviour, a park spokesperson said earlier to Omroep Brabant. "They are and remain predators." The caregiver has worked at the park, with short breaks, for almost forty years, eight of them with the panthers. "She has a big heart for the animals and for the park. In consultation with her family, the park will therefore remain open", Beekse Bergen says.

title: Hereditary Prince of Liechtenstein blocks abortion law, demonstrations against the monarch's veto
lead: In Liechtenstein there have been demonstrations against Hereditary Prince Alois, who has used his veto to block a new abortion law. Hundreds of demonstrators gathered yesterday in front of his castle in the capital Vaduz. Demonstrations are rare in the small Alpine country. Protesters carried banners reading "My body, my veto" and "My body does not belong to the principality", writes the Austrian broadcaster ORF , which was present. There is also criticism of the fact that the powerful prince is blocking a parliamentary decision. One demonstrator tells the broadcaster that in her view it is not acceptable for a monarch to decide on abortion legislation. "It concerns us women. We bear children." Heir to the throne with governing duties In September, parliament passed a law making abortion legal in the first twelve weeks of pregnancy. That law came about after a citizens' initiative. 5000 residents signed it, about a quarter of eligible voters . The principality has 41,269 residents. Hereditary Prince Alois had already said in June that he would not sign such a law. He is the heir to the throne of the Principality of Liechtenstein. Prince Hans-Adam II is officially the reigning monarch, but in 2004 he handed over his governing duties to his eldest son. The Liechtenstein royal house still holds a great deal of power. At the start of this century its powers were even expanded. The royal house then threatened to move to Vienna if the population rejected the expansion of power in a referendum. A majority then voted in favour of the expansion. Later attempts to curb the prince's power failed. The hereditary prince rarely uses his veto, but the abortion issue weighs heavily on the Catholic Alois. That is why he blocked the approved law last week. He did this, by his own account, to "protect unborn life", Liechtenstein media write. Abortion is prohibited in the principality by law and is permitted only in cases of absolute medical necessity . Since 2015, however, it has been legal for women to travel abroad to have an abortion. 'Show of power' The committee 'An abortion law for Liechtenstein' calls Alois's use of the veto "a show of power to impose a moral conviction", writes the Swiss public broadcaster SRF . According to the committee, the hereditary prince is denying women their right to self-determination by doing so. The committee organised yesterday's protest march through the capital Vaduz. The march ended in front of Schloss Vaduz castle, the official residence of the monarch. The demonstration was peaceful. According to the committee, 400 demonstrators took part, while according to the police there were 250. Liechtenstein is a parliamentary democracy with a politically active monarch. The monarchy has a veto over laws that the government wants to implement. In this way the monarchy effectively sidelines parliament. The veto is enshrined in the principality's constitution. Opinion research earlier showed that a large majority of Liechtenstein's residents are in favour of the new abortion law. More and more citizens also reject the far-reaching power of the royal house. About three quarters think that this power should be curbed. This abortion issue is therefore also about the future of the Liechtenstein monarchy.

title: Cyclist dies in Amsterdam after a tree falls on him
lead: In Amsterdam a cyclist died today after a tree fell on him. The investigation into the identity of the victim is still ongoing, the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> told NOS. The man died on the Sloterweg in the Nieuw-West district. It is not yet clear what time the accident happened. Emergency services received a report at the end of the afternoon from someone who had seen the man lying under a fallen tree. On arrival, the police found a dead man. Storm Earlier this weekend, two trees also fell onto moving cars in the capital due to stormy weather that moved over Amsterdam. A motorist was injured in the process, the other had no injuries. The Amsterdam Dance Event (ADE) also suffered from the strong wind. The festival Into the Woods at the NDSM wharf, for example, was stopped early because of the wind.

title: Audi builds first factory in the United States, criticism from Germany
lead: The German carmaker Audi is going to build a new factory in the state of Georgia for 4 billion dollars (3.6 billion euros), and will thereby produce cars in the United States for the first time. The Volkswagen subsidiary wants to produce 200,000 SUVs there annually. The news was announced by US President Trump during a Republican election rally in the city of Perry. Audi top executive Gernot Döllner also appeared on the stage. He thanked Trump for his support. The construction of the new factory still needs to be approved by the Volkswagen supervisory board. Audi supervisory board chairman Manfred Döss has already spoken in favour of it. "We must have the courage to invest, seize new opportunities and make decisions that will shape our company for the decades to come." According to him, the planned investment in the US is part of that. Criticism from Germany. Construction of the factory is scheduled to start in 2027 and production is to begin in the early 2030s, Audi announces in a statement. The factory will build models specifically tailored to the wishes of North American customers. Since the start of his second term, Trump has urged foreign companies to move their production to the United States, including by threatening high import duties. Companies that produce in the US could in fact be exempted from such tariffs. With this, Trump wants to stimulate the American economy and create industrial jobs. Criticism is coming from Germany over Audi's decision. While top executive Döllner invests billions in the US, parent company Volkswagen is in a deep crisis. Volkswagen is working on a major reorganisation in Germany due to disappointing sales, high costs and increasing competition from China. Against that background, a multi-billion investment in the United States is politically and socially especially sensitive. Factory closures, mass layoffs and wage freezes are namely threatening in Germany. Trade union IG Metall, which among other things represents workers in the German automotive industry, therefore reacted with irritation to Döllner's appearance in American media. A spokesperson for the union called it "more than worrying" that a German executive is positioning himself as a campaign helper for an American president who wants to turn German carmakers into American carmakers. "Trump has never hidden what his real intentions are: he wants to weaken our domestic economy, and especially the car industry. He wants jobs to cross the Atlantic Ocean, and his import tariff policy is the instrument for that", the spokesperson said. "It is hard to understand why Gernot Döllner is extending a hand to Trump in this situation. Especially because his own company is at the same time putting the future of factories and entire regions here in Germany up for discussion." Volkswagen top executive Oliver Blume stated that success in North America benefits the entire group. "A possible Audi factory in the US would create additional conditions for that: locally produced cars from the US for the American market."

title: Stranded cargo ship in North Sea sails again, rescue boats turn back
lead: The heavy cargo ship UHL Freedom, which became almost adrift this afternoon north of Schiermonnikoog, is sailing again. This is happening with "limited engine power", the Coast Guard reports. The vessel became almost adrift around 13.30, after the anchor lost its grip on the seabed and engine problems followed. Three of the 25 crew members were injured. The UHL Freedom has been sailing independently again since 18.35. "Where the ship is now heading is up to the shipping company", said the Coast Guard. The emergency service says it will continue to closely monitor the situation. Rescue operation After the cargo vessel asked for help, a large-scale rescue operation was launched. The Coast Guard deployed a helicopter and an aircraft, among other things. Three rescue boats from Eemshaven, Schiermonnikoog and Ameland of the Royal Dutch Shipwrecked Mariners' Society (KNRM) also came to the location in the North Sea. Those boats have returned. In addition, two tugs were called in, the Coast Guard's Guardian and the Nordic tug from Germany. The latter has turned around. The Guardian is near the cargo ship and is on standby, the Coast Guard reports. That means this tug can go into action if needed. Heavy cargo ship The UHL Freedom is a nearly 150-metre-long transport ship sailing under the Portuguese flag. The vessel is designed for transporting very heavy cargo, such as large machines or components for wind farms, for example.

title: Cheaper and more control: companies look with interest at Chinese AI
lead: What if you could use AI more cheaply and still keep control over the information you share? Companies and organisations that work with AI technology are looking with great interest at open AI models, which are mostly made by Chinese companies. While major American AI companies such as Anthropic, OpenAI and Google charge subscription fees and charge for use of their most powerful closed AI models, open AI models can be downloaded for free. Users can therefore choose for themselves on which servers an open AI model runs, whereas with closed models the maker decides. That can be risky if you want to process personal or sensitive information with a closed AI model: that data is processed on computer equipment you do not manage yourself. The most popular open AI models are made by Chinese companies such as Alibaba, DeepSeek, Moonshot and Z.ai. A number of American companies also release open AI models, including Meta, the company behind Facebook and Instagram. High interest in open AI models The law firm Driven Lawyers in Amsterdam makes good use of this. The firm runs a small version of the AI model Qwen on computer servers in Germany, says founder Arvid van Oorschot. "That model is less good than the large American AI models, but for some tasks it is very suitable. We use it, for example, to make summaries of legal contracts." "In the past that was manual work, now we do it with AI. We really don't want to use an expensive American AI model for that. If you keep going, the costs add up considerably. It is important for a company to keep an eye on that." There is a lot of interest from companies in this kind of open model, says Philip Gast. He is one of the founders of The Stack, a network of companies and people who work with AI technology. "For some tasks you really don't need an expensive AI model." "You can download open models for free. The largest and most powerful AI models can't simply be run on your laptop. For that you still need expensive equipment with a lot of computing power. That is why there are also companies that offer various open AI models on their servers. That also costs money, but you can still come out cheaper." One of those companies is OpenRouter, worldwide one of the largest providers offering various AI models. Global user figures from the American company show that AI use is increasing enormously and that open models are being used more and more. At the end of last year, about 30 percent of AI use was open and 70 percent was 'closed' AI models, such as Claude (from Anthropic), GPT (OpenAI) and Gemini (Google). Recently that has reversed: 70 percent of AI use now comes from open models, mainly from Chinese companies. Working with sensitive data Besides cost, another factor is that with an open AI model you have much more control over your data. "As a law firm we work with a great many sensitive files and information," says Van Oorschot. "We don't want to send those to servers in America or China." Because you can simply download the model, a company can decide for itself on which servers it runs. For many companies it is important, or even necessary, that the information stays within Europe, for example in healthcare or the defence industry. Open models therefore pose a serious threat to the American AI companies, says Gast. Keeping control over your information is important, but for many companies it is mainly about cost. "If you can do your work with much cheaper AI models from China, why would you still use an expensive American model?" China wants to impose restrictions Until now Chinese AI companies have been able to make their open models freely available, but the question is how long that will last. The Chinese government plans to impose restrictions on AI technology. If the rules come, open AI models could in future only be made public with a licence, or even be banned outside China. According to the current plan the licence requirement does not apply to AI models that are already public, such as the popular models from DeepSeek and Z.ai that are already widely used in Europe and the United States. China correspondent Gabi Verberg: "With these restrictions China wants to make sure that the country can use valuable knowledge as much as possible itself, while the major competitor, the United States, does not benefit from it. Earlier this year the Chinese government still blocked the takeover of the Chinese AI company Manus by the American company Meta." "Since last month it has been much easier for the Chinese government to stop Chinese people who want to travel abroad. According to experts this measure is also meant to make Chinese AI talent easier to control." "The proposal now on the table creates a lot of uncertainty. The question is whether the leading Chinese AI companies will be able to keep sharing their best new models as open models with the rest of the world in the future, and under what conditions. That could be a major blow for American and European companies that are only too eager to use Chinese AI technology."

title: Woman found dead in apartment in Eindhoven, man arrested
lead: In an apartment in Eindhoven a woman was found dead this afternoon under suspicious circumstances. A man suspected of involvement in her death has been arrested. The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> rules out that the woman died a natural death, says the spokesperson for the Oost-Brabant unit. The suspect was arrested "near the apartment". A detective team and forensic investigators are at the home this evening to carry out an investigation. The police received a report around 16.30 hours. The deceased woman was subsequently found in the apartment on Van Kinsbergenstraat in the north of Eindhoven. Whether the suspect and the victim knew each other, the police cannot say in the interest of the investigation. The police may have more information tomorrow.

title: Search for watersports enthusiast near Scheveningen halted due to darkness
lead: Around Scheveningen and Kijkduin there was a large search for a missing watersports enthusiast. It is presumably a surfer or kiter. The search was stopped at the beginning of the evening. Just after 14.00 hours an alarm was raised with the emergency services control room about the missing watersports enthusiast. Since then, searches have been carried out on land, at sea and in the air, in the area between Kijkduin and the pier at Scheveningen. "Despite the enormous effort of the emergency services, the missing person has unfortunately not yet been found," the Haaglanden Veilig safety region reports. "The conditions make it too dangerous for the rescuers to continue searching. The strong wind and high waves make the search difficult. Now that it is dark, it is impossible to continue a safe search." The search will resume tomorrow morning. A spokesperson for the Coastguard tells Omroep West that the missing person was part of a group and went out of sight. The weather was particularly stormy in the search area, with gusts up to 80 kilometres per hour.

title: Pro-Russian presidential candidate in Bulgaria in the lead after first election round
lead: The moderately pro-Russian president Iliana Jotova of Bulgaria has, according to exit polls, received the most votes in the first round of the presidential elections. Due to a historically low turnout, a second round will be needed on 1 November. According to various Bulgarian projections, just over 20 percent of eligible voters cast their vote. According to several exit polls, Jotova obtained between 35.2 and 36.5 percent of the votes. The pro-Western candidate, Andrej Gjoerov, the former interim prime minister and banker, received 32.2 to 32.4 percent of eligible voters' votes. The presidential elections revolved mainly around the war Russia started in Ukraine, the economic situation in Bulgaria and drone attacks on ships in the Black Sea. Important test The election is seen as an important test for the centre-left Progressive Bulgaria party of Prime Minister Roemen Radev. He won the parliamentary elections in April and was previously president until January. At that time he stepped down to run for the premiership. Jotova, previously vice president for nine years, succeeded him. The 62-year-old Jotova is considered an independent candidate, but enjoys the support of Radev's pro-Russian party and the Socialist Party, where she began her career. She wants to strengthen ties with Russia and, like Radev, does not want to provide military aid to Ukraine. In addition, Jotova advocates lifting sanctions against Russia. In doing so she departs from the EU's course, which wants to increase pressure on Moscow and continues to support Ukraine militarily. If Jotova wins, she will become the first elected female president of Bulgaria. Gjoerov, who enjoys the support of the reform-minded opposition, stands precisely for support for Ukraine. During his interim premiership, between February and May of this year, he signed, among other things, a security cooperation agreement with that country. The preliminary results are expected to be published tomorrow.

title: Former president Vucic admits defeat: student movement wins Serbian elections
lead: The Studentenlijst in Serbia has won the most votes in the parliamentary elections. That is what former president Vucic says based on an exit poll. He thereby acknowledges his defeat. "We do not have final results yet, but based on a sample it is clear that we have lost these elections. The Studentenlijst has won. They will get between 135 and 140 seats, while we will win 105", said Vucic. These are the most exciting elections in Serbia in a long time, in which a large-scale student protest movement, the Studentenlijst, is taking on the autocratic leader Aleksandar Vucic and his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS). In Belgrade people are celebrating: cars drive through the streets honking and people are shouting "victory" and "he's finished". The spokesperson for the Studentenlijst said that "the voice of the people has been heard". "Tonight we celebrate the victory, tomorrow we build the future", he added. Correspondent Thijs Kettenis is in Belgrade and is barely audible right after Vucic admitted his defeat: The voters have turned out in record numbers. Turnout stood at 67.6 percent at 19.00 hours, according to polling agencies and observer organisations CeSID and Ipsos. That is the highest turnout since the breakup of Yugoslavia in 1992. There were long queues at polling stations across Serbia and at embassies abroad today. According to news agency Reuters, Vucic also had to wait almost two hours to be able to vote. He stepped down in September after nine years as president and wanted to become prime minister now in order to stay in power. The student movement had called on people to vote early today, because the party feared that Vucic would try to stay in power with the help of fraud. Early in the evening, reports circulated of violent incidents at a number of polling stations. The European ambassador to Serbia expressed his concern on X. "We call on all parties to remain calm, act responsibly and refrain from violence and provocations. We also call on the competent authorities to guarantee the safety of everyone involved in the electoral process", he wrote. Images also circulated on social media of groups of men dressed in black marching through the capital Belgrade. The riot police have been deployed at various locations in the centre. Mass protests The Studentenlijst grew out of two years of mass protests against Vucic. These began when part of the station in the city of Novi Sad collapsed, killing sixteen people. The renovation of the station was reportedly poorly carried out by companies with close ties to the SNS, according to the criticism. In recent weeks, reports have emerged that civil servants, their friends and their families have been pressured to prove that they vote for Vuvic and his SNS.

title: Polling stations in Brazil open two hours longer after intervention by Supreme Court
lead: Polling stations in Brazil will remain open two hours longer today for the decisive round of the presidential election, the Supreme Court has decided. The reason is problems voters are experiencing with transport to polling stations. Originally, polling stations would close at 17.00 Brazilian time (21.00 Dutch time). Voting has now been extended on the order of the Supreme Court until 19.00 Brazilian time (23.00 Dutch time). In view of the ruling, the highest Brazilian electoral court (TSE) decided to temporarily halt the processing and publication of the interim results. Brazil votes electronically. This is at stake in these elections: The decision of the Supreme Court was taken by judge Cristiano Zanin and came after requests from the two presidential candidates Lula da Silva (80) and Flávio Bolsonaro (45). The team of the current left-wing president Lula said that voters in nine states were hindered by problems with buses from casting their vote in time. His opponent, the far-right Flávio Bolsonaro, submitted a similar request to the Supreme Court due to heavy rainfall in southern Brazil, where flooding made transport to polling stations difficult. According to the judge, extending voting by two hours was justified "given the seriousness of the reported facts". Neck-and-neck race Candidate Lula is trying to become president for the fourth time and is locked in a neck-and-neck race with his ideological counterpart Bolsonaro. Bolsonaro surprisingly won the first round of the presidential election, while Lula led in the polls. Because Bolsonaro did not obtain an absolute majority, a second round was needed to determine a winner. The result determines whether Brazil, with more than 200 million inhabitants, continues on its left-wing course or turns to the right. The elections are seen as important for the political balance in South America. Earlier this year, Trump-friendly right-wing candidates won the presidential elections in Peru and Colombia . In Chile that happened at the end of last year . A win for Lula would mean that Brazil, like Mexico, retains a left-wing <entity id="org:regering">regering</entity>.

title: Sven Kockelmann (56) wins Sonja Barend Award for interview with former prime minister Schoof
lead: Sven Kockelmann (56) has won the Sonja Barend Award. The journalist wins the prize for his interview with former prime minister Schoof. BNNVARA, the broadcaster that presents the prize, praises Kockelmann for the way he turned the interview with the then outgoing prime minister into "not a political cross-examination, but a personal conversation about a turbulent premiership". The interview took place on 20 February of this year during a special broadcast of the WNL programme Café Kockelmann. Kockelmann was chosen by a jury of fifty journalists. "A revealing conversation," says jury member Maartje van Weegen in a press release. His interview was one of the nine conversations on the longlist for the Sonja Barend Award this year. 'Honest look back' He received the award tonight from last year's winner, Coen Verbraak, during the broadcast of talk show Pauw & De Wit. Eva Jinek finished in second place with her interview with SGP leader Chris Stoffer about abortion. Verbraak came third with his interview with journalist Frits Abrahams about his wife's dementia in the Human programme Over Leven. Kockelmann says on the BNNVARA website that with the conversation he mainly wanted to get to know the person behind the prime minister. "The intention was an honest look back, with openness about matters. I wanted to know what had gone on inside him and how he had experienced the events." Kockelmann calls the interview with the prime minister "remarkable", mainly because of Schoof's candour. "I did wonder: was it sharp enough? Was it complete enough? The doubt remains, no matter how long I do this work. Even the people who were technically involved in the recording were silent afterwards." Sonja Barend has died Sonja Barend passed away in April of this year, but her trade prize for the best television interview continues to exist, as she herself wanted. It is the first time that 'The queen of the talk show' will not present the prize named after her.

title: Lula Wins Election in Brazil, Bolsonaro Does Not Accept Defeat
lead: The election in Brazil has been won by incumbent president Lula. He received about 52 percent of the votes, the electoral council has announced. The election was a close race between radical-right Flávio Bolsonaro (45) and left-wing Lula da Silva (80). The first round was won by Bolsonaro, although Lula had led in the polls. Because neither had an absolute majority, a second round had to follow. In this new round, the difference was ultimately about 4 million votes in favour of Lula. Lula also led Brazil between 2003 and 2011 and took office again as president in 2023. Now he begins his fourth term, which makes him history. Left-Wing Course With Lula's victory, the country is again choosing a left-wing course. He campaigned with a progressive and social agenda, including special family allowances for the poor. Bolsonaro, son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, is instead in favour of a free market with little government interference. He also wants the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> to act harshly against crime. Lula was welcomed with loud music at a gathering in Sao Paulo after the result. In a victory speech he thanked his voters. "We managed to convince people that voting was extremely important to keep democracy in Brazil safe." After losing the first round, Lula's supporters, many of them young people, began to mobilise. In groups they took to the streets to win over undecided voters. The fierce struggle between the two candidates shows how divided the country is. Part of the Brazilian population is celebrating and relieved that the presidency remains in Lula's hands. Another part of the population feels defeated and disappointed. Lula promised that he will be a president for all 215 million Brazilians. "There is no electoral opponent anymore." Bolsonaro Does Not Accept Result Bolsonaro refuses to accept the defeat. In a speech he said he wants the result declared invalid. In this he points to the decision of the Supreme Court to keep the polling stations open two hours longer. Bolsonaro calls that "unacceptable", which is striking, since he himself had asked for a longer voting period. Originally the polls would close at 17.00 Brazilian time (21.00 Dutch time). But on the orders of the Supreme Court they closed at 19.00 Brazilian time (23.00 Dutch time). Bolsonaro asked for an extension because voters in the south of the country had difficulty reaching polling stations due to heavy rainfall. Lula also wanted the polling stations kept open longer because voters in nine states could not otherwise cast their votes in time due to bus problems. Bolsonaro's refusal to recognise the election result could increase tension in an already polarised Brazil. The situation resembles 2022, when his father, former president Bolsonaro, also refused to accept his defeat. Angry and incited supporters stormed government buildings. Meanwhile, Bolsonaro and others planned a coup, which was eventually called off because there was too little support from the military. Last year Bolsonaro was sentenced to 27 years in prison for this. Governing Will Not Be Easy Governing will not be easy for Lula. In the National Congress he faces a powerful right-wing bloc, so it is unclear how much support he will get for his plans. In addition, the power of the Bolsonaro family has grown considerably. Members of the family are represented in both the Chamber of Deputies and <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Senaat</entity>. Lula will also have to take seriously the concerns of a large part of the population that did not vote for him. These Brazilians are drawn to the so-called bolsonarismo, the conservative radical-right movement around former president Bolsonaro. For them, issues such as crime and the economy were important election themes. For the Amazon and Indigenous Brazilians, Lula's victory is good news. Under his presidency deforestation decreased in recent years. Under Bolsonaro senior, more logging took place and large landowners got more room for production in the Amazon. The fear was that this policy would be continued under Bolsonaro junior. Left in a Right-Leaning Region Under Lula, Brazil is one of the few remaining left-wing countries in Latin America. The region has moved steadily further to the right over the past year and a half. US President Trump is trying to exert his influence in the region as much as possible. He prefers to do business with right-wing governments that are ideologically close to him.

title: Wake-up call 26/10: Lower House debate on Tax Plan • Who wins the Golden Ball?
lead: Good morning! Today the House of Representatives debates <entity id="person:eelco-heinen">minister Heinen</entity> on the Tax Plan, and tonight it will be announced who will be named the best footballer of the year. First the weather: in the morning it is mostly dry with some room for sun. In the afternoon it becomes cloudy from the southwest and some rain follows. The maxima are between 12 and 14 degrees with a fairly strong south wind. In the coming days it is often dry, with Wednesday and Thursday in particular offering room for sun. Are you heading out today? Here you can find the overview of traffic jams and roadworks, and here you can see the situation on the railways. What can you expect today? What did you miss: The elections in Brazil have been won by incumbent president Lula. He received about 52 percent of the votes, the electoral council has announced. The elections were a neck-and-neck race between far-right Flávio Bolsonaro (45) and leftist Lula da Silva (80). The difference ultimately amounted to 4 million votes. In a victory speech Lula thanked his voters. Bolsonaro refuses to accept the defeat. He said in a speech that he wants the result declared invalid. Other news from the night: And then this: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado has returned to Venezuela. She was warmly welcomed at the Santa Rosa church in Barquisimeto. The opposition leader stayed abroad for almost a year after secretly travelling to Norway to receive the Nobel Peace Prize. Recently she was in Panama. Have a nice day!

title: Two dead in UK after trees blown over during Storm Boelo
lead: In the United Kingdom two people died yesterday because of Storm Boelo. In London a man in his twenties died after a fallen tree landed on the car he was driving. In the southwest of Scotland a fallen tree struck a 60-year-old man. Both men died at the scene. In Scotland two women were also taken to hospital after being hit by falling trees. Strong gusts Storm Boelo brought gusts of up to 135 kilometres per hour. Streets flooded during the storm, rail, air and water traffic was hindered, and over the weekend around 800,000 households in total were without power because trees and branches fell onto electricity cables. According to the trade organisation of grid operators, Energy Networks Association, repair work was hampered by the weather, although by Sunday evening the vast majority of households were reconnected to the grid. Around 90,000 households were still without power then. Shortly before Boelo, Storm Austen had already caused disruption. Meteorologists expect more bad weather in the coming days. Disruption in the Netherlands The Netherlands also had a restless and stormy weekend due to Storms Austen and Boelo. In Amsterdam a cyclist died yesterday after a tree fell on him. Two cars in the capital were also hit by falling trees. One motorist was injured, the other escaped with a fright. In Volkel on Friday a falling tree made a large hole in the roof of a farmhouse. On Saturday evening a house was also damaged in Rijnsburg, near Leiden. In Culemborg a tree fell on a parked car. In many places the fire brigade was busy over the weekend removing trees and branches from roads. The N207 near Alphen aan den Rijn was blocked for some time. On Sunday evening Oudeschild on Texel experienced water nuisance due to Storm Boelo. Hotels and restaurants were no longer accessible. In an attempt to keep the water out, sandbags and water pumps were deployed. Water also stood high in Harlingen.

title: 'New Houthi attacks on international airport in Saudi Arabia'
lead: The Houthis in Yemen claim that they have hit the international airport of the Saudi capital Riyadh again. Nothing is known about possible casualties. Images of the attacks are not available for now, although that may also be related to the heavy censorship in Saudi Arabia. The airport reopened a few hours before the attacks, after it had been closed for just over two weeks due to deadly Houthi attacks earlier this month . The Saudis say they intercepted a ballistic missile that was heading for the airport. They also reportedly destroyed two missile launch sites in Sanaa, the capital of Yemen that the Houthis control. On Saturday, while the airport was still closed, the Houthis also claim to have attacked the airport in Riyadh. They also say they attacked an important oil pipeline. It is not known whether they caused damage there. Saudi Arabia has not yet confirmed the attacks. Deadly attacks Earlier this month, 12 people were killed and hundreds injured in a large attack on King Khalid airport. Other attacks in Saudi Arabia also killed people . The conflict between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis flared up almost two months ago, when the government of Yemen began an offensive against the Houthis. The Saudis support that internationally recognised government; the Houthis are trying to overthrow it and are supported by Iran. Due to the fighting in Yemen, around 200,000 people have fled . The UN organisation for migration and refugee aid (IOM) has called on the international community to take action.

title: PostNL sees the number of parcels from Asian webshops decline further
lead: In the past three months too, PostNL had much less work delivering parcels from outside the European Union. Especially from Asian webshops, far fewer are being sent. In the past three months, a total of just over 32 percent fewer international parcels were sent. That is according to the figures of the postal delivery company for the third quarter of 2026. Import rules In the previous quarter, far fewer parcels were also sent from Asia to Europe. Then the number of international parcels fell by 15 percent, mainly due to a decline in parcels from Asia. The decline is "largely the result of EU import rules effective 1 July", says the listed company. Parcels from outside the EU have since become more expensive due to a levy of 3 euros per product or product group. In November, parcels from outside the EU will become another 2 euros more expensive. Within Europe, PostNL delivers a lot more parcels, just over 40 percent more than a year ago. But that growth is "more than cancelled out" by the sharp decline in parcels to be delivered from Asia, according to PostNL. However, the company did earn more on each parcel. It passes the European import levy on to the customer, but it also charges more for shipping parcels and letterbox parcels. Sending letters that must be delivered within one day has also become more expensive since 1 July. As a result, the company's revenue rises slightly in the third quarter by 6 million euros to 768 million euros. Postal delivery Since mid-July this year, PostNL delivers letters less often. The company looks back on the change with satisfaction. Fewer letters were indeed delivered, but the company still managed to earn slightly more from them. The number of letters Dutch people send has been declining for years. PostNL has the statutory task of delivering that mail, but because earnings are falling, the company believes the government should add money. So far that call has not led to a contribution, but PostNL recently tried again. PostNL calls scaling back to delivery within two days an "intermediate step". In the long term, the company wants to be able to take three days.

title: Three suspects arrested after deadly attack on church in Jordan
lead: Jordanian authorities have arrested three suspects in connection with an attack on a church last Friday. Nine people were killed and around 40 others were injured. The three suspects were arrested early this morning after a shootout in the western city of Karak. The attack there also took place last week. The men were hiding in an abandoned house and refused to surrender, the Jordanian authorities report. The trio then reportedly opened fire on security forces, who shot back. The men were wounded but could be arrested. According to the authorities, the suspects had several weapons and ammunition with them. The shooting took place on Friday during a funeral in a Greek Orthodox church. Around 200 people were reportedly present at the time. The gunmen then fled. Iron fist Jordanian news channel Al-Mamlaka shared video from a church security camera showing three gunmen. The footage shows the trio shooting while taking cover behind trees and a wall. Afterwards they run to the church entrance. Jordanian King Abdullah had instructed the security services to act with an "iron fist" against the fleeing gunmen. On social media, the king responded to the arrests. "We have sworn that the terrorists will not escape their punishment, and that no follower of dark ideologies that divide Jordanians will be tolerated." Minority No one has claimed the attack yet. The Jordanian authorities have not yet made the identity of the three suspects public. Attacks like the one in Karak are rare in Jordan. In 2016, armed men attacked officers during an attack in the same town. Ten people died and dozens of others were injured. The attackers were killed by security forces. That attack was later claimed by the terrorist group Islamic State (IS). Jordan has one of the oldest Christian populations in the world, making up around 3 percent of the population. The country has many locations mentioned in the Bible, to which Christian pilgrims from around the world travel.

title: Search for missing kitesurfer called off again: 'Not safe enough'
lead: The rescue services that have been searching since this morning off the Scheveningen coast for the water sports enthusiast who went missing yesterday afternoon have stopped again. Conditions at sea today are not safe enough to continue, says a spokesperson for the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>. Yesterday afternoon at around 14.00 the man was reported missing. Rescue services began a search that was halted around 19.00 . It was getting too dark and therefore too dangerous. This morning rescue services resumed the search, but around midday it was suspended again. "There is still a jeep driving along the coastline and a helicopter flying overhead," said the spokesperson. Land, sea, air. Yesterday the kitesurfer was searched for all afternoon from land, sea and the air between Kijkduin and Noordwijk. Eventually the search area was limited to the coast of Scheveningen, because the water sports enthusiast was last seen there. The strong wind and high waves made searching difficult, a spokesperson said. The weather was particularly stormy in the search area, with gusts up to 80 kilometres per hour. Divers later today too. Boats from the Royal Dutch Sea Rescue Society (KNRM), among others, were deployed for the search. The safety region initially hoped that divers could also get to work later today to help.

title: Staff fed up with problems with Frisian taxis: 'People are waiting for hours'
lead: Staff members of the taxi company Dorenbos have difficulty with the way they have to do their work. Elderly people sometimes wait for hours to be picked up, and minibuses sometimes suffer long-lasting technical problems. That is what drivers working for the company say to Omrop <entity id="org:provincie-fryslan">Fryslân</entity> . Dorenbos is based in Norg in Drenthe and over the past two years took over four Frisian taxi companies. The company is responsible for pupil transport and Wmo transport. The latter type of transport is intended for people who can no longer travel themselves, for example because they are older or have an illness. The most recent takeovers took place last summer, in the municipalities of <entity id="org:gemeente-smallingerland">Smallingerland</entity> and <entity id="org:gemeente-sudwest-fryslan">Súdwest-Fryslân</entity>. In two months, those municipalities received a total of just over 300 complaints about the way taxi transport has been arranged. Two hours of waiting after chemotherapy A former driver who wishes to remain anonymous tells the broadcaster that the problems at Dorenbos were already occurring before the summer. "In the morning I get the schedule, and then I can already see that I will arrive three hours late," he says. He no longer works for Dorenbos. The last straw for him was when he collected a woman after chemotherapy more than two hours after the agreed time at the hospital. "That lady doesn't get a message, but the schedule knows the taxi is hours late," the former employee says. "That woman was very emotional. You feel responsible for that. It is inhumane." But 70 kilometres per hour The regional broadcaster has also viewed WhatsApp conversations between drivers. In them, they discussed defects and technical problems with taxi minibuses. The former driver says that one day he did not want to make a trip because the wheelchair locking system in his bus was not working. "But the next day the schedule sent another colleague out with that same bus." He also tells of another colleague who was sent out in a car that could not go faster than 70 kilometres per hour. "Dorenbos had said there was no other car and that she had to drive through side roads to destinations." 'Start-up problems' According to deputy director Rijk van Dijk of Dorenbos, the complaints from Smallingerland are due to start-up problems. Dorenbos had two weeks to set up the transport after the former taxi company there went bankrupt. According to him, the municipality was aware that the transport would not immediately meet all standards. Moreover, according to Van Dijk, Dorenbos could take over fewer drivers and minibuses from the former providers. He acknowledges that passengers in Smallingerland and in Súdwest-Fryslân may have been picked up one to two hours later since the summer. He offers his apologies for that. "I think we had to row with the oars we had, and that we stuck our necks out." Utrecht pupil transport Pupil transport is not always in order in other places in the Netherlands either. In <entity id="org:gemeente-utrecht">Utrecht</entity>, the company Willemsen de Koning is responsible for the hundreds of pupils who attend special education. Parents, schools and politicians regularly voice criticism of the way this is done. The complaints concern late buses, changing drivers and poor communication, writes RTV Utrecht . Nevertheless, the company may continue to carry out pupil transport from 2027, when the tender expires. Three other parties were interested, but according to the municipality Willemsen de Koning had "the best offer on both quality and price". The municipality has, however, tightened the quality requirements.
