title: Cabinet wants 25,000 fewer central government civil servants, police and defence excluded
lead: The central government must also be able to manage with about 25,000 fewer civil servants. This is in the plans of state secretary Van der Burg for Slagvaardige Overheid. By 2035, about 16 percent of the approximately 160,000 (full-time) civil servants must have been cut. That this cabinet is focusing on reducing the civil service was already known. But Van der Burg is now making, for the first time, an estimate of the number of jobs that will cost. He has not yet said which departments must cut how many jobs. What is clear is that police and defence are being spared. Implementing agencies such as the <entity id="org:zbo-uitvoeringsinstituut-werknemersverzekeringen">UWV</entity>, <entity id="org:immigratie-en-naturalisatiedienst">IND</entity> and the <entity id="org:belastingdienst">Belastingdienst</entity>, which are already under pressure, are not automatically excluded. Exceptions to exceptions Van der Burg states that such agencies too can manage with fewer people, provided work is done on simplifying or scrapping rules. That is a key priority of the cabinet . "With fewer exceptions to exceptions, the work becomes simpler." Incidentally, in recent years there were more cabinets that wanted to prune the number of civil servants, but in the meantime there have only been more . When asked, Van der Burg says that this cabinet will do it, because everyone understands "that it must be done differently". To manage with fewer people, among other things, facilities services at ministries are being scaled back, ICT systems are being standardised, and the cabinet is looking at other efficiency measures, including the use of AI. Cutting advisory bodies But Van der Burg acknowledges that working more efficiently alone is not enough. "Choices are needed about what the government will do differently, less or no longer do." Those choices have not yet been made, but are still being "further elaborated". The cabinet is also looking at scrapping advisory councils (of which there are now 28) and advisory committees (about 150), which give advice in a variety of areas. "Cutting there really saves a lot of civil service capacity," says Van der Burg. He will announce later which advisory bodies will be cut. The cabinet is also looking at reforming the Open Government Act. Journalists and other citizens can invoke this act if they want to obtain government information publicly. "The request for information is often so broad that it is no longer clear which information must be provided," Van der Burg writes to <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>. And that costs civil servants a lot of time. Within half a year the state secretary hopes to have finished many of the plans to make central government "simpler, smarter and smaller". Ultimately, all of this should lead to an annual saving of 3.5 billion euros by 2035.

title: No more pink biscuits for the taking: blood bank Sanquin tightens snack policy
lead: Anyone who has ever donated blood or blood plasma knows that pink biscuits are waiting for them afterwards. Such a free snack at one of blood bank Sanquin's donor cafes is a thank-you for your donation, but also meant to help you recover and top up your blood sugar. In recent weeks Omroep West noticed that the baskets, bowls and racks in the donor cafe in Delft were conspicuously empty. Not only the pink biscuits, but also the speculaas people, breakfast biscuits and stroopwafels were missing. It turns out that blood bank Sanquin has tightened its national policy. Donors can no longer take the snacks themselves, but must ask the volunteers who prepare the food and drink for them from now on. "Yes, those are no longer on the table," says a volunteer in Delft. "People used to leave here with their bags full." Donors and non-donors The head office in Amsterdam recognizes the reports. According to Sanquin, both donors and non-donors went too far. "People who take a bit more than you would reasonably expect," says a spokesperson to the regional broadcaster. "I've heard of people who filled their bags and didn't let themselves be called out on it." Sanquin, which is legally responsible for the blood supply in the Netherlands, cannot name a 'damage amount'. The volunteer in Delft mentions a cost of 1000 euros per month in treats taken home. The laminated menu cards on the tables now read: 'Feeling peckish? Ask our volunteer for your well-earned snack'. 'Locations may decide for themselves' The tightened national policy is not mandatory for all Sanquin locations, the head office clarifies. "Collection locations may decide for themselves how to handle this. They are in control themselves." At several Sanquin collection locations the snacks therefore still simply stand on the table, for example in Utrecht and in The Hague at football club Duno. "You can see it quickly enough: people taking more than they should," says one of the volunteers in The Hague. "But well, if someone says the biscuit is going home with them, are you supposed to forbid that?" 'How much is not clear' When the NOS asked, the spokesperson explained that Sanquin does not know at how many locations people take too many snacks. "We know it happens. There are examples, but how many exactly is not clear." He stresses that it is mainly important that donors continue to feel welcome, even if at some locations they now have to ask for a pink biscuit.

title: Eleventh of the Eleventh in doubt in Tilburg: municipality and hospitality sector clash over teenagers
lead: Are minors always welcome during the Elfde van de Elfde, the traditional opening of the carnival season? The municipality of Tilburg and the local hospitality businesses clash over that question. As a result, the celebration is hanging by a thread. Tomorrow the municipality and hospitality sector will sit down to talk. "Carnival is a party for everyone," says the municipality of Tilburg. "Minors must also be able to party, just like adults." But the hospitality sector wants to be able to refuse people at busy moments. "For example a 14-year-old who has never been in a crowd, but also someone who is in poor health on their legs," says entrepreneur Alex Boonmann on behalf of the Tilburg hospitality board. "It concerns their safety." According to him, the fact that teenagers often drink beforehand and are even less used to it plays a role with them. "They then arrive drunk and in such a crowd they pose a danger to themselves and their surroundings." Elfde van de Elfde 11 November is the traditional start of the carnival season, and it is celebrated on a grand scale mainly in <entity id="org:provincie-noord-brabant">Noord-Brabant</entity> and Limburg. At exactly 11:11 the season is rung in and the countdown to carnival can begin. Carnival itself starts next year on Sunday 7 February. The Tilburg hospitality sector refuses to sign a contract from the municipality stating that everyone is welcome on the festival squares. If the hospitality operators do not admit teenagers to the site, they can expect a fine of 2500 euros per case. A supervisor for every young person What the municipality of Tilburg is now proposing is "unworkable," Boonmann believes. If he is only allowed to intervene on the site when things go wrong, "I would have to put a supervisor on every young person." He also finds the risk too great. He points out that the hospitality operators are responsible for supervising the alcohol rules and safety on the festival site. "If a 14-year-old gets trampled somewhere, it is my responsibility." Other cities are also struggling with how to deal with minors during carnival. In many cafes age is checked and they are not welcome at all. As a result, teenagers can often only be outside, where checking alcohol is very difficult. Anyone under 18 who has alcohol with them is punishable and can receive a fine or community service. "Keeping watch is difficult," says Sjef de Graauw of the Oeteldonksche Club, the carnival association in Den Bosch. Mark van den Heuvel of the Sfeerbeheer Groep agrees, which oversees safety during the Elfde van de Elfde in Breda and <entity id="org:gemeente-eindhoven">Eindhoven</entity>. "If you drink from a can on a square with a thousand people, it doesn't get noticed easily." A bottle of drink on the way Moreover, the risk of incidents is greater because of the way teenagers drink today, says Boonmann. "They drink at home as if their last hour has come, because they know they won't get alcohol in a professional setting. Once they are on our site, the alcohol hits." Van den Heuvel of the Sfeerbeheer Groep sees it the same way. "They drink at home, on the way another bottle of lukewarm drink, and when they've been in town for a quarter of an hour, the lights go out." Regularly he and his colleagues have to call parents to come and pick up their children. "Then I say: 'I'm standing here with your daughter and she mistakes the earth for a currant bun. Maybe it's a good idea for you to come.'" Alcohol use among 12 to 16-year-olds has fallen over the past twenty years. But in recent years they have increasingly 'binge drunk', the Trimbos Institute observes. That means they drink a lot of alcohol in a short time. Drunk teenagers put great pressure on the first aid posts during the Elfde van de Elfde and carnival. "They keep us very busy," says hospitality operator Boonmann about the situation in Tilburg. In Breda too, the pressure on the first aid post was very high last year during carnival, the organization said earlier to BN De Stem. At the post, 88 people were treated at that time for heavy alcohol use, including minors. The youngest was 14 years old. At the Bossche first aid post they mainly see that alcohol poisonings among teenagers are more severe than before. "Earlier they came to us after too much beer, now it is often strong liquor," says Peter Aarsel. "The injuries are therefore greater." 'Preventing things from going wrong' In Tilburg the hospitality sector and municipality hope that the Elfde van Elfde will still go ahead. "We also very much want to organize festivals for minors," says Boonmann. "But I want to prevent things from going wrong." He hopes that the talks with the municipality tomorrow will offer a solution.

title: A-brands more expensive in supermarkets again, budget brands cheaper instead
lead: The price gap between A-brands and budget brands in supermarkets has grown again over the past year. The prices of A-brands rose by an average of 2 percent in one year, while store brands became on average 6 percent cheaper. That is the conclusion of the Consumentenbond after a survey of ten supermarket chains. The association compared the prices of over 900 A-brand products and over 400 budget brand products. According to the market researchers, the biggest riser is the Chinese tomato soup from Unox, which became 37 percent more expensive. In second place on the list of biggest risers is the huzarensalade from Johma, for which consumers now have to pay 32 percent more. A half-liter bottle of Sparkling Lemon from Crystal Clear takes third place with 31 percent. The gap keeps growing. These price increases do not stand alone: A-brands have become on average 16 percent more expensive since September 2023. The prices of budget brands rose by 2 percent compared with three years ago. The Consumentenbond concludes that the price difference between A-brands and budget brands is becoming ever larger. Still, there were also A-brand products that became cheaper. A pack of unsalted grass butter from Campina fell 28 percent in price, as did a half-liter of Fanta Orange Regular. For a 400-gram pack of Lassie wild rice, consumers have to pay 27 percent less. These budget products became more expensive. That budget brands fell 6 percent in price on average does not mean that all products in this category became cheaper. The Consumentenbond sees that many budget varieties of coffee and chocolate became more expensive over the past year. Rice, pasta and canned vegetables, on the other hand, often became tens of percent cheaper again. Whoever prefers to buy A-brands finds that prices differ between supermarkets. At Nettorama these are 7 percent cheaper than average. The supermarket chain with eighty stores in the Netherlands focuses on A-brands at low prices. At Spar you pay 13 percent more than average for them. At the large chains Albert Heijn, Jumbo and Plus, prices are on average 1 to 2 percent above the average. Shrinkflation Aldi and Lidl were not included in the study. According to the Consumentenbond, they sell too few A-brands for a good comparison. The Consumentenbond stresses that only regular prices were examined; promotional prices were left out of consideration. However, account was taken of 'shrinkflation': the phenomenon in which manufacturers reduce the contents of a package without the price falling by an equal amount.

title: Mecca Pact countries join forces for the first time at talks in Tehran
lead: Representatives of Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey are today together in Tehran, for talks with Iranian leaders. It is the first time the three countries act together since they signed a military cooperation treaty: the Mecca Pact. It is their first joint action, but the first test of the pact is already underway. Under the treaty the countries must come to each other's aid if one of the members is attacked. That has been happening for more than three weeks already: Houthis in Yemen, backed by Iran, are shelling Saudi airports and energy infrastructure. Yet Turkey and Pakistan have so far been reluctant about military support for Saudi Arabia. What is the Mecca Pact? On 7 August Pakistan, Turkey and Saudi Arabia signed the Joint Defence Agreement of Mecca, in short referred to as the Mecca Pact . The aim is to "strengthen the collective deterrence against any form of aggression". The pact promises mutual military support. The pact is named after the holy city for Sunnis, the branch of Islam to which the three countries belong. The full text of the pact has not been released. It is known, however, that it contains a clause resembling Article 5 of NATO: according to the official statement "an attack against one of the three states is seen as an attack on all three". What this concretely means is not made clear. On 5 October, after the Riyadh airport had been attacked with missiles by the Houthis, the pact was already officially 'activated'. The Mecca Pact is seen as a geopolitical shift: now that the role of the US in the Middle East has become less predictable, Gulf states such as Saudi Arabia are looking for new partnerships. "Those countries counted for decades on protection under the so-called 'security umbrella' of the US," says Paul Salem of the Center for Strategic and International Studies. "That umbrella now turns out to be full of holes." Since the outbreak of the war with Iran, several Gulf states have been hit by Iranian missiles. The US could not stop those missiles. "For the Saudis the relationship with the US is necessary, but not sufficient. So they are looking at multiple options to strengthen their security." One of those options was therefore the Mecca Pact: Turkey has a large army and a strongly growing arms industry, Pakistan is one of the few countries in the region with nuclear weapons. Saudi Arabia, as a rich oil country, is in turn an attractive partner, and market, for the other two. Saudi Arabia already had a longer military alliance with Pakistan, but Turkey is a competitor on the world stage: the countries have been competing for years for a leading role in the Sunni Muslim world and the region. "That they have set aside their differences and have essentially become allies is a huge step," said Salem. Response to the Houthis Still, Saudi Arabia cannot count on direct support for counterattacks on the Houthis in Yemen. "This is not an attack pact," said Turkish foreign minister Fidan earlier this month. "Turkey will not send troops to another country to attack from there." A day later his Pakistani colleague joined this. Military support is being provided, though the three countries are not transparent about it. This month ministers met for emergency talks. There it was agreed that Pakistan and Turkey will prepare troops for 'rapid deployment' in Saudi Arabia, but it did not become more concrete than that. Turkey has already supplied air defence systems and technical personnel, which may only be deployed for defensive operations. Thin line Under an earlier cooperation pact Pakistan already sent a substantial military package to Saudi Arabia: in the country there are, among others, Pakistani military personnel, combat aircraft and air defence systems. According to sources of The New York Times, Pakistani combat aircraft were also reportedly used last week in attacks on Houthis. Pakistan has to walk a thin line in this conflict: in the war between the US and Iran the country is positioning itself as mediator. If Pakistan directly attacks the Houthis, which are affiliated with Iran, it runs the risk of Iran turning against it. Pakistan therefore firmly denies that it helped with airstrikes on Houthi targets. With contributions from correspondents Devi Boerema (South Asia), Gulsah Ercetin (Turkey) and Daisy Mohr (Middle East)

title: Railway worker dies in train accident in Essen, colleague seriously injured
lead: In Germany last evening a railway worker died after a collision with a high-speed train in Essen. Another employee was seriously injured and taken to hospital. The accident happened when six people were working on the track, German emergency services report. The railway workers were possibly pruning trees and shrubs along the track, according to regional broadcaster WDR. Just after 23:00 the emergency services received the first report of the train accident yesterday. Upon arrival they found the deceased railway worker; a fire brigade cherry picker was needed to transfer his seriously injured colleague to a hospital. Investigation ongoing. The German victim support service came to the scene and offered help to the colleagues of the railway workers and to the driver of the ICE train. It is not clear how a train could be running during the work. The authorities are investigating, including by using a helicopter to survey the area from the air. The track where the accident happened remained closed this morning. Meanwhile trains are running again on one of the three tracks on the route. Passengers should expect delays, writes broadcaster WDR. Earlier accident: in 2023 two railway workers also died in a train accident in the state of North Rhine-Westphalia. They were working on the track in Cologne at the time. Five other railway workers witnessed that accident.

title: Storm Boelo causes flooded quays from Texel to Breskens
lead: Storm Boelo caused flooded quays in several places across the country yesterday. The harbour of Oudeschild on Texel was badly flooded in particular. The water rose as high as the facades of restaurants, shops and hotels. To keep water out of the doors, wooden boards and sandbags have been put in place. "We fasten those boards and then we fill the cracks with sawdust," says the owner of a restaurant in the harbour to regional broadcaster NH. "That swells in water." The owner also has water pumps ready. "In case water comes into the conservatory and the outbuilding. We keep an eye on that the whole time." Ferry operator TESO, responsible for the crossings between Den Helder and Texel, took into account that sailings might be cancelled this morning due to the high water level, but that turned out not to be the case. Storm surge barrier The Hollandsche IJssel barrier near Krimpen aan den IJssel closed yesterday evening for the first time this storm season. It is one of the thirteen Delta Works that are meant to protect the Netherlands from high water from the sea. The storm surge barrier closes on average about three times a year, according to <entity id="org:rijkswaterstaat">Rijkswaterstaat</entity>. Because the Hollandsche IJssel barrier closed, the water rose in Vlaardingen instead. At Koningin Wilhelminahaven the water stood about 40 centimetres high in some places, regional broadcaster Rijnmond reports. The quay was closed to traffic until 07.00. Car under water Harlingen also felt the effects of the high water levels. There too, several quays were flooded yesterday evening and almost 3 metres above NAP was measured. One quay had to be closed off, Omrop Fryslân reports. The harbour of Breskens in Zeeland also flooded overnight. Several cars were partly under water, Omroep Zeeland reports.

title: 'Former Hungarian prime minister Orbán on Trump's list for new UN chief'
lead: The Trump administration is considering nominating Viktor Orbán, the former prime minister of Hungary, as the new Secretary-General of the United Nations. The Wall Street Journal reports this, based on sources from three different countries. The plan would reportedly be supported by both Russia and China. Behind closed doors in New York, a successor is being sought for UN chief António Guterres, who leaves on 1 January. So far that selection process is proceeding haltingly. The process has been underway for a few months. Trump and his administration are reportedly therefore putting Orbán forward. The Hungarian is "the perfect MAGA conservative candidate", an American official tells the newspaper. This is due in part to his views on migration and NGOs (non-governmental organisations) that receive funding from abroad. Wednesday, new poll This coming Wednesday there will be a new, informal poll in the UN Security Council. Other candidates may still come forward. A candidate needs at least nine of the fifteen votes in the UN Security Council. The General Assembly, which includes all 193 UN member states, must then still approve the nomination. The question is whether Orbán can count on enough support in those votes. Call for a woman Last week another new candidate entered the race, The Wall Street Journal writes. It is Lana Nusseibeh, a diplomat from the United Arab Emirates. She was the first Arab president of the UN women's organisation. At the end of last month it emerged that the two frontrunners so far are women from Latin America. There are also African candidates in the race. The call for a woman as Secretary-General is growing louder. In the more than 80 years that the UN has existed, this has never happened. Lost elections Orbán has a free hand after his defeat earlier this year in the parliamentary elections in Hungary. The victory went decisively to Péter Magyar. He promised, among other things, to tackle the corruption from the Orbán era. With Magyar's victory, Orbán's 16 years as prime minister came to an end. In this Q&A our correspondents answered questions about those elections:

title: Eric Bauza, voice of Bugs Bunny, dies at age 46
lead: What's up, Doc? The best-known line of cartoon character Bugs Bunny will never again be voiced by Eric Bauza. The award-winning voice actor and cartoon fan died suddenly yesterday at the age of 46, his family announced on social media. The Canadian-born voice actor of Filipino descent died of cardiovascular disease, caused by high blood pressure, according to the American magazine Variety. During his career as a voice actor, Bauza won three Emmys, the most important American television award. Besides the voice of Bugs Bunny, Bauza was the voice of several other Looney Tunes characters: Tweety, Daffy Duck, Porky Pig and Marvin the Martian. The Looney Tunes characters are owned by the American media company Warner Bros. Eric Bauza as the voice of Bugs Bunny and other cartoon characters: Bauza, born in a suburb of Toronto in 1979, began his career as an animator, but ultimately decided to pursue voice acting. He had discovered at school that he had talent for it. "Kids like me who were the class clown at school found it hard to concentrate, but easy to make classmates laugh," he said in an interview. At secondary school, the arrangement was that he could make the morning announcements over the intercom if he had finished his homework on time. Behind that microphone, Bauza was already imitating Bugs Bunny and, for example, Marge Simpson from The Simpons. His schoolmates sometimes could not believe that he did all those voices. But Bauza knew exactly how they should sound. As a child he was obsessed with Warner Bros cartoons. He never missed anything with Bugs Bunny, he said in an interview from 2023. "I've practised that voice my whole life." 'Unique voice talent' The media world has responded with sadness to Bauza's death. The voice actor worked for the American media company Warner Bros for fifteen years. "Eric Bauza was a unique voice talent who brought joy and pleasure to millions of people around the world," says Channing Dungey, president of Warner Bros Television, in a statement reported by The Hollywood Reporter. "Bauza followed in the footsteps of greats like Mel Blanc," Dungey further says. Blanc was the first voice actor to voice Bugs Bunny's lines. Blanc was the voice for more than fifty years. Dungey also says Bauza was a "beloved member of our animation family". "Our thoughts go out to his loved ones," she concludes the statement.

title: Suspended prison sentence for Chris Brown over assault in British nightclub
lead: The American artist Chris Brown has been sentenced to a suspended prison sentence of eight months for a grievous assault in a London nightclub in 2023. A court in the British capital has decided this. Brown was present in court. He was met by fans at the entrance. He had covered his face with a face mask and wore a cap and sunglasses. The 37-year-old singer had pleaded guilty in July to affray in the nightclub. The artist and his vocal coach attacked a music producer with a tequila bottle. The victim, a former friend, was hit twice on the head with the bottle. The British prosecutors had agreed to drop more serious charges, such as causing bodily harm, if Brown and his vocal coach pleaded guilty to affray. Cameras Many people in the club saw the attack happen. It was also recorded on cameras. The footage was shown during the hearing. It shows that Brown had to be pulled away from the victim after he had hit him twice on the head with the bottle. According to the prosecutor, the music producer had to go to hospital for head and knee injuries. The court said that repeatedly striking with the glass bottle could have caused more serious injury to the victim. Despite the seriousness of the case, Brown is not getting an unconditional prison sentence because, among other things, he had pleaded guilty. During today's hearing the singer offered his apologies for the attack. "This is an unpleasant and disagreeable event," said Brown's lawyer in court. "It is something that undoubtedly caused suffering to those present, and for which Mr Brown offers his sincere apologies." Hotel Brown was arrested last year at his hotel in Manchester for the fight from February 2023. This happened after the British tabloid The Sun contacted the police with questions about his possible arrest. After paying the bail of 5 million pounds he was released and could begin his world tour.

title: Rare poisonous mushroom 'Angel of Death' found in Soest
lead: It looks like a harmless mushroom: 9 to 12 centimetres tall, with a cone-shaped cap and snow white. But appearances deceive with this sticky death cap: it is one of the most notorious mushrooms in Europe, nicknamed 'the Angel of Death'. Besides being notorious, the species is also endangered, and on the Utrecht Heuvelrug it was even considered extinct, yet it has now nevertheless been found there. "I jumped in the air", says mycologist (mushroom expert) Rob Chrispijn. He found the sticky death cap on the De Paltz estate in Soest, while he was leading an excursion there. Chrispijn found the species in two different places. Remarkable, because this mushroom is rare. The sticky death cap is listed as endangered on the Dutch Red List. The species has been declining sharply for years and is vulnerable to eutrophication and acidification of the soil. "Nitrogen plays a role in that", says Chrispijn. The mushroom looks a bit like a champignon, and that is exactly why things can go badly wrong. Eating the sticky death cap can be life-threatening without medical treatment. At first you won't notice anything after eating it, says Chrispijn. But later you may become nauseous and develop severe gastrointestinal complaints. "After two days the liver and kidneys are affected, and the consequences can be permanent." The Angel of Death is not easy to find, because the mushroom only stands above ground for a few days. Of the two specimens found, one is being investigated further. The other is still on the estate. Chrispijn does not expect anyone to take it. "The Dutch are a bit scared of mushrooms."

title: Bus with churchgoers collides head-on with truck in Kenya, 24 dead
lead: In a head-on collision between a bus and a truck, at least 24 people died yesterday in the south of Kenya. This happened on the motorway connecting the coastal town Mombasa with the capital Nairobi. Local media write that the bus driver had 45 churchgoers on board. The bus was on the return trip to Mombasa after attending the funeral of a pastor. Near the village of Mtito Andei, the driver tried to pass several vehicles during a long overtaking manoeuvre. That went wrong when a truck appeared. The bus driver still swerved to the right, but could no longer prevent a collision. 24 people were injured, most of whom were taken to the hospital in Mtito Andei. It is not the first accident on this road. Three weeks ago seventeen people died in an accident on the Nairobi-Mombasa Highway. The route between Nairobi and Mombasa is considered one of the most dangerous in the country. President Ruto now wants all vehicles in the country to be checked for road safety. A national day of mourning must also be held for all road traffic victims.

title: Podcast De Dag: the many questions surrounding the murder of Hajar
lead: On 16 October the body of 29-year-old Hajar was found in the water of the Amstel in Amsterdam. She had been stuffed into a suitcase. The case stirs up a lot and there are many questions, some of which cannot yet be answered, to the frustration of the public and journalists. What do we now know and what don't we know about the murder of Hajar? Listen: You can listen to this episode of De Dag via NPO Luister and all other podcast apps. Like it? Then don't forget to subscribe. In the podcast, crime reporter of AT5 Niels van Steijn tells how the news came in at the local broadcaster and how the editorial team went to work on it. Which questions remain and what is the current state of the investigation? Respond? Email dedag@nos.nl Presentation and editing: Elisabeth Steinz. Editorial team: Judith Kutschenreuter. Final editing: Judith van de Hulsbeek

lead: The measure meant to help petty thieves improve their lives is working less and less well. Addicted repeat offenders who are held against their will get less often the care they need. title: 'Organised chaos is what makes it so Amsterdam': for thirty years, partying and networking have gone hand in hand at Amsterdam Dance Event
lead: Thirty years after the first edition, Amsterdam Dance Event is bigger than ever. At the same time, the music industry is worldwide and permanently connected, and important deals are already being closed earlier. Why does that one Amsterdam week in October remain so important?

title: Daughter suspected of abuse, father in the pulpit: how a sexual abuse case divides this church in Elspeet
lead: The atmosphere is tense as members of the Gereformeerde Gemeente in Elspeet gather for a closed congregation evening. Holy Communion has already been cancelled several times. Families have left. It all began with a report of sexual abuse.

title: Renovation of the Binnenhof more expensive again, now due to higher interest costs: 'This is how we will really rack up the 3 billion euros'
Not only in cars, but also in boardrooms there may be spies
lead: Discussing sensitive matters in the car is advised against by the <entity id="org:directoraat-generaal-algemene-inlichtingen-en-veiligheidsdienst">AIVD</entity> due to the risk of espionage. But the meeting room may pose an even greater risk.

title: Live Champions League | Van Bronckhorst after defeat: 'We deserved a draw'
lead: Good evening and welcome to this live blog! Here we, Teun Heijmans and Lieve Wils, will keep you informed about the Champions League evening, with the highlight Real Betis-Feyenoord. Enjoy!

title: Karin (59) once wanted to become mayor, but long covid makes working impossible: 'That is what I miss most'
lead: Karin Lambrechts (59) used to work from early in the morning until late at night. Now her life runs on a battery of at most three hours because of long covid. The upcoming cuts from <entity id="org:gemeente-s-gravenhage">Den Haag</entity> frustrate her, especially when she thinks of her younger fellow sufferers. "How are they supposed to go on now?"

title: 'Certainty has been lacking for a very long time' for holiday park residents: 'Municipalities no longer know either'
lead: Living permanently in holiday parks is a subject that has been causing debate for decades. The national government and the municipalities often do not see eye to eye on this. Elanor Boekholt-O'Sullivan, the current minister of Volkshuisvesting, calls on municipalities to be restrained in enforcing the rules, but the vast majority of municipalities are not listening, research by NOS shows. "As a municipality, at some point you no longer know what to do," says Albertjan Tollenaar, professor of Administrative Law at the Rijksuniversiteit <entity id="org:gemeente-groningen">Groningen</entity>, on Spraakmakers.

title: Coalition conflict over scaling back paper gift donations: VVD does not want it
Trump lashes out again at Zelensky: 'Ukraine must want to stop the war'
lead: US President Donald Trump once again places the responsibility for ending the war in Ukraine on Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky. According to Trump, Russia is eager to end the war.

title: Nederlandse regering blokkeert opnieuw verkoop van DigiD-aanbieder Solvinity aan Amerikaans bedrijf
lead: Staatssecretaris voor Digitale Economie <entity id="person:willemijn-aerdts">Willemijn Aerdts</entity> handhaaft haar besluit om de verkoop van Solvinity aan het Amerikaanse bedrijf Kyndryl te blokkeren, ook nadat er bezwaar is gemaakt.

title: Pieterburen Seal Centre Postpones Bankruptcy Filing by One Week After Major Support From Donors
lead: World Heritage Wadden Sea Centre (WEC), under which the Stichting Zeehondencentrum Pieterburen falls, announced almost two weeks ago that it would have to file for bankruptcy at short notice. Now that the deadline is approaching, the organisation reports 'cautiously positive news': the planned bankruptcy filing will be postponed by one week.

title: Housing budget is hard to spend
lead: That housing construction in the Netherlands does not happen by itself is shown, among other things, by the underspending of the budgets of the ministry of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-vro">Volkshuisvesting en Ruimtelijke Ordening</entity> (VRO). That was emphasised by the <entity id="org:algemene-rekenkamer">Algemene Rekenkamer</entity> again after Prinsjesdag, in a document with points of attention on the then newly submitted draft budget of the ministry.

title: How astronomers investigated the exact night Van Gogh painted his starry sky
Richard Thompson sings and plays with his whole soul: 'Hippies, Thugs and Heroes' ranks among his best work
Traveller without visa held for four days after refusal at Eindhoven Airport: judge rules in his favour
lead: Arriving passengers who are not let through passport control at Eindhoven Airport risk being detained for days in a detention centre. Because the airport closes at night, a lighter measure is often impossible.

title: Vulnerabilities in PHP seem to have been resolved with an update, but tech experts think they see new risks
Festival Into the Woods stopped earlier on Saturday evening because of a storm
VVD bill for ban on religious clothing for boa's 'lacks foundation', Council of State finds
Laura (28) and Jim (33) got to know each other during their studies: 'The next morning, everyone knew what had happened on that sofa'
Industry wants temporary gas turbines to speed up sustainability
lead: Factories are suffering from the overly tight power grid. Gas turbines are already being deployed in the <entity id="org:provincie-utrecht">provincie Utrecht</entity> to be able to supply extra electricity.

title: Tielen: don't let yourself be distracted by politicizing the rainbow flag
lead: "We must not let ourselves be distracted by people who want to make the rainbow flag political", said State Secretary <entity id="person:judith-tielen">Judith Tielen</entity> for Emancipation today. "It is not about politics, it is about everyone being able to be free and equal."

title: Local administrators hopeful after speech by Jetten
lead: Local administrators respond positively to the words that Prime Minister <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Rob Jetten</entity> spoke on Tuesday about cooperation and covering the costs of youth care by the national government.

title: Fierce criticism of Audi CEO after Trump rally: 'Puppets in propaganda'
lead: The chairman of the works council of Volkswagen Group has voiced sharp criticism of the Audi CEO's performance on Saturday. He was at an election rally of Donald Trump, where the American president announced the first Audi factory in the United States.

title: Young Israelis are moving further to the right: 'They hardly ever mention the word peace anymore'
lead: Since the Hamas attacks of 7 October, young Israelis appear to have shifted even further to the right. They grew up during wars led by prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu, then served in the army, and have no memories of genuine peace efforts.

title: Rembrandt House also sounds the alarm over cultural visitors staying away: 'The unworkable maximum of 20 million overnight stays per year is strangling us'
How does an Israeli generation that grew up with war vote?
Former student Cornell gets police at her door after false tip about murders
lead: The woman who accuses students of Cornell University of gang rape received police at her door on Tuesday. Officers had been sent to her home after a false report of multiple murders at the address.

title: Cynthia Liem: 'AI is a vague umbrella term'
lead: The discussion about digitalisation focuses too much on technology alone. That scares off people you actually want to involve in the discussion, warns Cynthia Liem, lector Responsible Digital Society at Inholland University of Applied Sciences. For example, the people who will ultimately have to use the systems.

title: Call | Would you open your home to an asylum seeker? We are looking for you
lead: Last week twenty asylum seekers in Ter Apel had to sleep on the grass because the day shelter was full. Would you like to help solve the reception problems by taking in an asylum seeker at your home? Then we are looking for you.

title: Steven (39) was a safecracker: 'I felt like the director of the bank'
lead: For years Steven Kilian (39) put his own life and those of others at risk with safecracking. After he was arrested he fled, and he nonetheless spent years behind bars. Now that he is free again, and battered after an attack in prison, he wants to warn others: don't start. "How many innocent people I endangered. All for a few lousy cents."

title: Moeder alleen verantwoordelijk voor doden van 14-jarige dochter in Venlo, aldus het OM
lead: Het Openbaar Ministerie (OM) beschouwt de 59-jarige Fouzia R. als enige verantwoordelijke voor het doden van haar 14-jarige dochter Nour.

title: Municipalities reach energy-poor households mainly through personal contact
lead: Municipalities can help households struggling with energy poverty better by reaching out to them themselves. But the capacity for calls, home visits and building trust is often lacking. This is shown by an evaluation of the municipal pilot around the Tijdelijk Noodfonds Energie by RadarAdvies, commissioned by the <entity id="org:vereniging-van-nederlandse-gemeenten">Vereniging van Nederlandse Gemeenten</entity> (VNG).

title: Israel elections: more or less Netanyahu?
New research: millions of Ukrainians struggle with war trauma
lead: About 1 in 3 Ukrainians has symptoms of PTSD. That is reported by a group of researchers from Ukrainian, British and American universities. The Ukrainian healthcare system is incapable of treating millions of patients, and therefore the entire society will have to take action, the experts say.

title: Unrest in Pakistan after dissolution of the only provincial government with Imran Khan's party
lead: The Pakistani government has dissolved the administration of the northwestern province of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa. According to the government, the provincial administration is colluding with the Pakistani Taliban. Critics call the decision a power grab to sideline the party of former prime minister Imran Khan.

title: Video | Helmet camera films Israeli soldiers at fatal shooting on the West Bank
Five DJs, including Amsterdammer Job Jobse (36), cancel their performance at No Art Festival due to 'personal circumstances'
Municipalities and provinces can do more to protect migratory birds
lead: Municipalities and provinces can do more to prevent the extinction of vulnerable migratory birds. That is what Karsten Schipperheijn, managing director of Vogelbescherming Nederland, says.

title: Indonesians demonstrate against forest fires and poor air quality
lead: Demonstrators took to the streets in Jakarta and other Indonesian cities in anger over the forest fires and the poor air quality that resulted from them. In recent months, hundreds of thousands of people have developed breathing problems.

title: Mathematics played an important role in my life, until AI got involved
lead: Almost all the mathematical projects Piet Lammers worked on as a researcher were suddenly solved by AI in one fell swoop. A development of importance to all of society: how do we stay 'smart' ourselves when we no longer actually need that intelligence?

title: NS raises train ticket prices: 'Outrageous, life is expensive enough already'
lead: Prices of train tickets and most NS subscriptions will rise by an average of 4.7 percent early next year. As a result, the price of travelling by train is rising faster than inflation. Travellers are not happy about it: 'Life is expensive enough already.'

title: Major fire at Olympic Stadium under control, fire brigade trying to preserve national monument 'as well as possible'
Musk gives Republicans over 445 million dollars for midterms
Limburg has been named the 'smartest region' in the world, what is the value of such an award?
lead: The <entity id="org:provincie-limburg">provincie Limburg</entity> last week received the title 'smartest region in the world' from the Intelligent Community Forum (ICF). The jury praises the establishment of four Brightlands campuses that ensure more knowledge exchange. What does the award mean for the region?

title: Opinion: UN member states should protect Ukraine, where are they?
Anger among Volkswagen staff over wage freeze
lead: The works council is sounding the alarm because, in wage negotiations, the Volkswagen management wants to focus on a zero wage increase in the coming years. As a result, staff would certainly fall 10% behind by 2030.

title: Call for questions | What do you want to know from our political reporters?
lead: Now that the autumn recess has begun and there are no debates scheduled this week, our political reporters have time to answer questions. What do you want to know about politics in The Hague?

title: Good colours and good sound, this 65-inch television comes out best in the test
lead: You don't buy a new TV on size alone. For 65 inches, how black black is, how well the picture stays bright and how easy the controls are also matter. The Consumentenbond tested more than 115 televisions. These came out best in the test.

title: Overijssel: a deal is a deal regarding the Nedersaksenlijn
lead: The province of Overijssel has called on minister <entity id="person:vincent-karremans">Vincent Karremans</entity> to abide by the agreements made about the Nedersaksenlijn. 'A deal is a deal,' says deputy Martijn Dadema. 'We have raised all kinds of expectations among residents. It does something to the relationship between citizens and government when you don't keep such important agreements.'

title: In today's China, one's own history may only be glorious: 'There is no longer room for discussion'
Return hubs for rejected refugees: 'A total black box'
lead: Five European countries, including the Netherlands, are working on an initiative to send rejected asylum seekers to a country outside the European Union. Those reception locations are also called return hubs. The Greek asylum minister announced this week that the project will start in early 2027. The first refugees may go to Rwanda. But we then distance ourselves from all human rights. "As soon as you outsource that responsibility, it is completely, completely out of our hands", says Member of the European Parliament for Volt Anna Strolenberg in De Rode Draad. She has just returned from the area and tells what she saw there.

title: NEC cannot follow up historic European win in the Eredivisie: team draws with FC Groningen
lead: NEC failed to win in the Eredivisie after its victory over Dinamo Zagreb in the Europa League. At the Goffert, the team coached by Dick Schreuder drew 2-2 with FC Groningen, although for a long time it did not look that way.

title: A new twist on fraud
lead: The criminals are among us and will not rest until they have squeezed the last cent out of our pockets. In the past they were rogues who came to tidy up your garden for a moment and then demanded a few thousand guilders, now they link your WhatsApp account to their own laptop or phone and plunder your bank account.

title: "Grand, complex and not without danger": Kadir van Lohuizen photographed the energy transition in the North Sea
lead: For his project Nieuwe Energie, photographer and filmmaker Kadir van Lohuizen examined what the energy transition in and around the North Sea looks like. Everything in the photos breathes big, bigger, biggest. "That was quite a challenge: how do I show that scale?"

title: Jumbo recalls pulled chicken because it may contain raw chicken
lead: Supermarket chain Jumbo is recalling the prepared chicken dish pulled chicken because it was not cooked through as stated on the packaging. Customers are asked not to consume the product.

title: Twenty road deaths and 3950 victims: Amsterdam is not yet making traffic safer
A death wish can also be a suicidal thought
UWV must also pay domestic workers sickness benefits
lead: Domestic workers can also claim under the Sickness Benefits Act, the <entity id="org:centrale-raad-van-beroep">Centrale Raad van Beroep</entity> has ruled. For them, this ruling is a major step towards equal treatment with other employees.

title: Tennis player Goffin bids farewell with defeat in Brussels
lead: Belgian tennis player David Goffin has played his last singles match as a professional tennis player. The 35-year-old Goffin lost on Thursday in the ATP tournament in Brussels in the second round, in two sets to American Alex Michelsen: 6-3 6-4.

title: Everything offline: Netherlands learned from Albert Heijn and acted decisively in PHP cyber disaster: 'Very smart'
lead: Dutch websites went dark en masse on Wednesday. That is how we protected ourselves against abuse of vulnerabilities in PHP websites. A right choice, it turns out: worldwide, millions of attacks followed on websites that had stayed online. "Hackers can take over entire sites."

title: Minister of Agriculture: understanding for worried farmer, but 'plans stay in place'
lead: The new nitrogen plans of <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> are causing great gloom among Dutch livestock farmers. As many as 87 percent say that because of the plans they have less confidence in the future of their own farm. Minister of Agriculture Van Essen responds today with understanding for the concerns, but stresses that the plans remain in place.

title: Four years in prison demanded against Doetinchem man for preparing attack on asylum centre
lead: The Public Prosecution Service demanded four years in prison on Tuesday against a 37-year-old man from Doetinchem. He is suspected of preparing an attack on an asylum seekers' centre.

title: Central government has grown the most of all government tiers over the past ten years
Being against abortion belongs in the same list as being against asylum seekers, against climate policy, against LGBTI people and against nice people
AI objections add extra work for municipalities
lead: Municipalities, hospitals and public transport companies are increasingly dealing with objections drafted with the help of artificial intelligence (AI). The texts are generally longer, more legalistic and regularly contain incorrect references to legislation. This causes extra work and delays in handling objections.

title: 'I pick up my spirituality from everywhere, but shouldn't I have to choose?'
Former Groningen mayor Koen Schuiling challenges conviction at Supreme Court
lead: Former Groningen mayor Koen Schuiling is appealing to the Supreme Court. In March 2024 he was fined for masturbating in his car based on the testimony of a single witness. Earlier NRC reporting showed that the criminal file was incomplete and influenced by assumptions about Schuiling's homosexuality.

title: Whatever the rich lobby comes up with: a millionaires' tax works
Rob Jetten and his partner are expecting a baby: the rules on surrogacy in the Netherlands
lead: The Netherlands is getting a 'first baby': Prime Minister Rob Jetten and his fiancé Nicolás Keenan are expecting a child next year. The couple had already expressed their wish to have children, but finding a surrogate is complicated because of the rules in our country.

title: Choice for maintenance is right, but not at the expense of our water plan
lead: The state of many Dutch waterways and bridges is nothing to be proud of. It is right that <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> is freeing up money for the large backlog of maintenance. But that this comes at the expense of plans to protect us against drought is asking for new problems, writes political reporter Hans van Soest in this commentary.

title: Another person dies after infection with West Nile virus in the Netherlands
lead: In the Netherlands, another person has died after being infected with the West Nile virus. This is the tenth person this year to die after infection with the virus, the <entity id="org:rijksinstituut-voor-volksgezondheid-en-milieu">Rijksinstituut voor Volksgezondheid en Milieu</entity> reported on Thursday.

title: It is time for a diplomatic post at the Court of Elon
lead: The power of tech billionaires now extends well beyond their companies. It is time for the Netherlands and Europe to adapt their diplomacy accordingly.

title: 'I think it's really cozy that you hear 'tok tok tok' when you come home'
lead: Rein Hazelzet (37) and Sanne Brouwer (39) moved from the Randstad to a village in Gelderland, where they renovated an old parsonage into their dream home. "Everything had to be renovated, only the outer walls and the roof were left standing."

title: All those different bedrooms, and yet the same nest
lead: For years, photographer Bieke Depoorter travelled around Egypt, Russia and the United States and slept at people's homes. What stands out in particular is the resemblance between the bedrooms; the more or less universal nature of the human sleeping place.

title: Medewerkers van asielinstantie zeggen dat klachten over onveilige situaties onbeantwoord blijven; eisen verandering
lead: Medewerkers van Nederlandse asielcentra die onveilige situaties melden, krijgen binnen het Centraal Orgaan opvang asielzoekers (<entity id="org:zbo-centraal-orgaan-opvang-asielzoekers">COA</entity>) geen reactie en hebben hun klachten voorgelegd aan de Arbeidsinspectie

title: Vidi-beurs toegekend aan meer dan 100 onderzoekers en wetenschappers
lead: In totaal krijgen 109 Nederlandse onderzoekers een financiële subsidie van de overheid, ook wel de Vidi-beurs genoemd.

title: Van Roosmalen & Groenteman still not saved, PowNed has to back out: 'It is a crying shame'
lead: The BNNVara programme Van Roosmalen & Groenteman will definitely not move to broadcaster PowNed. "We really wanted to take it over, but we cannot get the financing sorted. It is a crying shame", says Dominique Weesie, director of PowNed.

title: Zeeland looks to English coastal town: learning from Folkestone
lead: 'From Zeeland it is actually only a short drive: two and a half hours to the Channel Tunnel, at the end of the tunnel turn left, and you are there.' Last September, Zeeland deputy Johan Aalberts took a seat on a bus heading for the English coastal town of Folkestone, not far from the famous White Cliffs of Dover. Besides the King's Commissioner <entity id="person:hugo-de-jonge">Hugo de Jonge</entity>, a group from Zeeland's education and business sectors was also on the bus with him.

title: "The courage shown by the women who report boundary-crossing behaviour is much stronger than what we men have shown"
Tiny Forest: a small jungle next to the school
lead: In 2015 the Netherlands had a genuine European first: IVN Natuureducatie introduced the first Tiny Forest in our country. A small forest of two hundred square metres, with 600 trees planted very close together and close to a primary school. Because a Tiny Forest is meant to be a place where children can learn more about and with nature. Meanwhile there are already 250 of these small forests in the Netherlands and they are appearing more and more in the rest of Europe.

title: Con artist Elizabeth Holmes draws full cinemas: 'Film of the year'
lead: The biggest con artist of this century is once again the center of attention. Before she went to prison, tech fraudster Elizabeth Holmes let two documentary makers live with her in her home for a month. America can't stop talking about it.

title: Why are protests taking place in so many major European cities this weekend?
US envoy Witkoff meets Putin in Moscow on Wednesday
Environmental organisations go to court over new Schiphol decision
Who will pick up free agent Luuk de Jong (36) after serious knee injury? 'I feel good, I am fit'
lead: Luuk de Jong is open to a new adventure. The striker has recovered from a knee injury he sustained last year. Since last summer the former international has been a free agent.

title: Gert and Viktor Verhulst take on well-known friends and their own family in new programme Missie Verhulst
lead: Gert Verhulst (58) and son Viktor (32) will soon unveil their latest project: Missie Verhulst. In the Videoland programme, the two join forces to prank their friends and family with a hidden camera.

title: Prisoners increasingly use drones to smuggle items inside, also a juicy morsel
Videoland may take over streamer Viaplay, including Formula 1 and darts

title: The fight for LGBTI acceptance is far from over, including in the Tweede Kamer
Can a train ticket to Lourdes reduce healthcare costs?
Jesse Klaver (Pro): 'The VVD calls a deal with us terrible. Then the base will believe it'
Girls with psychological complaints don't need a tissue, but someone who listens
The cork the internet floats on is broken: why the attack on PHP is paralysing half the internet
lead: One website after another is going offline due to vulnerabilities in the programming language PHP. Criminals are said to have already begun their first cyberattacks. It is a disaster, because 70 percent of the internet uses PHP. "This is very big."

title: Nederlandse koningin annuleerde werkbezoek waarbij een Pro-Palestijnse band betrokken was op 7 oktober
lead: Koningin Maxima annuleerde een geplande bezoek aan het Tilburgse muziekpodium Poppodium 013 slechts twee weken voor de datum, een zeldzaam voorval voor de Nederlandse koninklijke familie.

title: Outspoken and concerned: Coos Huijsen, the first openly gay parliamentarian in the world, has died
lead: Fifty years ago Coos Huijsen became the first parliamentarian in the world to publicly come out of the closet. Towards the end of his life he was worried about the waning acceptance of homosexuality.

title: Asylum minister Van den Brink wants to punish asylum seeker who frustrates deportation
Arsenal loses its unbeaten status despite late goal in Munich, Jurriën Timber causes penalty
lead: Bayern Munich handed Arsenal their first points loss in the Champions League. The top match at the Allianz Arena ended in a draw: 2-2.

title: Eredivisie sells itself (finally again) in Europe thanks to an unprecedented performance
lead: The Eredivisie sold itself excellently in Europe this week. Finally again. Five of the six clubs won their match, good for first place in the weekly ranking on the UEFA coefficient ranking. Our football expert Maarten Wijffels sees a common thread in this dream week for the Dutch clubs.

title: Storm Austen: boom valt op auto in Amsterdam en maakt gat in dak van boerderij
lead: Er zijn meldingen binnengekomen van omgevallen bomen en afgebroken takken uit het hele land na de komst van Storm Austen vrijdagnacht.

title: An absurdist who always colours neatly within the lines
Dozens of civil servants still hired after Amsterdam municipality's vacancy freeze was supposed to be tightened 'with immediate effect'
MolTalk returns to the old time slot after one season following Wie is de Mol?
lead: Discussing Wie is de Mol? will again take place straight after the broadcast of the programme from the coming season onward. After one season of broadcasting MolTalk in advance, AVROTROS again gets the room to return to the old time slot.

title: No one has to cycle alone to the ferry after dance festival: 'This is specifically meant for the lone cyclist'
lead: Your friends want to keep partying, but you long for your bed. Especially for many women, cycling alone in the dark feels even more unsafe than before, certainly after the murder of 17-year-old Lisa. To address that, cycling buddies are on hand at the DGTL festival during Amsterdam Dance Event.

title: Four dead in storms in France
lead: The severe weather in southern France and on the island of Corsica has already cost four people their lives, authorities in Bouches-du-Rhône say. Earlier, two fatalities had been reported. One person is also missing.

title: Joris Bijdendijk got a jaw injury from cooking: 'Needed painful therapy'
lead: The head chef can take a nap against the wall, serves his children goose, and always needs that dessert, he tells in this column from our weekend magazine Mezza .

title: Bertram wants to combine public transport and other types of transport in the region
lead: Public transport and, among other things, pupil transport must be combined in regions where accessibility is declining. State Secretary <entity id="person:annet-bertram">Annet Bertram</entity> (Infrastructure, CDA) wants in this way to move from public transport to 'public mobility' that can be booked by everyone all day, she writes in a letter to the House of Representatives.

title: At this primary school, the children receive bilingual education. 'Handy if I become a professional footballer later'
Woman gives birth on train while on her way to a check-up at a Groningen hospital
lead: A woman gave birth on a train on Monday morning. She was on her way to a hospital in Groningen for a check-up when her waters suddenly broke, De Telegraaf reports.

title: Queen Máxima was set to listen to a pro-Palestinian band on 7 October, and then the visit was called off
lead: A working visit by <entity id="person:willem-alexander">koning Willem-Alexander</entity> and Queen Máxima is rarely cancelled at the last minute. Yet it happened earlier this month: Máxima was due to visit Poppodium 013 on, of all days, 7 October, with the pro-Palestinian band Droom Dit on the programme. Behind the scenes it is now said that this date was not a good choice for the visit.

title: FC Twente houdt een perfecte Europese start vast met een 4-1 overwinning in Gibraltar
lead: FC Twente versloeg Lincoln Red Imps F.C. donderdag met 4-1 in de groepsfase van de UEFA Conference League.
